item.content:encoded:
On Day 5 of the League Championship Series, one team broke a series tie ... will another advance to the Fall Classic?
After splitting the first two games in Tampa Bay, the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays faced off at Progressive Field in the day's first game. Thanks toPetey Halpin-- and his epic bat flip -- Cleveland prevailed, taking a 2-1 ALCS lead.
Tonight, in what could be the finale of the NLCS, the Milwaukee Brewers will look to continue their dominant championship series run and sweep the reigning champion Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium. Can the Dodgers stave off elimination in Game 4 -- or will the Brewers advance to their first World Series since 1982?
Stay tuned for in-game action and postgame analysis from Los Angeles and Cleveland.
Key links: How final four teams were built | Playoff MVP tracker | Schedule
Cleveland leads series 2-1
It was over when ... Petey Halpin cranked a 96 mph sinker down the middle from Griffin Jax in the fifth inning. The ball landed deep into the right-field seats, 385 feet away, for a go-ahead two-run home run. Halpin flipped his bat nearly that high, too, and Cleveland didn't look back.
Game 3 star: Halpin, who began the season in Triple-A, had four big league home runs -- all during the regular season -- in 213 career plate appearances before Thursday. The center fielder's first postseason homer was the difference Thursday.
The stat that defined the game:The Rays' 13 strikeouts against Guardians pitching. The Rays posted the lowest strikeout rate in the majors this season at 18.8%. They struck out more than 12 times once, when they compiled 14 strikeouts against the Milwaukee Brewers back on March 30 in their fourth game of the season. Rays star Junior Caminero went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts -- matching a career high from 2025. So Thursday was an extreme outlier. Guardians starter Gavin Williams, the American League's strikeout leader this season, had nine strikeouts in five innings before four relievers combined for the remaining four punchouts. Tampa Bay will have to put the ball in play more to come back and win this series.
What it means for the rest of the series: With rain in the forecast Friday, there's a chance this series won't play Game 4 until Saturday. If so, the clubs would play Game 5 on Sunday, which would take away their travel day before a potential Game 6 in Tampa Bay on Monday. For now, Game 4 is scheduled for 6 p.m. ET Friday. -- Jorge Castillo

item.title: [cubbiescrib.com] Jake Bauers' Brewers heroics against Dodgers give Cubs an intriguing offseason target
item.dc:creator: Jordan Campbell
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers, to the chagrin of the Chicago Cubs, are on the verge of a advancing to the World Series, and could complete a four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night. The Dodgers nearly won on Wednesday night but that was before Jake Bauers had the at-bat seen around the world. Bauers worked an 11-pitch at-bat against Blake Snell in the seventh inning of Game 3, and on the final pitched, promptly delivered the ball to the right field stands, giving the Brewers a 3-2 l
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers, to the chagrin of the Chicago Cubs, are on the verge of a advancing to the World Series, and could complete a four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night. The Dodgers nearly won on Wednesday night but that was before Jake Bauers had the at-bat seen around the world.
Bauers worked an 11-pitch at-bat against Blake Snell in the seventh inning of Game 3, and on the final pitched, promptly delivered the ball to the right field stands, giving the Brewers a 3-2 lead and they never looked back.
For all the talk about the Brewers not having slug, and needing to play small ball to win games, it ignores the reality that while their lineup includes an emerging superstar in Jackson Chourio, they also had one of this season's best power hitters in Jake Bauers.
Cubs could find a sneaky offensive upgrade in Brewers' latest postseason hero Jake Bauers
Playing the matchups throughout the season, Bauers has mostly been used against right-handed pitching and he's made the most of his opportunity. The 31-year-old slashed .266/.389/.484 through 578 plate appearances, adding 26 home runs with a wRC+ of 143. In terms of the exact splits, Bauers had 418 plate appearances against right-handed pitchers, and 160 against lefties.
Faced with the potential of losing Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ this offseason, and the reality that neither Matt Shaw or Pedro Ramirez should be handed full-time roles in the outfield, it's possible the Cubs see Bauers as a potential fit this offseason. While he hasn't had the career track record that Suzuki or Happ have had, his success with the Brewers and recency bias of his playoff production is likely going to up his price tag.
For that reason, it's possible the Cubs simply aren't involved in the bidding. But, if there's an exception to be made, and it't not going to the top of the market for Suzuki's return, perhaps the Cubs see if there's common ground to be had with Bauers. He would be an ideal platoon option for either Shaw or Ramirez in the outfield, and would give the Cubs some cover at first base when Michael Busch needs a day off.
If not Bauers specifically, then the Cubs need to find their version of what the Brewers did. They took a flier on Bauers in a buy-low trade with the New York Yankees, and found a way to unlock his power. With an offseason focus on pitching, that level of creativity is what the Cubs will need to improve their offense.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Max Muncy’s no-nonsense response to Dodgers’ performance doesn’t instill confidence for Game 4
item.dc:creator: Colin Keane
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting severely outplayed by the Milwaukee Brewers through the first three games of the National League Championship Series. LA's been outscored 15-7 so far in the series, and they've hit zero home runs to Milwaukee's five. In Game 3, the Dodgers managed just five hits, failing to generate enough offense to compete with the Brewers' aggressive style. Jackson Chourio went yard on the first pitch of the game from Blake Snell. When LA seized the lead back in the sixth o
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting severely outplayed by the Milwaukee Brewers through the first three games of the National League Championship Series. LA's been outscored 15-7 so far in the series, and they've hit zero home runs to Milwaukee's five.
In Game 3, the Dodgers managed just five hits, failing to generate enough offense to compete with the Brewers' aggressive style. Jackson Chourio went yard on the first pitch of the game from Blake Snell. When LA seized the lead back in the sixth on a two-run double from Will Smith, Milwaukee bounced right back: In the next half inning, Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back jacks off of Snell to re-take the lead.
The Brewers added additional runs in the eighth and ninth, whereas the Dodgers' bats didn't capitalize on opportunities to stay in the game (1-for-6 with runners in scoring position). Following the deflating result, Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy didn't exactly wax poetic about LA's struggles.
Max Muncy's blunt analysis of the Dodgers' struggles doesn't inspire faith for Game 4
Muncy's assessment of things is accurate, but it doesn't help Dodgers fans feel any better about Game 4 on Thursday night. It's admirable that Muncy chose to be honest rather than come up with some excuses for the Dodgers, but doing so also reinforced the harsh reality that LA simply might not be good enough right now to overcome what looks like a team of destiny over in the Brewers' dugout.
And there aren't excuses to make -- the Dodgers' stars are present, just not performing. Shohei Ohtani hasn't been himself, and it's not like LA's offense is without proven playoff performers like Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman at the moment. Muncy's not helping matters, either, at least not in this series. After an awesome NLDS, Muncy is 1-for-9 with four strikeouts so far in the NLCS.
To keep their three-peat dream alive, the Dodgers must make history
If Muncy sounds pessimistic, it's probably because he understands the history of baseball. Only one team (the 2004 Boston Red Sox) has ever come back and won a best-of-seven series after trailing 3-0. It's never been done in an NLCS. If there's a group with the talent required to pull off the near-impossible, it's these Dodgers, but talent might not be the issue here.
The problem is momentum. The Brewers have scores of it, whereas the Dodgers look stuck in the mud. The other issue is that LA doesn't have any runway to generate the momentum they need. They are in the middle of a series and must act immediately or watch their season and three-peat hopes end just as swiftly.
Tyler Glasnow will surely put in a good performance in Game 4, but it won't mean anything if the Dodgers' offense is weak yet again. Muncy's simple assessment of things leads to a simple directive for the Dodgers: get on base early and often, and drive guys in when you do.

item.content:encoded:
The Brewers’ stunning 3-0 stranglehold on the Dodgers in the NLCS is the epitome of there being no guarantees in sports.
Milwaukee has several feats in front of them when they take the field for Game 4 on Thursday evening.
Firstly, the Brewers can slay the Los Angeles beast that has won back-to-back titles and outspends them by $193.1 million on their roster. Beyond that, they can end a 44-year World Series drought and become the first club in history to sweep an opponent the following year after getting swept by that same team.
Brewers vs. Dodgers Game 4 prediction, best bet
Narratives aside, Milwaukee has simply been the better team in all facets.
Their plate discipline has worn down the Dodgers’ all-world pitching staff by forcing pitchers into prolonged at-bats and pouncing on mistakes. The Brewers have drawn 13 walks in this series.
For all the power hitting the Dodgers deploy, the Brewers own a staggering .458-to-.187 advantage in slugging percentage.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy has masterfully mixed and matched his pitching staff, and it’s helped produce a postseason-best 1.74 ERA.
This is a team built on role players, and their collective execution has far outweighed financial might and market size.
In order to advance, the Brewers will have to solve Tyler Glasnow, who owns a 1.73 ERA across 26 career postseason innings and has helped the Dodgers go 7-0 in games he’s pitched. Fortunately, for Milwaukee, command was a problem in the NLDS, having walked five Braves hitters.
Glasnow’s effectiveness has waned since his Aug. 25 return from a three-and-a-half-month absence due to back spasms. He’s managed a 4.15 ERA across 39 innings since Aug. 25, with his Stuff+ dipping to 98, per FanGraphs.
The Brewers will counter with rookie left-hander Shane Drohan, who hasn’t pitched since Sept. 27, before potentially turning to former Dodger Dustin May for bulk innings.
While it’s hardly an intimidating arrangement on paper, the bullpen has allowed just one earned run over 28 ⅔ innings.

The Dodgers would need to crack that with a lineup that has batted .165 with a .187 slugging percentage in the series. And, oh yeah, they’re sticking with Shohei Ohtani, whose perseverance through injuries has made for a .182 average through seven postseason games and no home runs since Aug. 18.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Pat Murphy's Managing Masterclass Outshines Dave Roberts, Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy
item.description: The 2026 National League Championship Series has been all Milwaukee Brewers so far. Milwaukee has a commanding three-game lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers with Game 4 scheduled to be played on Thursday night. If the Brewers win, they will advance to the World Series. There were many who thought the Brewers' streak of winning the National League Central would come to an end this season. Instead, the Brewers are on the doorstep of history. There are many reasons why Milwaukee has outplayed the Do
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 National League Championship Series has been all Milwaukee Brewers so far.
Milwaukee has a commanding three-game lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers with Game 4 scheduled to be played on Thursday night. If the Brewers win, they will advance to the World Series.
There were many who thought the Brewers' streak of winning the National League Central would come to an end this season. Instead, the Brewers are on the doorstep of history. There are many reasons why Milwaukee has outplayed the Dodgers throughout the series. The bullpen has been incredible, Jake Bauers has shined and the rotation has done its job. One guy who deserves a lot of credit is Pat Murphy, as well.
There's a reason why he's the two-time reigning National League Manager of the Year and should win the award again. Murphy has pushed all of the right buttons throughout the NLCS. Between the Brewers and the Dodgers, the NLCS has two of the best managers in the game in Murphy and Dave Roberts. Of the two, Murphy has clearly been the best this series, though.
The Brewers Are Sitting Pretty
It seems like every single decision the Brewers have made this series has been the right one. In Game 2, the Brewers put David Hamilton in the starting lineup and he went 2-for-3 with three runs scored and two stolen bases. That was a game-changer. In Game 1, the Brewers had Luis Lara in the starting lineup and he drove in what would end up being the game-winning run for Milwaukee. In Game 3, the Brewers started the game with Christian Yelich, Sal Frelick and Hamilton all on the bench. Andrew Vaughn, who replaced Yelich in the lineup, drew an important walk in the seventh inning. Then, Yelich pinch-ran for him and was driven in by Bauers' two-run homer.
Ortiz, who was at third base over Hamilton, drove in a run during the Game 3 win as well. Plus, the Brewers have gotten seemingly every pitching decision right. The starters haven't gone deep and Milwaukee has known exactly when to turn it over to the bullpen. On the other hand, Roberts made what could be argued as a few mistakes, specifically in Game 3. Andy Pages was yanked in favor of Max Muncy. Prized rookie Josue De Paula was wasted in Game 3 as well and was replaced by Kiké Hernandez at a critical point in the game. Plus, the offense in general has done nothing.
Milwaukee has pushed all of the right buttons, whereas the Dodgers have faltered. This is absolutely a testament to Murphy, as well as the players on the field.

Roberts, entonces utilizado como corredor emerg
item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts sabe que se puede porque ayudó a hacerlo posible. Con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles abajo 0-3 ante los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, el manager tiene un recuerdo al cual aferrarse: fue protagonista de la única remontada de esa magnitud en la historia de la postemporada de Grandes Ligas.
Los Medias Rojas de Boston de 2004 son el único equipo que perdió los primeros tres encuentros de una serie a ganar cuatro y consiguió levantarse para avanzar. Roberts, entonces utilizado como corredor emergente, puso las piernas en la jugada que mantuvo con vida aquel regreso frente a los Yankees de Nueva York.
“Por supuesto que es posible. Yo lo viví, y creo que nuestros muchachos han sido puestos a prueba en grandes batallas, como aquel equipo del que fui parte”, declaró Roberts después de la derrota en el tercer encuentro.
El piloto angelino reconoció que la tarea comienza con algo más inmediato que imaginar cuatro victorias consecutivas: encontrar la primera.
La mentalidad tiene que ser que debemos ganar mañana. Es un juego de eliminación. Hemos disputado muchos juegos de eliminación. Tenemos que conseguir una victoria. Debemos encontrar la manera de generar impulso, y para eso necesitamos a todos”.
Un robo que abrió la puerta
Los Medias Rojas estaban a tres outs de ser barridos en el cuarto juego de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana de 2004. Los Yankees ganaban 4-3 en la novena entrada y tenían sobre la lomita a Mariano Rivera.
Kevin Millar recibió una base por bolas y Roberts entró a correr en su lugar. Aunque todos podían anticipar sus intenciones, el actual manager de los Dodgers robó la segunda base y después anotó el empate con un sencillo de Bill Mueller.
David Ortiz resolvió aquel encuentro con un jonrón de dos carreras en la entrada 12. Boston ganó también los siguientes tres partidos, completó la remontada y posteriormente barrió a los Cardenales de San Luis para conquistar su primera Serie Mundial desde 1918.
La historia concede muy poco
Los Dodgers se convirtieron en el equipo número 43 que enfrenta una desventaja de 0-3 en una serie de postemporada pactada a un máximo de siete juegos. En las 42 series anteriores, el conjunto que perdió los primeros tres encuentros terminó eliminado 41 veces: únicamente Boston sobrevivió, una tasa de éxito de 2.4 por ciento.
Sólo dos equipos consiguieron igualar 3-3 después de comenzar con tres derrotas: aquellos Medias Rojas de 2004 y los Astros de Houston de 2020.
Houston reaccionó contra los Rays de Tampa Bay en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana disputada en San Diego. Los Astros ganaron los encuentros cuatro, cinco y seis, pero perdieron el definitivo y se quedaron a una victoria de acompañar a Boston en esa exclusiva lista.
Los Bravos de 1998, ante los Padres, y los Mets de 1999, contra Atlanta, llegaron al sexto juego, pero quedaron eliminados.
Roberts necesita ahora que sus jugadores recorran el mismo camino que él ayudó a abrir hace 22 años. La diferencia es que esta vez deberá impulsar la remontada desde el dugout.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are on the brink of elimination. With a 6-2 loss in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, they are at risk of being swept by the Milwaukee Brewers and watching their chances of a three-peat be dashed.
Manager Dave Roberts has been in this position before as a player. In 2004, the Boston Red Sox faced a 3-0 deficit in the American League Championship Series before rallying to win four games in a row and knock out the New York Yankees before sweeping the St. Louis Cardinals in the World Series. A key stolen base by Roberts in the ninth inning of Game 4 sparked the comeback.
However, after Game 3 of the NLCS, Roberts was asked about the 2004 comeback and made clear that that is not his focus heading into Game 4 against the Brewers.
“They’ve all seen the documentary, so they know it can happen,” Roberts said.
Dave Roberts Weighs in on 2004 ALCS Comeback
It has been 22 years since the Red Sox pulled off their comeback against the Yankees. They were three outs away from being swept out of the playoffs by the Yankees.
Roberts obviously played a key role in that as a player with his stolen base. But the point he makes is that what happened in 2004 is irrelevant. The Dodgers are in the exact same spot as the Red Sox were, but to win this series, the focus isn’t going to be on the past, but rather, what they can do to chip away at the Brewers.
No two situations are going to play out exactly the same, even though the Dodgers are in the same position the Red Sox were all those years ago, this potential comeback will look a lot different.
Things are not looking good for the Dodgers, but Roberts made clear that he doesn’t want his team to dwell on the past and try to find inspiration in something that took place 22 years ago.
What that series proved is that it’s always possible for the unexpected to happen, and it is a reminder that it’s never over until it’s over. But that was a long time ago. The Dodgers have business to take care of and cannot afford to get lost in the past and try to replicate what was done.
They’re going to have to do it their own way. They have won back-to-back World Series titles after all, so there is certainly still some hope.
What’s Next for Los Angeles Dodgers After Game 3 Loss?
The Dodgers have already announced Tyler Glasnow as their Game 4 starter. If they win Game 4, they’ll get the ball back in Tarik Skubal’s hands for Game 5. Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Blake Snell would be next in line for Games 6 and 7 if the series gets that far. One win could potentially give the Dodgers a little bit of momentum as they try to get back to the World Series and stave off elimination, but there is a lot of momentum that they are already up against as they head into Game 4.

item.title: [New York Post] Kiké Hernández in his feels after Dodgers’ NLCS Game 3 loss: ‘This one sucks’

item.description: The Dodgers’ Game 3 NLCS loss to the Brewers on Wednesday hit hard for fans and players alike. Beloved Dodgers utilityman Kiké Hernández seemed to take this loss especially tough, given how he looked when speaking to the media postgame. “We didn’t expect to be in this situation, this position. But this one sucks,” Hernández said, per Santiago Gil Sam. “We’ve got to find a way to turn the page quick, because tomorrow is gonna be here pretty fast. And, yeah. We lose, we’re done. So we gotta go on
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers’ Game 3 NLCS loss to the Brewers on Wednesday hit hard for fans and players alike.
Beloved Dodgers utilityman Kiké Hernández seemed to take this loss especially tough, given how he looked when speaking to the media postgame.
“We didn’t expect to be in this situation, this position. But this one sucks,” Hernández said, per Santiago Gil Sam.
“We’ve got to find a way to turn the page quick, because tomorrow is gonna be here pretty fast. And, yeah. We lose, we’re done. So we gotta go on one-game winning streaks for four games in a row and see what happens. But, yeah, this one sucks,” he added.
Hernández’s eyes were noticeably watery throughout the interview, and he looked like he was about to cry when realizing that the Dodgers likely lost their one opportunity to salvage this NLCS.
Hernández doesn’t need to be reminded that history has not boded well for MLB teams down 3-0 in a series. Only one of 43 teams has won a series from this position, and Los Angeles’ uninspired performance to this point doesn’t make it seem like they will be No. 2.
The 35-year-old Hernández hasn’t tallied a hit in five NLCS at-bats. He’ll be a free agent after this season, which could mean Thursday will be his last game wearing a Dodgers uniform.
Perhaps that played in to his emotional reaction to Los Angeles’ Game 3 defeat.

item.content:encoded:
米メディア『ドジャース・ウェイ』は13日（日本時間14日）、「『大谷翔平は投手をやめるべきか』という議論が現実味を帯びてきた」と題して記事を公開。「ユニコーンとしての地位は間もなく終わりを迎えるかもしれない」とし、身体的負担の大きい二刀流を続けることが可能か、疑問の声が高まっている現状を伝えた。
■打者専念も……ポストシーズン絶不調
左膝痛、首周りの不調、右上腕二頭筋の炎症などを抱え、9月上旬に負傷者リスト入りした大谷。復帰後は今シーズン中の「二刀流」を断念し、打者に専念すると表明した。それでも完全回復には至っておらず、その影響からかレギュラーシーズン終盤からポストシーズンにかけて極度の打撃不振に陥っている。
そこで『ドジャース・ウェイ』は、「根本的な問題として、大谷は投手としてのキャリアを終える時が来たのだろうか」と投げ掛けた。
同メディアは記事の中で、米ポッドキャスト番組『ファウル・テリトリー』で司会を務めるA.J.ピアジンスキー氏のコメントを紹介。同氏はナ・リーグ優勝決定シリーズでドジャースが連敗した直後、同番組内で大谷に対する見解を述べた。
「ある朝、彼は目を覚まして『もう投手はやらない』と言うかもしれない」とし、それは早ければ来年訪れてもおかしくないと主張した。
■あと何年投げられる？
さらに「私は、彼とチームが契約した時に『あと何年で投げられなくなるのか』と疑問を提示したんだ」とし、この元メジャーリーグ捕手は以前から二刀流の“寿命”に注目していたと明かした。その上で「投手を続けることで得られるものが、そのための負担に見合うのか、近いうちに問う必要があるだろう」と指摘した。
投打を担うことで生じる負担と打撃への影響が改めて議論の的となっているが、『ドジャース・ウェイ』は「現在の打撃不振を二刀流の負担というだけで説明できるのか。投手をやめるべきだという結論も、外部から一方的に下せるものではない。今後の起用法は、大谷本人とデーブ・ロバーツ監督、アンドリュー・フリードマン編成本部長らが協議すべき課題である」とした。
大谷の二刀流を支えつつ、どう疲労や故障を抑え、どう能力を引き出すか。『ドジャース・ウェイ』は「ピアジンスキー氏の“負担に見合うのか”という問いは、来季以降の起用を考える上で重い論点になりそうだ」と締めくくった。

item.dc:creator: This article first appeared; Was Syndicated
item.description: Rawlings Gold Glove Award finalists for the National League and American League were announced, with the Los Angeles Dodgers having Max Muncy (third base) and Andy Pages (center field) placing among the top-three finishers at their respective positions. item.content:encoded:
Rawlings Gold Glove Award finalists for the National League and American League were announced, with the Los Angeles Dodgers having Max Muncy (third base) and Andy Pages (center field) placing among the top-three finishers at their respective positions.
The 2026 season marks a fifth consecutive year in which the Dodgers have had multiple Gold Glove Award finalists. Mookie Betts (shortstop) and Miguel Rojas (utility) were last season’s representatives.
From 2022-24, the Dodgers have had seven other nominees. Betts has been the only Dodgers player to win a Gold Glove since 2022, as he took home the hardware for right field that year.
Gold Glove Award winners for the nine standard positions are determined via vote of MLB managers and up to six coaches from each team. Managers and coaches cannot vote for their own players and are only permitted to submit ballots for those in their same league.
Those votes amount to 75% of the selection total, with the SABR Defensive Index accounting for the remaining 25%.
The Toronto Blue Jays and Chicago Cubs had an MLB-best five players named finalists, with the Atlanta Braves, Arizona Diamondbacks, Texas Rangers and Kansas City Royals close behind at four apiece.
All 2026 Gold Glove Award winners will be announced live on ESPN on Sunday, Nov. 1.
For Muncy, it is his second career Gold Glove nomination and his first as a third baseman.
It is an impressive accomplishment for Muncy, improving his defense to such an extent in his age 36 season. He is looking to win his first career Gold Glove Award after falling short as a first baseman in 2021.
Alex Bregman (Chicago Cubs) and Javier Sanoja (Marlins) are the other two finalists.
Pages has been one of the best defensive center fielders in baseball since his breakout 2025 season.
In just his third season, he has already collected his first individual award this season as a representative in the Fall Classic.
It would be the first Gold Glove of his career if he can secure the votes. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts foresaw this outcome for the 25-year-old at the midpoint of the season.
Pages arm has arguably been his best weapon on defense this season, as he led the league with 13 outfield assists.
He is facing some stiff competition, with Pete Crow-Armstrong and Michael Harris II also up for consideration.

item.title: [Us Weekly] Dodgers’ Alex Call Argues He Can’t Watch Baseball on TV With His Son Due to ‘Half-Naked Women’ in Ads

item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call argued that scandalous commercials are getting in the way of passing down his love of baseball to his son. “Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?” Call, 32, posted via X on Wednesday, October 14. “My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this.” Alex and his wife, Saman
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call argued that scandalous commercials are getting in the way of passing down his love of baseball to his son.
“Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?” Call, 32, posted via X on Wednesday, October 14. “My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this.”
Alex and his wife, Samantha, share a son born in 2023 whose name has been kept private and daughter Reverie, 9 months.
The Dodgers player was responding to a social media post that wondered if Major League Baseball is interested in getting “more kids” watching the sport.
“Maybe start with the commercials,” Utah-based entrepreneur Taylor Murphy wrote. “Watching the playoffs tonight with my kids and here’s the rundown: Megan Fox selling ED pills in a red bodysuit. The scariest movie trailer you’ve ever seen. Sydney Sweeney in zero clothes promoting betting on sports.”
He continued, “Leagues can’t figure out why kids don’t watch. You don’t need a Nickelodeon game. You’re not the Savannah Bananas. Just show baseball in a way I can leave on in my house.”
Murphy’s post has gone viral since being posted Monday, October 12, earning over 31,000 likes.
Sweeney’s ad campaign for sports trading app NOVIG has been particularly controversial. The commercials, which have aired throughout the 2026 MLB Playoffs, feature the actress, 29, in various states of undress with sports equipment covering her naked body.
Sharon Stone, who costarred with Sweeney on HBO’s Euphoria, urged the young star to “take responsibility for her actions.”
“It is up to me to be a cheerleader for the women who have made it through and become champions in women’s sports,” Stone, 68, told People last month.
Call played in 88 games as a reserve outfielder for the Dodgers during the 2026 season. He has yet to see any postseason action.
The athlete shared photos of his family of four to celebrate Mother’s Day in May.
“You are the heart of our family,” Call wrote via Instagram. “When I’m gone for a week at a time, you’re home grinding it out, taking care of our kids with a kind of love and sweetness that bring me joy every time I think about it. Our family doesn’t work without you, and I don’t know what I would do without you. You’re my best friend. You make me happier than I ever knew was possible. There’s no one I’d rather do life with, raise these kids with, or come home to.”
The Dodgers will attempt to avoid being swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series in Los Angeles on Thursday, October 15.

His answer was no, leaving Los Angeles to pursue a comeback without either pitcher as a relief option. The decision comes afte
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has ruled out using Tarik Skubal or Yoshinobu Yamamoto in relief for Thursday's must-win Game 4 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
According to Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet, Roberts was asked whether either starter could be available out of the bullpen with the Dodgers facing elimination. His answer was no, leaving Los Angeles to pursue a comeback without either pitcher as a relief option.
The decision comes after Milwaukee defeated Los Angeles 6-2 in Game 3 on Wednesday, pushing the Dodgers into a 3-0 series deficit. The Brewers are now one win away from reaching the World Series for the first time since 1982.
Skubal started Game 1 of the series and allowed two runs over five innings, recording seven strikeouts and two walks. The Dodgers lost that game 2-1, putting the pressure on their rotation early in the series.
Yamamoto started Game 2 but struggled to work deep into the contest. He allowed three runs on four hits and two walks over 2 2/3 innings as Milwaukee secured a 7-4 victory. The right-hander had been named the 2025 World Series MVP after helping Los Angeles win the championship.
The Dodgers entered the postseason after finishing the regular season 100-62, while Milwaukee went 103-59 to earn the National League's top seed. The Brewers have carried that form into the NLCS, winning the first three games and limiting Los Angeles' margin for error.
Tyler Glasnow is scheduled to start Game 4 for the Dodgers. He pitched 4 2/3 innings of one-run baseball in the NLDS-clinching win over the Atlanta Braves, although he issued five walks in that appearance.
The Dodgers must win four consecutive games to advance, beginning Thursday at Dodger Stadium. Only the 2004 Boston Red Sox have overcome a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven MLB postseason series.
Roberts' decision means Los Angeles will need Glasnow and its available bullpen arms to handle the elimination game. Milwaukee, meanwhile, can clinch the NLCS and secure its first World Series berth since 1982 with another victory.
This story was originally published by Athlon on Oct 15, 2026, where it first appeared in the MLB section. Add Athlon as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Miguel Rojas is getting rightfully roasted for fate-tempting cleats as Dodgers go down 3-0

Since then, all the talk about from the national media has been whether or not they could follow that 1998-2000 New York Yankees squad into the hallowed halls of three-peaters. item.content:encoded:
These Los Angeles Dodgers broke a 25-year streak by becoming the first back-to-back champions with the World Series victory over the Toronto Blue Jays last year.
Since then, all the talk about from the national media has been whether or not they could follow that 1998-2000 New York Yankees squad into the hallowed halls of three-peaters.
Down 2-0 to the Brewers in the NLCS, however, the goal of Game 3 was merely about survival. Which is why Miguel Rojas' cleats suggesting that a third title is on the horizon has naturally garnered quite a lot of attention on social media.
Now faced with the prospect of having to win four games in a row to even advance to the World Series, baseball fans may be waiting for that three-peat to load for quite a long time.
Dodgers have been humbled by Brewers, but they're equipped to make an improbable NLCS comeback
Because the Dodgers have been so dominant for so long, fans of other teams rarely miss their chance dunk on Los Angeles when the opportunity presents itself.
The good news for the Dodgers is that this series isn't over. A 3-0 deficit is daunting, but they're better equipped than most to come back from it. Tyler Glasnow will take the ball tonight against old friend Dustin May, giving Dave Roberts a clear advantage on the mound from the get-go.
If the Dodgers able to stave off the sweep at Chavez Ravine, they'll get one more game at home, this time with Tarik Skubal on the mound. Then, Game 6 in Milwaukee would allow them to deploy Yoshinobu Yamamoto again. After that would come a do-or-die Game 7 with Blake Snell eyeing a chance at redemption after Jake Bauers got the better of him last night.
That's a lot of looking ahead for a team that hasn't won a game in the NLCS to date, but it's a reminder of how stacked this roster is. Even with Jacob Misiorowski waiting in the wings, you'd have to like the Dodgers' chances of winning with Skubal and Yamamoto on the mound if they can get to their next starts.
It all starts with getting back in win column tonight and delaying the inevitable for another day. Failing that, Rojas may need to find the nearest dumpster in which to deposit his custom cleats.

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ blasts on brink of World Series
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: Is this finally the year the Brewers exorcise their playoff demons and advance past the Dodgers on the Senior Circuit side of the bracket? Alongside LA, Milwaukee has been the class of the NL regular season for the last decade. However, they have never beaten their postseason final boss during this era, getting eliminated by the Dodgers in seven games in the instant classic 2018 NLCS before getting swept in the 2020 NL Wild Card Series and 2025 NLCS. MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ bl
item.content:encoded:
Is this finally the year the Brewers exorcise their playoff demons and advance past the Dodgers on the Senior Circuit side of the bracket? Alongside LA, Milwaukee has been the class of the NL regular season for the last decade. However, they have never beaten their postseason final boss during this era, getting eliminated by the Dodgers in seven games in the instant classic 2018 NLCS before getting swept in the 2020 NL Wild Card Series and 2025 NLCS.
MLB Playoff Roundup: Bauers leads Brewers’ blasts on brink of World Series
Milwaukee is on the cusp of sweeping the Dodgers and making their second World Series appearance in franchise history.
That finally looks set to change, the Brewers taking a commanding 3-0 lead in the series on a brilliant start from Robert Gasser and home runs from Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers, and Garrett Mitchell. With one more win, they’ll not only avenge those losses, but also win their first pennant in 44 years, when Harvey’s Wallbangers led the 1982 Brewers to the AL flag. Only the Pirates and Mariners have waited longer for a World Series berth. Could this be the year at last for dreams of a first Brewers championship to truly ignite?
They have one more win to go. Here’s how they got to the doorstep.
NLCS Game 3
Milwaukee Brewers 5, Los Angeles Dodgers 2
(Milwaukee leads, 3-0)
There is no better start to the game as a visiting team than a leadoff home run to put the home starter and crowd immediately on the back foot. Chourio said “hold my beer” as he homered on the first pitch of Game 3, ambushing a center-cut four-seamer from Blake Snell and lining it oppo just over the wall in right-center to instantly deflate a raucous crowd at Chavez Ravine who had been desperate to energize their wounded Dodgers. It is already the third postseason leadoff home run in the young career of the Brewers’ star left fielder, Chourio the hero of the NLDS against the Padres with six RBIs in four games.
Gasser typifies a Milwaukee Brewers player — a gamer with plenty of talent but not a name a baseball fan outside of Wisconsin is likely to recognize. He was part of the 2022 deadline trade that sent Josh Hader to San Diego. He debuted in 2024 but missed most of that and the next season to Tommy John surgery. He spent the first month-and-a-half of 2026 at Triple-A but didn’t look back after a mid-May call-up, starting 20 games and posting a 5-5 record, 3.87 ERA, 4.23 FIP, 103 strikeouts and 1.5 fWAR in 109.1 innings.
With the Brewers unsettled on their postseason rotation plans, Gasser allowed one or fewer runs in his final four starts of the regular season to cement his starting role in the playoffs. The 27-year-old lefty held the Padres to a run on three hits in four innings of Game 4 of the NLDS as the Brewers punched their ticket to the next round. Against this backdrop of hitting his stride once the games really started to matter, Gasser pitched possibly the best start of his life last night.
He’s not going to blow you away with velocity, but the unique way he hides the ball until the last moment of his delivery let his mid-90s sinker play up in LA. The Dodgers had no answer for the pitch as Gasser was able to paint both sides of the plate, getting the ball by the dangerous hitters in their lineup as if they collectively were not ready to hit the fastball.
Gasser waltzed through five scoreless innings allowing just three hits and a walk, but cameras curiously spotted handshakes in the dugout between the fifth and sixth innings. Gasser hadn’t had to make a stressful pitch all game and seemed to have plenty in the tank at just 72 pitches, but trainers did appear to be tending to a blister on the ring finger of his pitching hand. Practically every button that Brewers manager Pat Murphy has pushed this season and postseason has worked, seeing the team pace MLB with 103 wins and easily brush aside the Padres in the NLDS before taking a 2-0 lead over the two-time reigning champions, but this one blew up in his face.
Whatever the case, Murphy called on Abner Uribe for the sixth inning and it backfired spectacularly. He walked Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker, and Shohei Ohtani (batting a rare sixth amid his awful slump) to load the bases with one out. Despite a pair of relievers hot in the Milwaukee bullpen, Murphy allowed Uribe to face the struggling Will Smith — 1-for-23 in six games this postseason. Smith ambushed a first pitch sinker right down the pipe, the deep fly ball clanging halfway up the wall in left-center to plate a pair and give the Dodgers their first lead of the series, 2-1.
Murphy belatedly called on flame throwing lefty DL Hall to clean up Uribe’s mess, and he struck out Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman to strand runners on second and third and limit the damage to the two runs.
Murphy was perhaps vindicated in lifting his starter earlier than it seemed necessary, because we witnessed the flip side of that debate two innings later. It is perhaps fitting that Snell was the starter opposite Gasser in this game —the Rays’ Kevin Cash memorably removed Snell in the sixth inning of Game 6 of the 2020 World Series against the Dodgers despite Snell having struck out nine and not allowed a run on just 73 pitches — Gasser removed with his pitch count at 72.
After the Chourio leadoff blast, Snell was untouchable for six innings, allowing one hit and one walk while striking out nine as his four-seamer had some extra juice en route to racking up a gaudy 46-percent whiff rate. Dave Roberts allowed his dominating starter to come back out for the seventh, and it is amazing how the tide turned in an instant. He issued a leadoff walk to Andrew Vaughn, but with two lefties due up in Bauers and Mitchell, Roberts stuck with his southpaw starter.
The fatigue was apparent against Bauers, Snell’s misses occurring over the heart of the plate instead of outside of the zone, and the Brewers’ regular season home run leader won the monumental 11-pitch battle by blasting a middle-middle full count four-seamer 412 feet to right to put the Brewers back on top, 3-2. Mitchell then jumped on a 1-0 mistake changeup right down the middle, going back-to-back with Bauers to almost the exact same spot of the ballpark.
It was the first time in Snell’s entire career that he had allowed back-to-back homers to lefties and just the second time that he’d ever allowed two lefty-hitter homers in the same game (let alone inning). He’d allowed one lefty-hitter homer since Juan Soto took him deep for the Yankees in June 2024 in San Francisco.
That fully sucked all of the air out of Dodger Stadium, and the team nor their fans could will the comeback. Milwaukee added a pair of valuable insurance runs in the eighth and ninth. Brice Turang and William Contreras reached in the eighth on consecutive one-out singles to put runners on the corners where a Justin Wrobleski wild pitch allowed Turang to score the Brewers’ fifth run. Rookie Cooper Pratt lined a one-out single in the ninth, stole second, and scored on a Joey Ortiz single to make it 6-2. Hall and closer Trevor Megill combined to pitch a scoreless final 3.2 innings to seal the win and put the Brewers on the brink of sweeping the champions of the last two seasons.
Game 4 is tomorrow with first pitch scheduled for 8:00 pm ET. Tyler Glasnow will look to keep the Dodgers’ season alive while Milwaukee has yet to name a starter. The Brewers now have four chances to clinch the series and advance to the Fall Classic, where they will look to win their first ever title as one of five teams to have never won a ring. No expansion team has waited longer. It may finally be the Brew Crew’s year.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers LF Alex Call “received a warm welcome from fans” at Dodger Stadium hours after he “made some controversial remarks about risqué advertisements that have been running during MLB games,” according to Edward Lewis of the N.Y. POST. Call was introduced to the crowd before Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday, and several fans “got out of their seat to cheer him on.”
Call first “pleaded for an end to the racy MLB advertisements, some of which featured a nearly nude Sydney Sweeney promoting prediction market Novig, on his Twitter page” on Tuesday. He described them as “soft porn.”
Call wrote: “Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB? My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women [sic] could come on screen anytime??” The post was “met with mixed reviews,” and Call has “yet to further address his statement” (N.Y. POST, 10/14).

item.title: [Yahoo] Fans de los Dodgers apoyan la postura de Alex Call tras la polémica con Sydney Sweeney
item.dc:creator: Tom Malley
item.description: Los fanáticos de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles no permitieron que los recientes comentarios de Alex Call sobre los comerciales de "pornografía suave" afectaran su apoyo hacia él antes del Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional el miércoles, ya que lo vitorearon como de costumbre durante la presentación de los jugadores. item.content:encoded:
Los fanáticos de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles no permitieron que los recientes comentarios de Alex Call sobre los comerciales de "pornografía suave" afectaran su apoyo hacia él antes del Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional el miércoles, ya que lo vitorearon como de costumbre durante la presentación de los jugadores.
Call, de 32 años, causó revuelo esta semana cuando comentó una publicación viral de X que criticaba los anuncios que se emiten durante los partidos de los playoffs de la MLB, afirmando que los padres no deberían tener que preocuparse de que "una mujer semidesnuda" aparezca en la pantalla en cualquier momento.
Las declaraciones del jardinero derecho de los Dodgers se producen tras semanas de controversia en torno a las atrevidas campañas publicitarias de la actriz de primera línea Sydney Sweeney con la empresa de pronósticos Novig, en las que aparece con poca ropa, y en algunos casos completamente desnuda, mientras se cubre estratégicamente con equipamiento deportivo.
Esta semana, los aficionados que sintonizaban los playoffs de la MLB se vieron expuestos a un anuncio sobre disfunción eréctil protagonizado por Megan Fox y el spot de Novig de Sweeney, respaldado por los dueños de la compañía, lo que provocó varias quejas de padres en internet.
Una de esas quejas llamó la atención de Call, quien respondió con su propia publicación argumentando que la MLB no necesitaba trucos para atraer a los espectadores más jóvenes, sino simplemente una transmisión que las familias pudieran seguir viendo cómodamente.
Dodgers outfielder Alex Call was cheered during the player introductions of Game 3 of the NLCS in the wake of his recent comments about MLB ads. https://t.co/9pePuNriDK pic.twitter.com/lXB5pT8hAZ
— California Post Sports (@capostsports) October 15, 2026
"¿Podemos, por favor, quitar los anuncios sugerentes de las transmisiones de los playoffs en TBS, Fox, NBC y la MLB?", escribió Call. "Mi hijo quiere ver béisbol con papá, pero ¿cómo lo justifico cuando una mujer semidesnuda podría aparecer en pantalla en cualquier momento? Este es el pasatiempo nacional de Estados Unidos. Los padres no deberían tener que preocuparse por esto".
Call recibió mucho apoyo por su mensaje, con muchos fanáticos de acuerdo con su postura y exigiendo que algo cambiara, y esos sentimientos hacia la estrella de los Dodgers ciertamente se transmitieron a las gradas el miércoles antes del choque del Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional de su equipo contra los Milwaukee Brewers.
En un video grabado desde las gradas y publicado en X, se podía ver a Call, quien no había aparecido en un partido de postemporada hasta el momento, a pesar de estar en la plantilla activa de los Dodgers, alineándose junto a sus compañeros en el campo del Dodger Stadium mientras se leían los nombres de los jugadores.
Tras una gran ovación para el tercera base de los Dodgers, Max Clusty, el nombre de Call fue el siguiente en la lista a ser anunciado, y se podía oír claramente a los aficionados dándole una cálida bienvenida mientras él saludaba cortésmente a la multitud.
Poco después, algunos aficionados acusaron a Joe Davis, de FOX Sports, de haber hecho la "peor narración de la historia" tras ser sorprendido en plena presentación cuando Jackson Chourio conectó un jonrón en el primer lanzamiento del tercer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional.
El comentarista de FOX estaba dando sus palabras de apertura antes del partido cuando Chourio sorprendió al primer lanzamiento del juego, enviando una bola rápida de 98 mph de Blake Snell a las gradas del jardín derecho para darle a los Brewers una ventaja de 1-0.
Desafortunadamente para todos los seguidores de Los Ángeles, el equipo no pudo lograr la victoria contra los Brewers, cayendo 6-2 y quedando abajo 3-0 en la serie al mejor de siete, al borde de la eliminación.
Eso convierte el cuarto partido de esta noche (jueves 15 de octubre), programado en el Dodger Stadium, en una victoria imprescindible para los Dodgers si quieren tener alguna posibilidad de lograr una remontada memorable, ya que otra derrota confirmaría el final de su temporada.

item.title: [The Daily Beast] MLB Star Hits Out at Sydney Sweeney’s ‘Soft Porn Ads’
item.dc:creator: Reagin von Lehe
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call called on Major League Baseball and its broadcast partners to remove what he called “soft porn” ads from 2026 playoff telecasts. Maybe start with the commercials,” Murphy said. When trying to watch the prog
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call called on Major League Baseball and its broadcast partners to remove what he called “soft porn” ads from 2026 playoff telecasts.
The callout was in response to an MLB fan on X, Taylor Murphy, who went viral after posting that the MLB could get younger kids watching if it aired ads that made parents comfortable leaving the TV on unattended.
“Wanna get more kids watching baseball? Maybe start with the commercials,” Murphy said.
When trying to watch the program with his kids, ads of Megan Fox selling erectile dysfunction pills in a red bodysuit, “the scariest movie trailer you’ve ever seen,” and Sydney Sweeney in “zero clothes” promoting sports betting aired between plays.
He continued, saying the MLB doesn’t need a Savannah Bananas gimmick or a Nickelodeon-style game. The league can simply “show baseball in a way I can leave on in my house.”
Call, a father of two, agreed with Murphy on X.
“Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts—TBS, Fox, NBC—@MLB?” Call wrote. “My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked woman could come on screen anytime?”
This is the sports world’s latest snub of Sweeney over her ad for the sports-prediction market Novig. She’s filmed talking about the “just sports” betting platform and covering her naked body with various sports equipment.
Female athletes and celebrities have responded, calling the ad “damaging” to women’s sports.
Four-time Olympic swimming champion Ariarne Titmus said it “monetizes” women’s bodies, while former UCLA gymnast Gracie Kramer said female athletes have long fought to be seen for their performance rather than their bodies.
Sprinter Amy Hunt, water-polo player Tilly Kearns, and rugby player Sofie Fella also all pushed back on the ad.
Novig CEO Jack Fortinsky defended the campaign, saying the company is “hugely supportive of women’s sports,” never intended to portray female athletes, and viewed Sweeney simply as an actress delivering a sports-focused message.
Though she hasn’t responded to Call directly, Sweeney publicly said she filmed the ad because she believes in the company’s leadership and message.
Murphy and Call received mixed responses, with parents supporting the take and others saying kids “aren’t the target audience” and the MLB doesn’t control the ads that play between programming. To which Murphy replied with a highlighted screenshot from a 2024 MLB advertising standards document.
The MLB reserves the right to “reject or instruct” any partner to cease the use of any ad “during, or in connection with, any Baseball Programming Transmission,” according to the document.
Call concluded his X rant with, “This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this.”
Obsessed with pop culture and entertainment? Follow us on Substack and YouTube for even more coverage.

"Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?" the Los Angeles Dodgers player wrote on X Wednesday, Oct. 14, in response to a
item.content:encoded:
NEED TO KNOW
- Alex Call is taking issue with suggestive ads that air during MLB games
- The Dodgers outfielder shared his outrage on X in a post
- "Parents shouldn't have to worry about this," Call, who is not on the team's postseason roster, said
Alex Call is calling foul on recent commercials that he says feature "half-naked women."
"Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB?" the Los Angeles Dodgers player wrote on X Wednesday, Oct. 14, in response to a post discussing the trend. "My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America's Pastime. Parents shouldn't have to worry about this."
Call's response was to a post in which a Utah-based X user shared his displeasure with commercials that star Sydney Sweeney and Megan Fox.
Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB? My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this. https://t.co/7YAWSZgo5d
— Alex Call (@ACAD_27) October 14, 2026
In addition to the 32-year-old outfielder, female athletes are among those outraged by Sweeney's sports-betting ad for Novig.
In the commercials, the Euphoria actress, 29, bares almost all while posing in provocative positions.
"Just you, your takes and sports," Sweeney, topless and holding her breasts, says into the camera.
Call — who was left off the Dodgers' postseason roster — has had time to watch games at home with his family amid the team's playoff run.
The right fielder also made headlines earlier this season for his position — in which he nearly injured Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani.
In July, Call clipped Ohtani's right elbow with his cleat while jumping over the dugout railing to celebrate the team's win against the Philadelphia Phillies.
Ohtani, 32, briefly clutched his elbow before the two players laughed off the near-miss.
Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!
On Wednesday night, the designated hitter managed a single in two at bats amid a self-owned slump triggered by lingering injuries.
"The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit," Ohtani told reporters through his interpreter on Tuesday, Oct. 13. "The results, [I] take full responsibility."
The Dodgers will try to stave off elimination on Friday, Oct. 16 for Game 5, when they face the Milwaukee Brewers, who will earn a trip to the World Series with a win.

item.dc:creator: Rex Villas

The Dodgers ace struggled to silence Milwaukee’s relentless bats, and perhaps no one personified that better than Brewers slugger Jake Bauers. The Milwaukee first baseman put on a batting masterclass in the seventh inning at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, Calif., battling Snell in an epic 11-pitch at-bat that featured five foul ba
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are facing an uphill battle in the 2026 National League Championship Series after Blake Snell failed to rescue his team in Game 3 on Wednesday.
The Dodgers ace struggled to silence Milwaukee’s relentless bats, and perhaps no one personified that better than Brewers slugger Jake Bauers.
The Milwaukee first baseman put on a batting masterclass in the seventh inning at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles, Calif., battling Snell in an epic 11-pitch at-bat that featured five foul balls before launching a go-ahead home run.
Every pitch from that UNREAL Jake Bauers at-bat 😤 11 pitches. One unforgettable moment. https://t.co/QpDMUMMPFP
— MLB (@MLB) October 15, 2026
That home run was followed by another solo blast off Snell from Brewers outfielder Garrett Mitchell.
That prompted Snell’s exit from the mound, as the Brewers went on to win the game, 6-2, for a commanding 3-0 series lead.
Despite his struggles against the Brewers, Snell gave props to his former teammate.
“I’ve known him since he got drafted with San Diego, then he was with the Rays. I was with him for
probably four years, something like that,” Snell said of Bauers, via Alden González of ESPN.
“I’ve seen all the ups and downs he’s been through and it’s been a lot of downs. So for him to go through this right now, he’s earned it. Hat’s off to him. I mean, what an at- bat. I threw everything I had. Fastball down the middle. If I can locate that better, who knows what would happen. It’s the best I’ve ever seen him play. It’s a good at-bat. Hat’s off to him.”
In six innings of work, Snell allowed four earned runs on four hits (three home runs), but racked up nine strikeouts through 101 pitches.
Unless the Dodgers find a way to overcome a 3-0 series deficit against Milwaukee, Snell has likely thrown his last pitch of 2026.

item.title: [FanSided] Freddie Freeman’s October collapse should put any Braves regret to bed
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman
item.description: In the 2021 offseason, the Atlanta Braves made the controversial decision to let Freddie Freeman, a franchise legend who had just led the team to a World Series title, walk in free agency. item.content:encoded:
In the 2021 offseason, the Atlanta Braves made the controversial decision to let Freddie Freeman, a franchise legend who had just led the team to a World Series title, walk in free agency. Freeman received a six-year, $162 million offer from the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Braves famously did not want to give the legend a sixth guaranteed year. Even though the Braves acquired an All-Star, Matt Olson, to replace him, many Braves fans were infuriated with the organization for letting a player of Freeman's stature go.
There have been times when letting Freeman walk has looked bad. He's been a great player in L.A. most of the time he's been there, and has had several iconic moments in Dodger Blue, including a pair of walk-off home runs in the World Series. How's this decision looking now, though? The decision to let Freeman walk and replace him with Olson looks better and better by the day, with Freeman's decline playing a major role.
Freddie Freeman is not the superstar he once was
Freeman was performing at a superstar level in the first four years of his contract with the Dodgers, hitting .310 with a .907 OPS with more postseason moments to remember than we can count. This season, however, he hit .288 with a career-low .792 OPS in the regular season, and somehow, it feels like only been regressing as the year has progressed. Freeman hit just one home run and had a .681 OPS in the second half of the regular season, and while he hit a couple of home runs in the NLDS against Atlanta, he's 5-for-26 (.192 BA) in the postseason overall, and 1-for-11 in the NLCS. Freeman has no-showed when the Dodgers have needed him most, alongside many of his star teammates.
It's easy to blame Freeman for his performance, but it's also worth noting that he's 37 years old. Father Time is undefeated at the end of the day, and that's exactly why the Braves were hesitant when it came to giving Freeman, who was already over the age of 30 while playing a position that historically doesn't age well, such a long deal.
Now, the Dodgers not only have to watch Freeman look overmatched with their season and three-peat on the line, but they have Freeman locked in for another year. If Freeman is declining at age 37, how will he look when he's a year older? Meanwhile, the Braves have Matt Olson, who is very much in his prime.
Matt Olson is making it easy for the Braves to forget all about Freddie Freeman
Olson has been just as good, if not better, than Freeman since the two changed teams ahead of the 2022 campaign. Sure, he isn't the contact hitter Freeman is, but Olson has hit at least 29 home runs, driven in 90 runs, and appeared in 162 games in each of his five seasons in Atlanta. He quite literally hasn't missed a single regular-season game since joining his hometown team. Since being traded to the Braves, Olson leads the majors in games played (810), ranks fifth in home runs (187) and third in RBI (528). Is that good? Oh, he's also made three All-Star teams, won a Silver Slugger, and he's a finalist to win his second Gold Glove in a Braves uniform. Again, is that good?
His postseason numbers have admittedly not measured up, and that's absolutely an issue, but is there really an argument regarding who the better player is overall right now? Olson is better, five years younger, cheaper (Olson makes $21 million annually while Freeman makes $27 million per year), and he's signed for longer, giving Atlanta more stability. Freeman will be a free agent after the 2027 campaign, while Olson is locked in through 2029 (with a club option for 2030). By that point, Olson will be 35 or 36 when he hits free agency, while Freeman is already older than that right now.
It's never easy to watch a franchise legend walk, and Braves fans have had to do just that with Freeman, Max Fried and Dansby Swanson, to name a few, in recent years. However, while you can argue that Fried and Swanson should've been brought back, can Braves fans really deny that Olson is an upgrade over Freeman at this point?
There're plenty of things the Braves should regret. Having Olson, a 32-year-old who might be the best overall player at his position right now, over Freeman, a 37-year-old in a steep decline, is not one of them.

item.content:encoded:
By BETH HARRIS AP Sports Writer
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Milwaukee Brewers hit the second-fewest home runs in baseball during the regular season, even as they topped the majors with 103 wins.
Maybe they were saving their biggest swings for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell launched back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh inning, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to build a 3-0 cushion in the National League Championship Series.
Jackson Chourio also went deep on the first pitch of the game to help the Brewers close within one win of their first NL pennant. Milwaukee was in the American League when the franchise reached its only World Series, a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said.
Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium, where the Brewers can become the first major league club to complete a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason.
Los Angeles took all four games against Milwaukee in the NLCS last year.
The Dodgers had just gone ahead 2-1 in the sixth inning before getting stunned by the Brewers in their three-run seventh. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination.
“All three games we’ve played so far, and hopefully that continues, where just every time they score, we come back and score,” Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy said. “That’s not easy to do in baseball.”
It was the fifth comeback victory in seven postseason games for the Brewers, who have never beaten Los Angeles in three previous playoff series.
The only other time the Dodgers trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.
The lone team in big league history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven postseason series was the Boston Red Sox in the 2004 AL Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“We’ve won four in a row a number of times this year,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “We’ve got to win tomorrow. That’s our only focus.”
Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 batters in a row. But the first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was hit for a home run by Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell’s solo shot.
Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the seventh and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot drive to right field on the 11th pitch of his at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of the players in Milwaukee’s dugout came onto the field to celebrate.
“I was looking for a fastball, and I didn’t want to miss it,” said Bauers, who had a team-leading 26 of Milwaukee’s 154 regular-season homers.
It was his latest relentless plate appearance, too, after Bauers drew a 12-pitch walk from Yoshinobu Yamamoto that helped the Brewers go ahead early in Game 2.
“I think what changed for me this year was I stopped caring about results,” Bauers said. “I started caring about competing. I started caring about being in the moment and getting out of my own way.”
Watching Bauers work over Snell was “super sick,” Mitchell said.
And then it was his turn.
Mitchell’s drive traveled 428 feet to right-center. That chased Snell, who hadn’t given up a home run in 46 1/3 innings this year entering the game. It was the first time in his career he served up back-to-back homers to left-handed hitters and only the second time he gave up multiple longballs to left-handed batters in one game.
Bauers and Mitchell became just the third pair of left-handed hitters with consecutive postseason home runs off the same left-handed pitcher. Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper did it for Philadelphia against Atlanta reliever Dylan Lee in an NL Wild Card Series this year, and Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig connected for the New York Yankees off Bill Sherdel of the St. Louis Cardinals in the 1928 World Series.
Milwaukee has five homers in the NLCS and eight this postseason.
Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six-plus innings. He struck out nine and walked two.
The Brewers extended their lead to 5-2 in the eighth on Justin Wrobleski’s wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single and advanced to third on William Contreras’ single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz’s two-strike RBI single in the ninth.
The offensively starved Dodgers took a 2-1 lead on Will Smith’s two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.
After rookie starter Robert Gasser pitched five shutout innings, Uribe entered and loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who was 1 for 25 in the playoffs, doubled off the left-center fence with one out for his first hit of the NLCS.
DL Hall took over from Uribe and stranded runners at second and third by striking out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman.
Hall allowed one hit in 2 1/3 scoreless innings to improve to 3-0 in these playoffs. Trevor Megill got four outs for his second save of the series and fourth this postseason.
The Dodgers played from behind again after the 22-year-old Chourio connected for his third career leadoff homer in the postseason as fans were still heading to their seats.
After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh.
The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings, but couldn’t get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS and are 3 for 32 with runners in scoring position this postseason.
Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk while hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he’s batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.
___

item.title: [amNewYork] Mets rumors: Is Tarik Skubal a legitimate target? | amNewYork
item.dc:creator: Joe Pantorno; Amnewyork
item.description: The prospect of Tarik Skubal becoming the Mets’ next big free-agent signing is already dancing in the head of some members of the organization. item.content:encoded:
The prospect of Tarik Skubal becoming the Mets’ next big free-agent signing is already dancing in the head of some members of the organization.
Zac Thornton spoke with Mike Puma of the New York Post earlier this week and admitted that it’s a hot topic of conversation with his teammates.
“I talk to [Nolan McLean] all the time about it, and he had some good talks with Skubal when they were in the [World Baseball Classic] together,” Thornton told Puma. “It would be awesome to bounce ideas, especially coming from another left-handed pitcher. Sean [Manaea] and I talk a lot, just about being lefties — there are not many around here, so it would be awesome to have another powerhouse left-handed pitcher around here.”
Even with a young core of promising arms like McLean, Thornton, Christian Scott, and Jonah Tong, president of baseball operations David Stearns made it clear in his end-of-season availability that “it is necessary for us to add to our rotation.”
Skubal would provide the bona fide veteran ace Freddy Peralta never became after his half season in Queens—though he certainly looks the part with the Tampa Bay Rays, who are battling the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS.
Regardless, the left-handed Skubal will be the crown jewel of the free agent market this winter. The two-time defending American League Cy Young Award winner was dealt from the Detroit Tigers to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the trade deadline and remained his dominant self, going 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 1.048 WHIP.
Over his last three seasons, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA and 655 strikeouts in 546 innings pitched.
With a lockout looming, which could potentially carry a salary cap that will limit player salaries, Skubal will likely sign quickly — and that deal will be historic. He is projected to sign the richest contract for a free-agent pitcher ever, which should exceed $300 million.
Whether Stearns would be intrigued by doling out such an offer might not be as cut-and-dry as many might initially think.
Yes, the Mets’ president of baseball operations has had an aversion to handing out long-term big-money contracts to pitchers, which is understandable given the fragility of many major-league arms and the seemingly never-ending onslaught of injuries that come with it.
Skubal himself missed a month earlier this season when he had to undergo surgery to remove loose bodies from his pitching elbow.
But Stearns has gone to the negotiating table with a big-money contract offer for a starting pitcher while with the Mets. He offered Yoshinobu Yamamoto a 12-year, $325 million deal in December of 2023, but the Japanese superstar took an identical deal to join the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Skubal would certainly fit the mold of coaxing such an offer from Stearns, especially if it means that the Mets are that much closer to legitimate contention in 2027, if there is baseball.

item.title: [truebluela.com] NLCS Game 4 viewing guide
item.dc:creator: Estevão Maximo
item.description: The Dodgers are one loss away from getting swept in the postseason for the first time since the 2023 NLDS against the Diamondbacks. No matter how you want to slice it, they’ve looked inferior in every facet of the game in this series, from situational hitting to defense, bullpen work, and so on—now it’ll be up to Tyler Glasnow to at the very least delay what appears to be an unavoidable postseason exit for the reigning back-to-back champs. Although the Brewers have yet to formally announce a sta
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are one loss away from getting swept in the postseason for the first time since the 2023 NLDS against the Diamondbacks. No matter how you want to slice it, they’ve looked inferior in every facet of the game in this series, from situational hitting to defense, bullpen work, and so on—now it’ll be up to Tyler Glasnow to at the very least delay what appears to be an unavoidable postseason exit for the reigning back-to-back champs.
Although the Brewers have yet to formally announce a starter, all signs point towards Dustin May taking the ball in Game 4 of this series—it might be with an opener, or it might be with him as a starter; either way, the bulk innings role will belong to the former Dodger.
When it comes to lineup decisions, Max Muncy figures to regain a starting role at third base, and you have to wonder if Will Smith remains in the seventh spot—the Dodger catcher was responsible for the only big hit the home team had in a Game 3 loss. Speaking of hitters who moved down in the order, although it amounted to very little, Shohei Ohtani reached safely in three of his four plate appearances in a 6-2 defeat.
Neither Evan Phillips nor Roki Sasaki had especially lengthy appearances off the bullpen, so apart from Justin Wrobleski, there’ll be no one else unavailable in the bullpen for Game 4. With nothing to lose and following the seventh-inning debacle of leaving Blake Snell in too long, expect potential aggressive calls to the bullpen at the first sign of trouble for Glasnow.
NLCS Game 4 info
- Teams: No. 2 seed Dodgers vs. No. 1 seed Brewers
- Series: Milwaukee leads, 3-0
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium, Los Angeles
- Start time: 5:08 p.m.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Max Muncy Puts Dodgers' Problems Plainly
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are now down 3-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, and Dodgers veteran Max Muncy knows exactly why that is. Wednesday night was a frustrating loss in which the Dodgers finally seemed to fix their offensive woes, only for star pitcher Blake Snell to implode with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning. Max Muncy sounds off on the Dodgers Muncy, the third baseman, was asked by reporters what has been going on with the team’s offensive
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are now down 3-0 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, and Dodgers veteran Max Muncy knows exactly why that is.
Wednesday night was a frustrating loss in which the Dodgers finally seemed to fix their offensive woes, only for star pitcher Blake Snell to implode with back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning.
Max Muncy sounds off on the Dodgers
Muncy, the third baseman, was asked by reporters what has been going on with the team’s offensive struggles, and he pulled no punches.
“It’s a pretty simple answer. We’re playing like s—. They’re playing great,” he said, as reported by the California Post’s Jack Harris and other reporters.
In case you think Muncy is being hyperbolic, he’s not.
As detailed by Newsweek baseball writer J.P. Hoornstra, the Dodgers are one of 274 teams too play at least seven postseason games in a season since 1903.
Their team OPS of .572 isn’t just in the lower end of that group; it’s almost dead last.
The 2026 Dodgers are 268th, meaning only six teams have had a worse OPS in more than a century.
It’s a far cry from the powerful lineup fans expected from the back-to-back World Series champions.
In fact, the Dodgers haven’t hit a home run at all in this series against the Brewers, despite boasting power hitters like Muncy, Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and plenty of others.
What’s next for the Dodgers?
The Dodgers will try to avoid “playing like s—” for a fourth straight game on Thursday, knowing that a loss will end their season.
Tyler Glasnow is the mound for the Boys in Blue as they look to avoid the sweep.
The game will begin at 5 p.m. PT, an hour earlier than the previously announced start time of 6 p.m. PT.
Pitcher Blake Snell, who started Game 3 and gave up a pair of back-breaking home runs in the seventh inning, told reporters the team is focused on winning Thursday’s game.
“Yeah, it sucks, but it’s part of it,” he said. “How do we bounce back, how do we fight? I think that’s the most important thing, us coming together and finding a way to win.”
Do you think the Dodgers can stave off elimination on Thursday?

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dave Roberts' Blake Snell decision was the tip of the iceberg in mortifying Dodgers Game 3 loss
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
