Shohei Ohtani is forcing Dave Roberts to make a critical decision for the Dodgers With the Los Angeles Dodgers facing a difficult situation in the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, all eyes will be on Shohei Ohtani as he looks to end his offensive slump and rediscover the dominant form that has made him one of baseball’s biggest s
item.content:encoded:
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Blake Snell's shocking new look and the multi-million dollar mission to save the Dodgers
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Shohei Ohtani is forcing Dave Roberts to make a critical decision for the Dodgers
With the Los Angeles Dodgers facing a difficult situation in the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, all eyes will be on Shohei Ohtani as he looks to end his offensive slump and rediscover the dominant form that has made him one of baseball’s biggest stars.
Heading into Game 3, manager Dave Roberts confirmed a significant change in the Japanese star’s place in the batting order and shared Ohtani’s mindset — he is willing to make any adjustment to help the team.
Dodgers drop Shohei Ohtani lower in the lineup
Accustomed to hitting near the top of the order, either leading off or in the upper half of the lineup, Ohtani will bat sixth on Wednesday, the lowest spot he has ever occupied in his Major League career.
For Roberts, the decision reflects the Japanese star’s commitment to the Dodgers.
“Shohei Ohtani stayed late at Dodger Stadium working on his swing,” Bob Nightengale wrote on X, “with manager Dave Roberts calling him the ultimate team player.”
Ohtani’s current form stands in sharp contrast to previous seasons. The four-time MVP.150 in the playoffs.
Despite the prolonged struggle, the Japanese star refuses to quit. Ohtani even stayed after a workout at Dodger Stadium to continue working on his swing — a clear sign of his determination to return to form.
“He was determined, and that’s an understatement,” Roberts said.
Shohei Ohtani confident he can respond
The lack of offensive production and ongoing physical discomfort led some to question whether the Dodgers should bench him. But Ohtani is convinced he has found meaningful mechanical adjustments in his swing.
“He was very convinced that he is onto something mechanically,” Roberts said, via MLB.com. “He was adamant that he can help us. He’s well enough to help us win a baseball game. So that’s all I needed to hear.”
Now the Dodgers hope Game 3 becomes the turning point for both Ohtani and the team, which finds itself on the ropes after falling into an 0-2 hole against the Brewers in the NLCS.

item.content:encoded:
In early August, the Detroit Tigers put to rest any idea of extending ace pitcher Tarik Skubal, who was dealt to the Los Angeles Dodgers in return for a trio of prospects, which included pitcher River Ryan.
While the Tigers unfortunately failed to earn a spot in the MLB postseason, the Dodgers are back in the National League Championship Series once again. And Skubal is attempting to help the club become the first team in over a quarter-century to win three straight World Series titles.
Former Detroit Tigers Pitcher Tarik Skubal Comes Clean On Heavy Expectations
Given his status as one of the premier players at his position in baseball, along with what the Dodgers are trying to accomplish, Skubal is well aware of the heavy expectations that he’s facing.
However, he made it clear that he embraces it.
“The pressure surrounding the Dodgers is a privilege. As an athlete, this is what you want to be and you want to have an expectation to win,” Skubal said to Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez.
“I have those same expectations as a player and in my shoes, I think just keeping the game the game, going out there and competing and doing what I can to put my team in a position to win is important.”
Despite a good performance on the mound against the Brewers in Game 1 of the NLCS, Skubal was credited with the loss; his next starting opportunity is Game 5, but he and his teammates currently trail two games to none.
It Was Not Easy For The Tigers To Lose Tarik Skubal
Shortly after the trade of Skubal to the Dodgers was completed, Tigers manager A.J. Hinch admitted that it wasn’t easy despite having been preparing for that potential outcome.
“We’ve been bracing for something like this to happen,” Hinch said of the trade via the Detroit News. “Even though we’ve been talking about it for a couple of months, it’s still tough when it becomes a reality. But these guys are pretty resilient.”
“It’s been incredible to watch this guy rise to the top of the sport,” Hinch said. “He carried us a lot and I am forever grateful that our paths crossed. And for the things he did for this organization and the two playoff teams. His presence, his work ethic, his example, his dominance, there’s just so much to go through. But I am very grateful I was able to manage him for the time I did.”

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES – Slumping Shohei Ohtani is set to bat sixth for the Los Angeles Dodgers against the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series on Wednesday night.
That's the lowest the left-handed hitting Ohtani has hit since joining the Dodgers three years ago on a $700 million, 10-year contract. Manager Dave Roberts said he wanted to sprinkle left- and right-handed hitters throughout the lineup against Milwaukee's left-handed starter Robert Gasser.
Recommended Videos
”Shohei’s all on board," Roberts said before the game. “Whatever it takes to win.”
The two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers trail 2-0 in the best-of-seven series.
Ohtani, the designated hitter, is typically atop the order, but Roberts has dropped him lower during a slump that has extended into the postseason. Ohtani has been struggling with left knee and right biceps issues for a few months, and said before the National League Division Series that he's not 100% healthy.
During his six years with the Los Angeles Angels, Ohtani started games batting sixth or lower 19 times, all during the 2020 season or earlier.
Ohtani is hitting .150 (3 for 20) over six postseason games while appearing visibly uncomfortable at the plate. He has seven strikeouts, three walks and one stolen base with no home runs, no RBIs and an OPS of .411.
He hasn’t homered since Aug. 18 at Colorado.
“I couldn’t imagine really kind of having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him,” teammate Mookie Betts said before the game. “Then having to come back and be present in this postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
Roberts said he saw a more focused Ohtani during off-day batting practice Tuesday.
“He was determined, and that’s an understatement,” the manager said. “He was here late last night working on his swing, out with the guys and talking about things on how we're going to beat these guys.”
Dodgers pitcher Tyler Glasnow, set to start Game 4 on Thursday, said Ohtani's demeanor doesn't deviate regardless of how well he's performing.
“I think most people put in that situation, you’d have a lot more emotional volatility, so it’s just impressive to see him just be a good dude always,” Glasnow said. “I don’t think he needs reassurance or anything. He’s confident in himself. It’s just business as usual and a lot of smiles and the same laugh.”
___

item.content:encoded:
The NLCS resumes at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday, with the Dodgers looking to embark on a comeback down 2-0 in the series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
The top three in the lineup remain the same, as Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Teoscar Hernández hit in the top three spots. The middle of the lineup received an adjustment that comes as little to no surprise with how Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith have hit in the postseason.
Kyle Tucker moves up to cleanup in the starting lineup, the highest spot in the order he's been placed in this October. After a rough regular season, Tucker has found his stride at the plate at the bottom of the lineup, slashing .300/.391/.500 with a home run and two RBI over six games. Tucker has faced Milwaukee's Game 3 starter Robert Gasser twice in his career, collecting three hits across six at-bats including a home run.
Andy Pages has also impressed at the plate this postseason, turning the page on what was a historically awful title run at the plate last year. The 2026 All-Star has five hits across 20 at-bats, with his highlights being his go-ahead, two-run single in Game 4 of the NLDS and for getting the Dodgers on the board against Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1 of the NLCS. Pages has gone hitless since his Game 1 RBI single, but he moves up to fifth in the lineup against Gasser, also the highest spot he's hit in the postseason this year.
The elephant in the room is Shohei Ohtani getting moved all the way down to sixth in the lineup. Ohtani was adamant about playing in Game 3, and Dave Roberts ultimately granted his wish.
"He's adamant he feels good enough to be in there. He's close to finding something with his swing. I feel great about it," manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday just before the Dodgers workout at Dodger Stadium. "He was very convicted that he is onto something mechanically. He was adamant that he can help us. He's well enough to help us win a baseball game. So that's all I needed to hear."
Try as he might to will his way into the lineup, Ohtani has been a detriment offensively since hitting his final regular season home run on Aug. 18 in Denver, and he's carried that funk over the team's six playoff games slashing just .150/.261/.150 with zero RBI. Ohtani had never hit as low as second in the lineup until Game 3 of the NLDS, and it's the first time Ohtani is hitting sixth in the lineup since Sept. 19, 2020 back when he was with the Angels.
Will Smith has also struggled mightily this October, and he slides all the way down to seventh in the starting lineup. Miguel Rojas gets the start at third base over Max Muncy against the left-hander Gasser, and Tommy Edman gets the start at second base, rounding things out in the lineup. Blake Snell makes his first start since getting the ball for Game 2 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves.

item.content:encoded:
Game 3 of the National League Championship Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium is scheduled to start at 5:00 p.m. PDT on Wednesday.
The Brewers won the first two games of the series on Sunday and Monday.
Milwaukee won the first game 2-1 and the second game 7-4.
Before Wednesday’s game, Mookie Betts dropped an honest quote on Shohei Ohtani, who has struggled significantly this postseason.
Dodgers Star Mookie Betts Makes Honest Shohei Ohtani Statement Amid Brewers Series
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts in the third inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images)
“I couldn’t imagine really having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him,” Betts said to reporters, including USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. “Then having to come back and be present in the postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
“He’s trying. It’s just really, really hard. It’s really hard to make these slight adjustments in this short amount of time. Like I said, it took me almost two years. I feel for him. I know he’s grinding, he’s working. So we’ll just see. We’ll see how he comes and prepares.”
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers walks back to the dugout after striking out in the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
“But I know he’s giving it his all. We can at least lay our heads on a pillow at night knowing that we’ve given it everything.”
This postseason, Ohtani has gone 3-for-20 with seven strikeouts and three walks. He is dealing with biceps and knee injuries.
Looking at NLCS Game 3 Between Dodgers and Brewers
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 11: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers hits a fly ball against the Milwaukee Brewers during the eighth inning in game one of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
The Dodgers considered benching Ohtani for Game 3, but ultimately placed him in the lineup.
Ohtani is batting sixth, a career low, as the DH today.
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers returns to the dugout after grounding out in the third inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
Here is the Dodgers’ lineup:
- Mookie Betts SS
- Freddie Freeman 1B
- Teoscar Hernandez LF
- Kyle Tucker RF
- Andy Pages CF
- Shohei Ohtani DH
- Will Smith C
- Miguel Rojas 3B
- Tommy Edman 2B
Left-hander Blake Snell will start for the Dodgers today. Southpaw Robert Gasser is slated to start for the Brewers.

item.title: [New York Post] Mookie Betts understands Shohei Ohtani’s playoff struggles: ‘It’s really, really hard’
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Mookie Betts understands what Shohei Ohtani is dealing with in this National League Championship Series. Betts knows what can happen to a once-dangerous swing when a hitter takes the field with physical limitations. Two years ago, Betts was struck by a 98 mph fastball and fractured his left hand. “It’s really, really hard,” Betts said. “It took me almost like two years before I was able to really kind of feel normal again and get those bad habits out.” Before he was placed on the injured list in
item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts understands what Shohei Ohtani is dealing with in this National League Championship Series.
Betts knows what can happen to a once-dangerous swing when a hitter takes the field with physical limitations.
Two years ago, Betts was struck by a 98 mph fastball and fractured his left hand.
“It’s really, really hard,” Betts said. “It took me almost like two years before I was able to really kind of feel normal again and get those bad habits out.”
Before he was placed on the injured list in September, Ohtani said he was experiencing discomfort in his right arm and left knee. Asked on Tuesday what was bothering Ohtani, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, “It’s everything.”
“When you’re hurt, you just want to play,” Betts said. “So you’ll make adjustments to the swing or to your body so you can play. Then you don’t want to hurt while you play, so you make the adjustments to where your body doesn’t feel it. Sometimes it’s to the detriment of who you are as a player, and you don’t really realize it.”
Betts imagined that navigating the situation would be more difficult for Ohtani because of his stature.
“I couldn’t imagine really kind of having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him. Then having to come back and be present in this postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
Ohtani is hitting .150 in the postseason.
“He’s trying,” Betts said. “It’s just really, really hard. It’s really hard to make these slight adjustments in this short amount of time. Like I said, it took me almost two years. I feel for him. I know he’s grinding, he’s working. So we’ll just see. We’ll see how he comes and prepares.
“But I know he’s giving it his all. We know he’s giving it his all. We can at least lay our heads on a pillow at night knowing that we’ve given it everything.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are set for a pivotal Game Three in their NLCS with the Milwaukee Brewers.
Milwaukee holds a 2-0 lead, and if the Dodgers want to advance to the World Series, they must win four of the next five games, which will certainly be a tall task.
However, the series has now shifted to LA, and the Dodgers have another ace in Blake Snell taking the ball on Wednesday evening.
Before the NLCS Game Three, the Dodgers revealed their lineup to try and muster runs off southpaw Robert Gasser, and Max Muncy is not featured in the group.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Issued Strong Anthony Volpe Take Amid Major Decision
Dodgers’ Max Muncy OUT of Game Three Batting Order
Likely due to the Brewers throwing a southpaw the Dodgers way in Game 3, Max Muncy is not featured in the batting order, but he will likely be used in a pinch-hit scenario if Milwaukee deploys a RHP at some in the game to face Miguel Rojas, who is IN at 3B in Muncy’s place.
@UnderdogMLB help break the news of the full Dodgers lineup for 10/14:
Dodgers 10/14: “M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF K. Tucker RF A. Pages CF S. Ohtani DH W. Smith C M. Rojas 3B T. Edman 2B B. Snell SP”
Other lineup notes include: Both Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith dropping in the order, Kyle Tucker getting the start at cleanup, and Teoscar Hernandez batting third.
Tommy Edman is also getting a start, while the Dodgers are relying on a strong start from Blake Snell.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are facing a must-win in Game Three of the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday evening.
The good news for the Dodgers is that the series is shifting back to Los Angeles. Blake Snell will get the start for LA on Wednesday evening, and he will oppose Robert Gasser.
Before the game started, the Dodgers announced their Game Three lineup, which featured a major Will Smith decision.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Blake Snell News Before Pivotal Brewers Game
Will Smith Dropped in Los Angeles Dodgers Batting Order
When the Dodgers Game Three lineup dropped on Wednesday afternoon, it came with a few surprises.
In two big developments, Will Smith and Shohei Ohtani have dropped in the batting order.
Here is the full group, per @UnderdogMLB:
Dodgers 10/14: “M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF K. Tucker RF A. Pages CF S. Ohtani DH W. Smith C M. Rojas 3B T. Edman 2B B. Snell SP”
The flip to Will Smith being demoted in the lineup is that Kyle Tucker has moved up several spots and will bat cleanup against the Brewers’ LHP Gasser.
Shohei Ohtani bats sixth, and Tommy Edman/Miguel Rojas are getting starts in the infield, while Max Muncy gets the pine.
More MLB on Heavy: Toronto Blue Jays Predicted to Poach Yankees All-Star for $80 Million
Taking a Quick Look at Will Smith’s 2026 Season
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – MAY 08: Will Smith #16 of the Los Angeles Dodgers during a 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves at Dodger Stadium on May 08, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
As did many of the Los Angeles Dodgers (at some point in 2026), Will Smith spent a good chunk of time on the Injured List with a neck issue.
He got a handful of starts down the stretch of the regular season, but he’s been really struggling at the plate in the MLB playoffs, and after moving him down for Game Two, manager Dave Roberts is now demoting him to the 7-spot in the lineup.
Perhaps it’s a wake-up call for Smith, but as the Dodgers search for the right lineup combination, having Smith (who is 1-for-20+) in the 3-hole just isn’t going to get things going.
It will be interesting to see if this decision pays off for Roberts and the rest of the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Issued Strong Anthony Volpe Take Amid Major Decision

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers' Muncy, Pages Named 2026 Gold Glove Finalists
item.dc:creator: Jordon Lawrenz
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to avoid being swept in the National League Championship Series, and that starts in Game 3, which takes place on Wednesday, the same day when the Gold Glove Award finalists were revealed. The likes of Mookie Betts, Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker, and even Yoshinobu Yamamoto weren't named finalists, but Andy Pages and Max Muncy were. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are looking to avoid being swept in the National League Championship Series, and that starts in Game 3, which takes place on Wednesday, the same day when the Gold Glove Award finalists were revealed.
The likes of Mookie Betts, Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker, and even Yoshinobu Yamamoto weren't named finalists, but Andy Pages and Max Muncy were.
Pages represents the Dodgers in center field while Muncy is their third base representative.
Both players have their work cut out for them, but even being named one of three NL finalists is a huge accomplishment for how grueling a 162-game season is.
Dodgers face stiff odds for Muncy to win
Muncy is officially a Gold Glove finalist for the second time in his career, but it seems like he's going to need to try again next year.
The three-time All-Star is matched up against Alex Bregman, one of the best defenders in all of baseball, and Javier Sanoja.
MLB.com made note that Muncy hasn't been a plus defender by fielding run value since 2021, and that's something that Bregman has been doing on a consistent basis.
Here in 2026, Bregman notched his seventh straight season of being an above-average defender, and the 2024 Gold Glove Award winner ended the year with +9 outs above average.
For reference, that was second among all third basemen. Sanoja has a case to be made with his +6 OAA, which is fourth in the NL, along with his +5 FRV, which was tied for fourth.
Sanoja won the Gold Glove Award last year as a utility player, but now is stuck at third base where both he and Muncy will likely fall to Bregman.
Pages is stuck against Pete Crow-Armstrong
Is there a worse person to be going up against than Pete Crow-Armstrong? The likely 2026 NL MVP had a defensive value worth +23 runs, which led the league.
PCA's OAA came in at +26, which is officially the highest by an outfielder in a single season this decade.
Pages sported a strong +13 FRV, which was the third most among qualified outfielders, but it was still nothing in comparison to Crow-Armstrong's +26.
Sure, Pages led the league with 14 outfield assists, but it seems like a foregone conclusion that PCA will be leaving with the hardware on Sunday, Nov. 1.
Michael Harris II was the third finalist. He put together a career year with his +14 OAA and +12 FRV.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers hope to punch back in the NLCS with a home win in Game 3 over the Milwaukee Brewers.
The Dodgers are down 0-2 in the series, but hope isn’t lost; this Dodgers team thrives when it’s backed into a corner. To turn things around, the offense needs to convert on scoring chances.
Dodgers’ Lineup vs. Brewers
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Kyle Tucker, RF
5. Andy Pages, CF
6. Shohei Ohtani, DH
7. Will Smith, C
8. Miguel Rojas, 3B
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
The Dodgers announced Tuesday that Shohei Ohtani will play despite his struggles and injuries. He will stay in the 6-hole, his lowest spot yet for the Dodgers.
The Brewers are rolling out lefty Robert Gasser, who possesses some matchup problems. Naturally, right-handers Teoscar Hernandez and Andy Pages are moving up from their usual positions.
Will Smith, who has also struggled in the postseason, is moving down to his lowest spot in a while.
Other than shuffling players around, Roberts is sticking with the same group from Game 2, with the only exception being Miguel Rojas at third base while Max Muncy sits.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
Blake Snell takes the mound for the Dodgers in the biggest spot of his career. The team needs him to deliver a great outing to keep their three-peat hopes alive against a game Brewers team.
Snell has posted a 1.90 ERA over 42.2 innings this year. In the postseason, he hasn’t been as sharp in one start. He pitched just 3.2 innings in Game 2 of the NLDS, allowing one run but giving up five walks and three hits.
Against this crop of Brewers hitters, they’re hitting only 11-for-64 with a .172 average, a .274 OBP, and 29 strikeouts.
If Snell does well in this game, his legacy as a Dodger and pitcher will grow exponentially.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Dave Roberts Explains Controversial Pitching Decisions in NLCS Game 2 Loss
item.dc:creator: Gabe Smallson; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are two games away from being eliminated at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series. With right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto having pitched in Game 2, the current state of affairs is far from where fans expected the Dodgers to be as the series heads back to LA. The 2025 World Series MVP lasted just 2.2 innings on Monday in an uncharacteristic one-strikeout performance, but there was still tons of baseball to be played after his exit. Aft
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are two games away from being eliminated at the hands of the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series.
With right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto having pitched in Game 2, the current state of affairs is far from where fans expected the Dodgers to be as the series heads back to LA. The 2025 World Series MVP lasted just 2.2 innings on Monday in an uncharacteristic one-strikeout performance, but there was still tons of baseball to be played after his exit.
After left-hander Alex Vesia finished off the third inning with four pitches, one of last year's October standouts in Roki Sasaki trotted out to the mound to face the Brewers in the fourth.
Sasaki's October success last season, especially in multi-inning spots, is partially why manager Dave Roberts was in a position to explain himself for only having Sasaki out to throw one frame.
The man who opened up the bottom of the fifth inning for LA, southpaw Kris Bubic, recorded just two outs on 22 pitches, one of which was turned into a solo home run for Brewers catcher William Contreras to tie the game.
Despite Sasaki's resume, Roberts went with the left-hander, but revealed he was looking for far more than two outs from the former All-Star.
"To me, you're trying to cover six-plus innings," Roberts said. "For me, I felt Bubic had four out of five left-handed hitters, and that's a perfect spot for him. I knew they weren't going to for him, and you got Roki for an inning, and then you still have a guy — in my opinion, you've got a great spot for Bubic. Tries to go with the fastball up to Contreras and then hits a homer.
"That's a decision I made, and we just didn't — again, that's his lane to be able to go out there and throw up a zero."
After Bubic walked a batter to leave a man on first and second, Brock Stewart came in to end the inning. Instead of a fresh arm coming in for the bottom of the sixth, Stewart remained in the game. Three batters later, Contreras was back up to bat with a tie game, two on and one out.
Contreras hit the first pitch he saw 76.9 mph into the outfield grass to give his team the lead and Stewart was removed from the contest. Tanner Scott entered the game after him and promptly struck out the next two batters to get out of the inning.
Roberts was asked about why Stewart was in instead of Scott entering against an already hot Contreras.
"It just felt like trying to put Contreras on the ground," Roberts said. "Contreras didn't hit the ball hard. He flared it out to left field, drove in a run, and that's what they do."
Roberts continued to point out the differences between the kind of at-bats that the Brewers' brand is a byproduct of.
"I think for me just in total they saw a ton more pitches than we did," Roberts said. "They had much better at-bats than we did across the board top to bottom, and then they put the ball in play, created havoc, and that's what they do, and we didn't do that.
"That's the difference in the game. I think that there's certainly a lot to unpack, but they did what needed to do tonight."

Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Andy Pages and Max Muncy Named Gold Glove Finalists for 2026
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — Max Muncy and Andy Pages have given Dodgers fans something to celebrate on the defensive side of the ball. Both are among the Gold Glove finalists announced so far, recognition that puts their gloves in the spotlight while Los Angeles fights to keep its postseason run going. Muncy is a National League finalist at third base alongside Alex Bregman of the Cubs and Javier Sanoja of the Marlins. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Max Muncy and Andy Pages have given Dodgers fans something to celebrate on the defensive side of the ball. Both are among the Gold Glove finalists announced so far, recognition that puts their gloves in the spotlight while Los Angeles fights to keep its postseason run going.
Muncy is a National League finalist at third base alongside Alex Bregman of the Cubs and Javier Sanoja of the Marlins. For a player whose home runs and walks drive so much of the talk about his value, being recognized for his defense is a welcome addition.
Third base offers little time to react and plenty of chances to look bad. A hard grounder, a slow roller or a difficult throw across the diamond can test a defender in very different ways. Muncy’s place among the finalists deserves some applause from a fan base that has spent plenty of time discussing his work at the hot corner. Max has put a lot of effort into improving his defense, and this nod shows that folks around the league have noticed.
Pages joins Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs and Michael Harris II of the Braves among the National League center-field finalists. That is a tough field, and making the final three gives the Dodgers another reason to feel good about their young outfielder.
Center field carries a great deal of responsibility. The Dodgers need Pages to cover ground, make sound choices and finish plays, particularly in tight games when an extra out can mean everything. His nomination brings attention to the part of his job that can get lost amid discussions of his power and production at the plate.
No Mookie or Tuck This Year
The name many Dodgers fans expected to see elsewhere on the list was Mookie Betts. He was a Gold Glove finalist last year after his first full season at shortstop, a reward for the work he put into taking on one of baseball’s hardest positions. This year, the National League shortstop finalists are Geraldo Perdomo of the Diamondbacks, Dansby Swanson of the Cubs and Masyn Winn of the Cardinals. Betts missed the cut.
That omission will raise eyebrows in Los Angeles. Last year’s recognition made it reasonable to hope Betts would remain in the award conversation. The competition at shortstop is strong, but seeing the final three without him still feels like a notable snub from the Dodgers’ side.
Kyle Tucker’s absence is another surprise. Tucker won the American League Gold Glove in right field with Houston in 2022, so he has an established record of earning recognition for his glove. This year’s NL right-field finalists are Carson Benge of the Mets, Corbin Carroll of the Diamondbacks and Seiya Suzuki of the Cubs.
Past honors do not guarantee another nomination. Still, Betts and Tucker are familiar names in discussions of good defense, and their omissions give Dodgers fans plenty to debate.
Muncy and Pages deserve their moment, though. On a team whose biggest swings often make the headlines, recognition for the work done with a glove is worth celebrating. The Dodgers will need that work tonight, too, with outs to secure and a series to turn around.

A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
[Publicidad]
El astro japonés, Shohei Ohtani, sigue con la pólvora mojada en esta Postemporada de la Major League Baseball (MLB), pero desde los controles de Los Ángeles Dodgers ha recibido un espaldarazo.
Dave Roberts, mánager de la novena angelina, aseguró que el nipón seguirá en el Line up de los Dodgers, para el Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato, frente los Milwaukee Brewers.
Hoy, Los Ángeles reciben el primero de la serie en Dodger Stadium y se había rumorado que Ohtani podría salir del rol de bateador designado tras su pobre bateo en los Playoffs.
“Estaba muy convencido de que está logrando algo mecánicamente (con su swing). Insistió en que puede ayudarnos. Está lo suficientemente bien como para ayudarnos a ganar un juego de beisbol, así que eso es todo lo que necesitaba escuchar. Tiene todo nuestro apoyo”, dijo Roberts en conferencia de prensa.
Shohei Ohtani está bateando para .150 (3 de 20) en seis juegos de postemporada. Tiene siete ponches, tres bases por bolas y una base robada, sin jonrones, sin carreras impulsadas y un OPS de .411.
“Los síntomas han disminuido mucho. Los síntomas no deberían ser la razón por la que no puedo batear, y aunque las lesiones ocurran por accidente, asumo toda la responsabilidad”, agregó por su parte el pelotero japonés.
[Publicidad]
Blake Snell busca recuperarse con los Dodgers en el Juego 3
El dos veces ganador del Premio Cy Young, Blake Snell, abrirá por Los Ángeles contra Robert Gasser de los Cerveceros en un duelo de zurdos el miércoles.
Los Dodgers buscarán obtener considerablemente más entradas de Snell que en su última apertura el 4 de octubre.
Trabajó 3 2/3 entradas, permitiendo una carrera, tres hits, otorgando cinco bases por bolas y ponchando a cinco, en una derrota 3-2 en el Juego 2 de la serie divisional contra Atlanta. No habló con los medios después y ha mantenido un perfil bajo desde entonces.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Breaking Down Shohei Ohtani’s Hitting Issues—and How He Could Fix Them
item.dc:creator: Tom Verducci
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Shohei Ohtani will be in the lineup for the Dodgers in a virtual must-win Wednesday in Game 3 of the National League championship series. He convinced manager Dave Roberts on Tuesday he is a full go. But it’s obvious Ohtani is not fully healthy and must make quick tweaks to have a chance at being productive. “As of now with the swing, it's a daily process of trying different things, different feel on a daily basis,” Ohtani said. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Shohei Ohtani will be in the lineup for the Dodgers in a virtual must-win Wednesday in Game 3 of the National League championship series. He convinced manager Dave Roberts on Tuesday he is a full go. But it’s obvious Ohtani is not fully healthy and must make quick tweaks to have a chance at being productive.
“As of now with the swing, it's a daily process of trying different things, different feel on a daily basis,” Ohtani said.
What’s wrong with Ohtani? His lower half is collapsing, leading to too much head movement. Of the injuries to his neck, right biceps and left knee, the one to his knee is causing him to collapse his lower half, which triggers a breakdown in his kinetic chain, especially too much head movement.
You can see a video breakdown of his problems above. But you can see an abbreviated version below in these stills. Both swings are against left-handed mid-zone sinkers. The one on the left is a home run from June 6 and the one on the right is a pop-up to third base in NLCS Game 2.
As his lower half collapses on the right, Ohtani can’t get to the firm front side you see on the left when he was healthy, a key to generating power. Now his back leg and foot are sliding behind him (arrow) instead of remaining in line with his front foot.
With the back foot behind him and an unstable lower half, Ohtani loses his proper spine angle. Instead of rotating around his core, the more severe spine angle pushes his head farther from his center of mass. He loses his firm front side and his head moves too much—sapping him of power.
The Brewers can see all this. They are attacking him. They are not prioritizing matchup lefties against him and they are absolutely pounding him with fastballs:
Brewers Fastballs (Not Including Cutters) vs. Ohtani
| Time Period | Usage | BA |
|---|---|---|
| Regular Season | 48.9% | .400 |
| NLCS | 75.0% | .000 |
This compromised version of Ohtani is nothing new. He has not pulled an extra-base hit since Aug. 25. He has not hit a home run since Aug. 18. Look at how injuries have depleted Ohtani since then:
| Ohtani Splits | Games | HR | BA | SLG | Exit Velocity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Through Aug. 18 | 121 | 30 | .294 | .558 | 93.5 |
| Since | 24 | 0 | .156 | .200 | 91.1 |
The most glaring issues are he cannot pull the ball, and he is unable to get to above-average velocity. Since Aug. 19, Ohtani has faced 136 pitches with at least 95-mph velocity, and has just one hit and a .036 batting average to show for it.
Those problems are related to too much head movement, which is caused by an unstable base. His remedy for Game 3 likely will be to prioritize keeping his head still, which may involve less lower-half movement and a more controlled swing.
“The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit, and even if the injuries happen by accident, I take full responsibility,” he said. “I take that as an opportunity for me to just take full responsibility for it. Today it's going to be another process for me to tinker and try new things.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts admitted after Game 2 that the thought of sitting Ohtani in Game 3 was a possibility. But Roberts met with Ohtani on Tuesday, along with president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, general manager Brandon Gomes and Ohtani’s interpreter. Ohtani convinced the room he is ready and convicted. When the best player on the planet tells you he’s good to go, you put him in the lineup. It’s that simple.
All eyes are on Ohtani ahead of Wednesday’s Game 3. Can he find a swing adjustment to have better at-bats? Can he catch up to a fastball? Can the Dodgers win the NLCS without getting slug from Ohtani? They’re running out of time to find out.
Tom Verducci is a senior writer for Sports Illustrated who has covered Major League Baseball since 1981. He also serves as an analyst for FOX Sports and the MLB Network; is a New York Times best-selling author; and cohosts The Book of Joe podcast with Joe Maddon. A five-time Emmy Award winner across three categories (studio analyst, reporter, short form writing) and nominated in a fourth (game analyst), he is a three-time National Sportswriter of the Year winner, two-time National Magazine Award finalist, and a Penn State Distinguished Alumnus Award recipient. Verducci is a member of the National Sports Media Hall of Fame, Baseball Writers Association of America (including past New York chapter chairman) and a Baseball Hall of Fame voter since 1993. He also is the only writer to be a game analyst for World Series telecasts. He lives in New Jersey with his wife, with whom he has two children.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call apparently isn’t a fan of the new Novig advertising campaign featuring actress Sydney Sweeney.
Call tagged MLB in a post to his X account Wednesday, Oct. 14, saying “Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB? My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this.”
One advertisement airing during the League Championship Series round — specifically, Tuesday’s ALCS game between the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays — fits the description: the “Just Sports” series of commercials in which Sweeney appears unclothed, promoting the sports prediction market platform.
Call isn’t the only sports figure who has complained about the commercials. Genevieve Albernaz, the wife of Baltimore Orioles manager Craig Albernaz, echoed Call’s sentiment on her own X account while watching the ALCS.
British sprinter Amy Hunt recently called out the ad campaign for demeaning female athletes. So did Olympic water polo silver medalist Tilly Kearns.
Who is Dodgers outfielder Alex Call?
Call, 32, did not make the Dodgers’ 26-man roster for the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers or NL Division Series against the Atlanta Braves. He batted .233 with a .349 on-base percentage in 88 regular-season games for the Dodgers in 2026.
Across five seasons with the Guardians, Washington Nationals and Dodgers, Call has played 403 games and slashed .241/.343/.360 with 22 home runs and 116 RBIs. He appeared in seven postseason games a year ago for the eventual World Series champions.

item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani insisting he can play through injury puts Dodgers in awkward spot originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are down 0-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, with their hopes of a three-peat in peril before they've even hosted a game in the championship series.
One of the big reasons for the team's struggles through the first two games is that Shohei Ohtani is clearly laboring through multiple injury issues. It got so bad that there was speculation he could be benched. But the Dodgers are sticking with Ohtani.
Andy McCullough of The Athletic highlighted Dave Roberts and the Dodgers' decision to stick with Ohtani through injury. While the Dodgers are on board with him playing, Ohtani is putting the team in an awkward spot that could come back to haunt them.
Shohei Ohtani puts Dodgers in awkward spot amid insistence he can play through injury
"He was adamant that he can help us," Dave Roberts told reporters. "He's well enough to help us win a baseball game, so that's all I needed to hear."
The Dodgers are sticking with Ohtani despite there being some clear issues with his health. But, as Ohtani told reporters: "The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit."
He's currently dealing with problems with his upper body and his knee. As Roberts said, "It's everything." The Dodgers superstar is dealing with a lot of injury issues right now.
But despite all of the injury issues he's dealing with and his clear struggles on the field in the NLCS, Ohtani is playing through it.
His insistence that he's good to go is putting the Dodgers in an awkward spot. Will they really bench Ohtani when he believes he's good to go?
Ohtani has become the face of the Dodgers' franchise and is arguably the face of baseball as a whole right now. Benching him in the middle of the NLCS is a massive decision for the Dodgers to make.
Based on his play so far, benching him might not be the worst decision. If he wasn't Ohtani and instead was an ordinary player, the Dodgers would likely not have let him play through injury as he has so far.
But because Ohtani insists he's good to go, the Dodgers are put in a bad spot, as benching Ohtani, down 0-2 in the NLCS, would be met with a ton of scrutiny even if it might be the best decision for the team.
Ohtani could prove the worrywarts wrong with a strong performance at home to salvage the Dodgers' NLCS chances, but if his struggles at the plate from Milwaukee continue, Ohtani might be one of the reasons why Los Angeles is eliminated this postseason.
This situation is a very tricky one for the Dodgers. While Ohtani isn't 100% and he's struggling at the plate, benching the $700M superstar is something that would be very difficult to do.

item.title: [Brewer Fanatic] A Different Kind of Challenge: How Can Brewers Beat Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow?
item.dc:creator: Jake McKibbin
item.description: Brewers Video Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto are the Dodgers' near-immortal October heroes. After most teams start a series with hurlers like that, there's a major step down in quality to the back half of their rotation. In Los Angeles's case, though, that step is much smaller. Here's how the Brewers can attack the other two-time Cy Young Award winner in the Dodgers rotation, and one of the most physically intimidating pitchers in baseball. Projected Game 3 Starter: Blake Snell The Brewers
item.content:encoded:
Brewers Video
Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto are the Dodgers' near-immortal October heroes. After most teams start a series with hurlers like that, there's a major step down in quality to the back half of their rotation. In Los Angeles's case, though, that step is much smaller. Here's how the Brewers can attack the other two-time Cy Young Award winner in the Dodgers rotation, and one of the most physically intimidating pitchers in baseball.
Projected Game 3 Starter: Blake Snell
The Brewers got a first-hand look at just how good Snell can be in 2025. He capitalized on a change in his pitch mix, throwing a heavy dose of in-zone changeups that completely befuddled Milwaukee in one of the best starts of his career: eight innings, one hit, 10 strikeouts. But that isn't always the version of Snell that opponents see.
Snell is willing to nibble around the edges of the zone, making swing decisions in the shadow zone particularly important for Milwaukee against another high-release, left-handed pitcher with a devastating fastball and changeup. The difference is that Snell is much more comfortable giving up a walk than Skubal, and somehow even harder to square up when hitters do swing.
His start against the Braves showed both sides of that equation. Snell lasted just 3⅔ innings, walking five hitters and striking out five, but he allowed only one run. Three hits and five walks might suggest that Atlanta simply missed its opportunity, but there is a reason Snell can survive that kind of traffic. His fastball has elite ride, and when he works at the top of the zone, it's extremely difficult to get on top of. Add a wicked slider and curveball that blend beautifully with the fastball from his high release point, plus a quality changeup, and Snell's four-pitch mix is loaded with ways to beat a hitter.
This is the type of contact quality Snell has allowed this season:
Snell isn't overly concerned about the walks, because he trusts his ability to strand runners once they reach base. Especially in the tense environment of a playoff game, he can induce chase, generate swing-and-miss, and force weak contact when hitters finally do get the ball in the zone.
Even when he does throw strikes, Snell is difficult to hit. Fresh off the injured list, his fastball has gained roughly an inch of both ride and run compared with 2025. As a result, the one pitch that hitters had previously been able to barrel with some consistency has taken a step forward.
That makes this a waiting game for Milwaukee. Can the Brewers build enough pressure on Snell that he finally blinks before they do? Can they turn the walks and deep counts into hard contact when he eventually has to come into the zone? More importantly, can they force him to throw enough pitches that the Dodgers have to turn to their bullpen earlier than they'd like?
Atlanta managed to run Snell's pitch count up and get him out of the game, and white-knuckled their way to a win from there. Milwaukee may need a similar approach. They're unlikely to drop the hammer on Snell, and they'll need some batted-ball fortune when their opportunities arrive, but if they can make him work, accept the walks and punish the mistakes, they have a path to turning Snell's greatest strength, his willingness to live on the edges, into a weakness. Braves batters swung at just 34 of the 90 pitches Snell threw in the NLDS. To match that patience in last year's NLCS Game 1, the Brewers would have had to swing 10 fewer times. The key to beating Snell is those 10 fewer swings.
NLCS Game Four Starter: Tyler Glasnow
Tyler Glasnow works from one of the highest release points in baseball, pairing a high-velocity fastball with breaking balls that feature sharp, late movement. Like Snell, he's comfortable working outside the strike zone and using his secondary pitches to induce chases. His two breaking balls can fall off the table, making them difficult to touch—let alone hit hard.
Glasnow threw just 74 innings during the regular season, but posted a 0.95 WHIP and a 34% strikeout rate, a testament to how difficult he is to handle—particularly when he gets ahead in the count. There is, however, another dimension to the matchup. Glasnow can be vulnerable to the running game: opposing runners went 14-for-17 on stolen-base attempts against him in 2026, an 82% success rate. If the Brewers can get men on base, they may have opportunities to pile on pressure with their legs. The bigger question, of course, is how they get on in the first place.
Once again, the fastball could be the key. Glasnow's breaking balls have enough depth and movement to make consistent contact a challenge, particularly when hitters are forced to protect against them outside the strike zone. The Brewers will need to recognise those pitches early and avoid expanding the zone. The encouraging sign is that, unlike Yamamoto, Glasnow has shown a more conventional relationship between count leverage and pitch selection: as he falls behind, the likelihood of seeing a fastball increases.
Glasnow's outing against the Braves offered a glimpse of both his vulnerability and his ability to limit the damage. He struggled to locate his secondary pitches, walking five hitters, and threw his four-seam fastball in the strike zone roughly two-thirds of the time. The Braves managed just one run, however, illustrating how difficult it can be to capitalize on Glasnow's occasional command issues.
Even when Glasnow loses his feel for the secondaries, his four-seamer remains a formidable weapon. Released from a high arm slot, the pitch can play above the barrel, but it also cuts just enough to slide along the barrel. That helps him limit hard contact and keep the ball in the park, even when hitters know a fastball is coming. The offering has some similarities to the one the Brewers recently faced from Nick Pivetta, against whom they timed the fastball well. That being said, recognizing the pitch and actually squaring it up are two very different things.
The Brewers' best approach will be to make Glasnow work. Extending at-bats, laying off pitches outside the zone, and forcing him to find the strike zone with his secondary offerings could create opportunities to get runners aboard. From there, they can look to apply pressure on the bases and turn a difficult matchup into a more uncomfortable one. That fits their broader approach of building pressure and forcing mistakes, but Glasnow is unlikely to unravel simply because the Brewers make him work.
Ultimately, the Brewers will need to combine disciplined at-bats with timely hitting. Glasnow has the stuff to overpower even a patient lineup, and he would be an ace in most postseason rotations. The opportunity is there, but exploiting it will require the Brewers to turn the few openings he gives them into meaningful damage.

item.content:encoded:
With a 2-0 series lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series, the Milwaukee Brewers are hoping to win their third consecutive game over the reigning back-to-back World Series champions tonight. The Brewers, who will send Robert Gasser to the mound first in Game 3, are not taking wins in Games 1 and 2 of the NLCS for granted, knowing that the script can quickly be flipped with Dave Roberts' star-studded squad manning the opposing dugout.
That said, a 2-0 series lead in the League Championship Series is uncharted territory for the Brew Crew. The Brewers didn't possess a 2-0 lead in any of their previous four appearances in the LCS -- they were down 0-2 in the ALCS in 1982 before winning three straight, were even at 1-1 through two games in 2011 and 2018, and trailed 0-2 in their NLCS matchup with the Dodgers last year.
While Pat Murphy's squad clearly has the advantage, especially after defeating Los Angeles' dominant starting duo of Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and seeing manager Dave Roberts consider benching 4x MVP Shohei Ohtani, the Brewers remain locked in on winning the series as quickly as possible, knowing that doing so gives them the best chance of eventually securing the first World Series title in franchise history. Staying locked in required them to maintain their focus through yesterday's off-day, during which a trio of intriguing storylines emerged. Let's take a closer look at these three storylines and the implications they could have on the Brewers' path to their first World Series title.
Brandon Woodruff tosses 31-pitch bullpen on Tuesday, narrow chance of returning for potential World Series appearance remains
Perhaps the most exciting piece of news from Tuesday's mid-series off-day was the fact that veteran right-hander Brandon Woodruff kept his hopes of returning for a potential World Series appearance alive by throwing a 31-pitch bullpen. As reported by Curt Hogg of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, Woodruff, who reversed course on his decision to have season-ending shoulder surgery and is instead rehabbing his anterior capsule injury, said his stuff felt "pretty good" during his Tuesday afternoon bullpen session.
It remains a long shot that Woodruff returns to the Brewers' pitching staff for a potential World Series appearance, but the franchise legend is certainly doing whatever he can to pitch in the postseason for the first time since 2021. The Brewers not only have to consider whether or not they trust Woodruff to make his return to the mound in the World Series, but also if including him on a potential World Series roster is worth losing an arm who may be more prepared for the Fall Classic.
The best-case scenario is that Woodruff proves he's healthy enough to be included on a potential World Series roster and makes a significant impact on the Brewers' pitching staff down the stretch, but such a scenario feels highly unlikely. That improbability, however, is not stopping Big Woo from putting in the work to be ready for an appearance in the Fall Classic should the Brewers need him.
Dave Roberts says Shohei Ohtani will be in the Game 3 lineup after rumors of Dodgers potentially benching the 4x MVP
Shohei Ohtani has not been his usual dominant self through the Dodgers' first six games of the 2026 postseason. In part due to lingering knee and biceps injuries that caused the 4x MVP to miss time during the regular season, Ohtani has surprisingly been something of an afterthought during Los Angeles' 2026 playoff run.
As a result, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was reportedly seriously considering benching Ohtani for Game 3 of the NLCS. The consideration was in part due to the fact that rookie southpaw Robert Gasser, who pitches from a low arm slot, is a tough matchup for Ohtani. However, as noted in Roberts' press conference on Tuesday afternoon, Ohtani will be in the Dodgers' starting lineup for Game 3.
Said Roberts, as seen in the video above, Ohtani is "adamant he feels good enough to be in there, he's close to finding something with his swing. And I feel great about it." Whether or not that vote of confidence is genuine or not, Roberts needs his star hitter to find his groove quickly for the Dodgers to slow the momentum of the surging Brewers. Ohtani is just 3-for-20 in the postseason this year, and 1-for-7 with three strikeouts against the Brewers in the NLCS. Whether or not keeping him in the starting lineup is the right decision, Roberts is making the safe call by not removing the generational talent from his NLCS batting order in Game 3.
Dodgers' Game 3 starter Blake Snell comments on change in Brewers' mentality from last year's NLCS
A year ago, Cy Young southpaw Blake Snell took to the podium ahead of his NLCS start against the Brewers and commented on how he wasn't buying the "Average Joes" mindset that Pat Murphy was putting forward. While Snell's comments somewhat missed the mark, due to the fact that the broken financial landscape of baseball will always have the Brewers disadvantaged in comparison to the blank check-bearing Dodgers, it was out of respect that Snell said he didn't believe the Brewers were a bunch of "Average Joes."
This year, the Brewers have shed the underdog mentality, and Snell, who will start Game 3 tonight, has certainly noticed. Said Snell on Tuesday afternoon ahead, "Even the way that Pat [Murphy] talks, and how he talks to the team is way different than last year."
The Brewers are expecting to win this year, which is a stark shift from last year's mentality. No longer does Milwaukee need to do something out of the ordinary to topple the mighty Dodgers and advance to the World Series. Rather, they simply need to play brand of baseball, avoid unforced errors, and continue to prove their roster is capable of success in the postseason. Brewers fans know it, Pat Murphy's squad knows it, and Game 3 starter Blake Snell understands that this isn't the same team who was swept by the Dodgers last year.

【ロサンゼルス13日（日本時間14日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）がリーグ優勝決定シリーズ第3戦の前日会見に登壇。ポストシーズンで長打ゼロ、レギュラーシーズンから110打席本塁打から遠ざかるが、コンディションの懸念を再三否定した。この日、ロバーツ監督と対話の場を持ち、改めて「強い出場意思」を示したという。敵地で2連敗し、後がない状況で自ら退路を断つ形となった。
「大谷スタメン落ち」の報道が出た翌日、自ら会見に登壇し、口を開いた。大谷はこの日、ロバーツ監督と対話の場を持ち「強い出場意思」を伝えたという。ポストシーズン6試合で20打数3安打（打率・150）で長打ゼロ。敵地で2連敗を喫し、土俵際に追い込まれている。
「なぜと言われると実力だからというしかない。長い間そういう中でやっていると癖になってそういう動きになってしまう。毎日工夫しながらやっている」
左膝、右上腕、そして腰のコンディション懸念に「特にない」「大丈夫」と再三、否定。ただ、言葉通りに受け取ったとして結果が出ていない現状に「不運なけがだとしても、実力」と受け止めた。ロバーツ監督は「そもそも彼をベンチに下げるという話ではない。数日の休養を与え、立て直す時間をつくろうとした」とスタメン外ではなく、休養が選択肢にあったと明かした。
110打席本塁打から遠ざかっている大谷。直近18試合で長打1本という現状に「ポイントの問題だと思う。メジャーでプレーする選手で長打を打てないということはない。それは体の状態ではなくて、どちらかというとタイミングとポイントだと思う」とこの点においても体調を言い訳にせず、自身の技術に焦点を当てた。
大谷の状態を直接確認したロバーツ監督は「彼には強い出場意思がある。打撃でも何かをつかみかけている。試合に出て、チームの勝利、そして世界一に貢献したいと思っている」と思いをくみ取った。そして、大谷も「信じてくれる人のために頑張りたいと思う」と苦境に立つ中で必死に前を向く。3連覇の夢が途絶えかけてる今、真価が問われている。

item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts, mánager de la franquicia angelina, aseguró que el pelotero japonés seguirá liderando la ofensiva en el Juego 3.
Respaldo total para Shohei Ohtani. Ese fue el contundente mensaje del mánager de Los Angeles Dodgers, Dave Roberts, previo al decisivo Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional ante los Milwaukee Brewers. Sus declaraciones llegaron en medio de las dudas sobre la continuidad del japonés en el lineup titular, ante la posibilidad de que la estrella de los 700 millones de dólares fuera enviada a la banca tras una prolongada sequía de cuadrangulares. Ohtani no conecta un jonrón desde el 18 de agosto, cuando todavía peleaba por el Premio al Jugador Más Valioso.
El peor momento de Ohtani
Shohei Ohtani atraviesa uno de los momentos más complicados de su carrera en las Grandes Ligas, justo cuando los Dodgers más necesitan de su poder ofensivo. La franquicia angelina sueña con conquistar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva, pero la falta de producción de su principal estrella ha complicado el panorama en la Serie de Campeonato.
Los Dodgers están contra las cuerdas ante los Brewers y se encuentran dos derrotas de quedar eliminados en su propio estadio, el Dodger Stadium. En este escenario, el respaldo de Roberts cobra especial importancia, mientras Ohtani busca recuperar su mejor versión y ayudar a la franquicia angelina a mantenerse con vida en la lucha por el campeonato.
“Sí, obviamente, las cosas no han salido bien”, dijo Roberts. “Él no se siente del todo bien. Creo que, en mi caso, se trata de hablar con él mañana e intentar determinar qué es lo mejor para él y qué es lo mejor para nosotros. Sin duda, se ha ganado el derecho a tener esa conversación y la merece. Hablaré con él mañana”, comentó el martes por la tarde.
“En este momento, estamos escuchando a Shohei y lo estamos apoyando con todo lo que tenemos. Eso es todo”, comentó Roberts sobre la decisión del japonés de mantenerse como la alineación de bateo de los Dodgers durante la postemporada a pesar de su poca productividad ofensiva desde agosto.
Shohei Ohtani sufrió una lesión en la rodilla el pasado 3 de julio y posteriormente presentó problemas en el bíceps en septiembre. La primera le impidió regresar al montículo y lo dejó fuera de los planes de los Dodgers como lanzador para el mes de octubre. La segunda apenas le permitió recuperarse a tiempo para la postemporada, aunque hasta ahora no ha logrado mostrar su mejor versión ofensiva.
De cara al Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional en el Dodger Stadium, se espera que Dave Roberts mantenga al japonés en el lineup, con la posibilidad de ubicarlo como segundo o sexto bate en la alineación de los Dodgers.

item.title: [Yahoo] Comentario: Los Dodgers deberían haber excluido a Shohei Ohtani de la plantilla para la fase final

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers nunca se desvían de su plan de juego para la temporada regular: ganar los partidos suficientes para asegurarse una exención en la primera ronda de los playoffs y, de este modo, proporcionar a los jugadores todo el tiempo de descanso que necesitan durante el verano para estar en plena forma cuando llegue el otoño. No necesitan apresurar la vuelta de nadie de la lista de lesionados para hacerse con otro título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
Por desgracia para los Dodgers y su cada vez más precaria esperanza de lograr un triplete, no siguieron ese plan de juego con Shohei Ohtani. Los Dodgers le fallaron a Ohtani este verano, y ahora solo les queda cruzar los dedos y esperar lo mejor.
La esperanza, como se suele decir, no es una estrategia.
Los Dodgers deberían excluir a Ohtani de la plantilla para la postemporada.
No lo harán. Ni siquiera lo sacarán de la alineación del miércoles.
En medio de los titulares sobre cómo los Dodgers podrían haber dejado a Ohtani en el banquillo para el tercer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, el entrenador Dave Roberts explicó que la idea era más bien combinar el día libre del martes con un segundo día consecutivo de descanso.
"Nunca fue una decisión de dejarlo en el banquillo", afirmó Roberts.
Read more: Shohei Ohtani estará en la alineación de los Dodgers para el Juego 3 ante Cerveceros
Roberts estableció un paralelismo entre lo que podría haber ocurrido con Ohtani y lo que sí ocurrió con Freddie Freeman durante la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional de hace dos años, cuando los Dodgers proporcionaron lo que el entrenador denominó un "reinicio": un día libre para el equipo, seguido de un día de descanso para Freeman.
"Y acabó ganando el MVP en la Serie Mundial", señaló Roberts.
Freeman llevaba tres semanas jugando con un tobillo lesionado y, aun así, había sido más productivo aquel octubre de lo que lo ha sido Ohtani este. Ohtani lleva tres meses jugando con una lesión en la rodilla y en el bíceps, y los Dodgers ya han probado con descansos intermitentes.
Lo intentaron en septiembre, dos veces. Hicieron hincapié en su semana de descanso antes del inicio de los playoffs. Hablaron mucho de sus días libres antes del inicio de la NLCS.
Han fallado las cuatro veces. Ya basta.
Roberts afirmó que los Dodgers —no solo Ohtani, sino también el cuerpo técnico y el equipo de preparadores físicos— ven progresos. Es cierto, sin duda. Pero hemos oído palabras igualmente alentadoras tras cada uno de los periodos de descanso de Ohtani.
"Estamos escuchando a Shohei, y vamos a apoyarle a tope y a creer en él", dijo Roberts, "y eso es todo".
Ohtani afirmó el martes que sus síntomas han remitido desde que los Dodgers le incluyeron en la lista de lesionados, por el tiempo mínimo. De eso hace ya un mes.
El martes, afirmó que su enfoque puede alternar entre "centrarse en reducir los síntomas y eliminar el dolor y/o simplemente asegurarme de que me muevo bien en el swing".
Hasta ahora no hay pruebas de que esto pueda funcionar, y sí un conjunto de indicios, cada vez más inquietante, de que quizá no sea así.
Ohtani tiene un promedio de bateo de .150 en los playoffs, con tres hits en 20 turnos al bate. De los 39 jugadores con al menos 20 turnos al bate en esta postemporada antes del partido del martes, solo tres tienen un OPS inferior al de Ohtani, que es de .411.
Uno de ellos, el receptor de los Dodgers Will Smith, tiene un hit en 23 turnos al bate. Pero está golpeando la pelota con fuerza: en la NLCS, una bola salió a 102 mph, otra a 101, y todas las bolas salieron con más fuerza que la que Ohtani golpeó con más fuerza.
Esa velocidad de salida: 86 mph.
No ha bateado ninguna bola hacia la derecha en la serie, ni para conseguir un hit ni para ser eliminado.
A lo largo de su carrera en las Grandes Ligas, ha conectado un jonrón cada 14 turnos al bate.
No ha bateado un jonrón desde el 18 de agosto, un lapso de 107 turnos al bate. Ha impulsado una carrera desde entonces; los Dodgers lo colocaron de cuarto bate en el segundo partido.
Y, desde que bateó ese último jonrón, Ohtani tiene un promedio de bateo de .036 contra bolas rápidas lanzadas a 95 mph o más. La velocidad media de las bolas rápidas en esta postemporada: 96,2 mph, según el análisis detallado del analista Mike Petriello sobre todas las formas en que el swing de Ohtani falla.
¿Bolas con efecto? El relevista de los Brewers, JoJo Romero, le lanzó una baja y alejada en el segundo partido, y Ohtani perdió el control del bate al lanzarse para conectar.
Cuando Ohtani habló con los periodistas antes de que comenzaran los playoffs, dijo que quizá no supiera el alcance total de sus lesiones ni lo que tendría que hacer para recuperarse hasta después de la postemporada.
"No he podido comprender bien la causa principal de todo esto", dijo entonces. "Creo que ese proceso tendrá lugar durante la temporada baja, cuando tenga un poco más de tiempo para poder abordarlo. Pero, por ahora, es algo con lo que simplemente tendré que lidiar".
Los Dodgers no necesitaban a Ohtani para ganar la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. Necesitaban dejarlo de lado durante un periodo prolongado para maximizar sus posibilidades de ganar en octubre.
No lo consiguieron. Creían que unos pocos días de descanso les permitirían cuidar a Ohtani durante el resto de la temporada.
Un gran golpe en octubre, ¿y qué más da? Pregúntaselo a Kirk Gibson, quien cojeó hasta el bate y luego conectó uno de los jonrones más dramáticos de la historia de la Serie Mundial.
Esto es lo que los Dodgers deberían tener en cuenta: ese fue el único turno al bate que Gibson tuvo en aquella Serie Mundial de 1988.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers placed super-utility man Enrique Hernandez on the injured list Wednesday and will do the same with left fielderTeoscar Hernandez the next time they play Friday.
Enrique Hernandez suffered what Dodgers manager Dave Roberts described as a "significant tear" in his oblique earlier this week, an injury that will keep him out for several weeks, if not months. Teoscar Hernandez pulled up lame while running to first base in Wednesday's second inning and was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain, though the initial expectation is that his injury is not as serious.
"He tested well," Roberts said after the Dodgers' 4-1 win over the Colorado Rockies. "But we're going to get a scan tomorrow. Obviously it's an IL. There's just no timeline. But something like that obviously is going to be a few weeks at the minimum."
Enrique Hernandez spent the season's first two months building back up after offseason elbow surgery and suffered the oblique injury while taking batting practice before his season debut Monday. He picked up two hits that night, received treatment Tuesday, homered, then hit a fourth-inning double under significant pain in his left side and was later replaced on defense.
Cameras caught Roberts consoling a visibly shaken Enrique Hernandez in the dugout shortly thereafter.
"I feel pretty defeated right now," Hernandez told reporters after the game.
The Dodgers recalled infield prospect Alex Freeland to fill the vacant roster spot, starting him at second base for the series finale. Freeland will probably get most of the playing time there until Tommy Edman makes his expected return from offseason ankle surgery at some point in June, though Hyeseong Kim will draw starts at second base, too.
The hope is that Enrique Hernandez will at least return for the stretch run of the regular season so he can be a factor in the playoffs, the time of year in which he usually shines. Teoscar Hernandez's stay should be shorter, though it's nonetheless painful for the Dodgers, given his 1.018 OPS over the past 18 games.
"It's pretty frustrating for us," Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages said in Spanish. "We have the opportunity to see them work hard every day and prepare so that those things don't happen. But [injuries are] going to happen all the time."

item.title: [El Comercio de Colorado] Shohei Ohtani en alineación de Dodgers del Juego 3 ante Cerveceros - El Comercio de Colorado

item.content:encoded:
¿LOGRARÁN LA REMONTADA?
Por BETH HARRIS
Shohei Ohtani estará en la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles el miércoles para el Juego 3 de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional contra los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. El mánager Dave Roberts manifestó el martes que Ohtani bateará entre el segundo y sexto turno con los dos veces campeones defensores de la Serie Mundial que están 0-2 después de los dos primeros juegos de la serie al mejor de siete.“Estaba muy convencido de que está logrando algo mecánicamente (con su swing)”, dijo Roberts.
“Insistió en que puede ayudarnos. Está lo suficientemente bien como para ayudarnos a ganar un juego de béisbol, así que eso es todo lo que necesitaba escuchar”. Ohtani está bateando para .150 (3 de 20) en seis juegos de postemporada. Tiene siete ponches, tres bases por bolas y una base robada, sin jonrones, sin carreras impulsadas y un OPS de .411. No ha conectado un jonrón desde el 18 de agosto en Colorado.
Ohtani admitió antes de la serie divisional de la Liga Nacional contra Atlanta que no está 100% saludable debido a problemas en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda que le molestaron los últimos meses de la temporada regular. Se le ha visto visiblemente incómodo en el plato mientras abanica lanzamientos. “Los síntomas han disminuido mucho”, dijo Ohtani el martes a través de un traductor.
El jugador hizo una aparición no programada en la sala de entrevistas en el día libre. “Los síntomas no deberían ser la razón por la que no puedo batear, y aunque las lesiones ocurran por accidente, asumo toda la responsabilidad”. Roberts habló con Ohtani antes de que el equipo entrenara en el Dodger Stadium, donde Ohtani tomó práctica de bateo en el terreno, algo que rara vez hace durante la temporada regular.
Señaló que no se trataba de sentar a la superestrella japonesa, sino de ofrecerle descanso, similar a lo que ocurrió con Freddie Freeman durante la postemporada en 2024. Freeman tenía un esguince de tobillo y una contusión ósea , se tomó tres días libres que abarcaron la serie divisional y Serie de Campeonato antes de terminar ganando los honores de Jugador Más Valioso de la Serie Mundial.
“A lo largo de esta larga temporada, en realidad sólo hay un corto periodo de tiempo en el que mi mecánica está completamente en sincronía”, dijo Ohtani. “Así que en realidad es como ir y venir, encontrar las partes correctas del swing y manejar simplemente las diferentes partes del swing. Es un proceso constante y continuo que va en la dirección correcta”.
Ohtani lideró a los Dodgers a una barrida de cuatro juegos sobre Milwaukee en la SCLN del año pasado, cuando los Cerveceros batearon un mísero .118 contra el pitcheo de Los Ángeles. Se fue de 5 de 14 (.357) con tres jonrones, cuatro bases por bolas y cinco ponches como Jugador Más Valioso de la SCLN — los tres jonrones llegaron en un memorable Juego 4 que aseguró la serie, en el que también ponchó a 10 como lanzador. Tuvo un OPS de 1.643 y un porcentaje de slugging de 1.143.
Snell busca recuperarse con los Dodgers en el Juego 3
El dos veces ganador del Premio Cy Young Blake Snell abrirá por Los Ángeles contra Robert Gasser de los Cerveceros en un duelo de zurdos el miércoles. Los Dodgers buscarán obtener considerablemente más entradas de Snell que en su última apertura el 4 de octubre. Trabajó 3 2/3 entradas, permitiendo una carrera, tres hits, otorgando cinco bases por bolas y ponchando a cinco, en una derrota 3-2 en el Juego 2 de la serie divisional contra Atlanta.
No habló con los medios después y ha mantenido un perfil bajo desde entonces.
“Simplemente mucho tiempo hablando conmigo mismo, averiguando a dónde necesito llegar, dónde estoy”, dijo. “Viendo dos juegos contra Milwaukee, simplemente como planeando el juego, viendo qué puedo exponer, qué están haciendo realmente bien. Sólo tratando de descifrarlos”.
Mitchell de vuelta en casa
El jardinero central de los Cerveceros Garrett Mitchell regresa para jugar en creció pues creció en el Condado de Orange como aficionado de los Angelinos de Los Ángeles. Su familia tenía abonos en el jardín izquierdo. Fue a la preparatoria con el hijo de la estrella de los Angelinos Garret Anderson.
“Pude tener algunas buenas conversaciones con él, dar algunos viajes al pasado y hablar de recuerdos”, dijo Mitchell. “Yo también era campocorto cuando era niño. Así que disfrutaba ver a David Eckstein y Adam Kennedy, y también tengo una relación personal con Adam Kennedy”.

item.dc:creator: José Moreno
item.description: Los Ángeles Dodgers se juegan buena parte de sus aspiraciones en la postemporada este miércoles, cuando reciban a los Milwaukee Brewers en el tercer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, por esa razón el equipo angelino contará con Shohei Ohtani en busca de una reacción que lo mantenga en la pelea por el boleto a la Serie Mundial. Tampa Bay vence a Cleveland e iguala la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó que el astro japonés estará en el li
item.content:encoded:
Los Ángeles Dodgers se juegan buena parte de sus aspiraciones en la postemporada este miércoles, cuando reciban a los Milwaukee Brewers en el tercer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, por esa razón el equipo angelino contará con Shohei Ohtani en busca de una reacción que lo mantenga en la pelea por el boleto a la Serie Mundial.
Tampa Bay vence a Cleveland e iguala la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana
El mánager Dave Roberts confirmó que el astro japonés estará en el lineup para el encuentro en el Dodger Stadium, aunque todavía podía ocupar distintos puestos en el orden al bate, entre el segundo y el sexto turno.
Ohtani busca despertar en el momento más importante
El rendimiento de Ohtani en esta postemporada está lejos de sus mejores números: registra tres imparables en 20 turnos, para un promedio de .150, además de siete ponches y ninguna carrera impulsada.
A sus problemas ofensivos se suman las molestias en el bíceps derecho y la rodilla izquierda, que lo han acompañado durante los últimos meses. Sin embargo, Ohtani considera que puede ayudar al equipo y aseguró que sus síntomas han disminuido.
Dodgers, obligados a reaccionar ante Milwaukee
Los Brewers aprovecharon su localía para ganar los dos primeros encuentros y colocarse a dos triunfos de avanzar a la Serie Mundial. Para los Dodgers, actuales bicampeones, perder el tercer juego significaría quedar abajo 0-3 en una serie al mejor de siete, un escenario que los dejaría al borde de la eliminación.
El tercer partido se disputará este miércoles en Los Ángeles, donde los Dodgers buscarán apoyarse en su afición y en el regreso de Ohtani al lineup para cambiar la dinámica de la eliminatoria.
Milwaukee, por su parte, intentará mantener el control y acercarse a la clasificación, mientras la estrella japonesa tendrá una nueva oportunidad de marcar la diferencia cuando más lo necesita su equipo.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Yankees Trade Pitch Sacrifices No. 1 Prospect, Lands Ex-Red Sox MVP Mookie Betts
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Vankin
item.description: The New York Yankees exited the playoffs in the American League Division Series for the second year in a row, meaning that they have now gone 17 straight years without a World Series championship.
