item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have announced their roster for the 2026 National League Championship Series, and it includes the organization's top prospect.
Outfielder Josue De Paula, MLB Pipeline's No. 4 overall prospect for 2026, is on the Dodgers' 26-man roster for the NLCS. The 21-year-old made his MLB postseason debut in Los Angeles' 3-1 National League Division Series win over the Atlanta Braves, appearing as a pinch hitter in two games.
While De Paula had a couple of at-bats in the NLDS, he could play a larger role in the Dodgers' best-of-seven matchup with the Milwaukee Brewers. But even if he doesn't, the top prospect's presence on the NLCS roster still reflects the organization's confidence in the young outfielder.
What kind of impact can Josue De Paula have on the NLCS?
So far in the 2026 MLB playoffs, De Paula popped out to third base to end Game 2 of the NLDS and drew a walk in Game 4. The 21-year-old displayed his ability to get on base during his first stint in the majors, walking 11 times in his first 11 games with the Dodgers. That's at least part of the reason why the young prospect is on Los Angeles' postseason roster. In a late-game situation where the Dodgers need to get a runner on base, the 6-foot-3 outfielder could create a scoring opportunity on his own.
Los Angeles mostly used De Paula as a designated hitter in the majors, but that's obviously two-way star Shohei Ohtani's spot in the lineup. The four-time MVP has struggled in the postseason this year, though, going 2-for-13 with no extra-base hits in the NLDS. Ohtani dealt with multiple injuries during the regular season, which is what led to De Paula's first promotion to the big leagues. If the six-time All-Star misses any time in the postseason, the Dodgers' top prospect could be a natural candidate to earn a start at designated hitter.
Regardless of what role he plays in the rest of the playoffs, it wouldn't be surprising to see De Paula take a couple of big at-bats in the NLCS. The Brewers have tough right-handers like Abner Uribe and Trevor Megill in their bullpen. That could set the stage for the lefty-swinging slugger to pinch-hit in the clutch.
Justin Binkowski is a lifelong baseball fan returning to cover the sport he loves after spending nearly a decade writing about video games. Before his time as managing editor at Dot Esports, Binkowski attended King's College in Wilkes-Barre, PA, where he was also a relief pitcher on the school's baseball team. While in college, Binkowski was a media relations intern for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders during the 2014 season.

item.content:encoded:
grandes ligas
Dodgers mantienen a Miguel Rojas en su roster de la Serie de Campeonato
Los Cerveceros mantuvieron el mismo grupo de 26 jugadores que tuvieron para su serie divisional de la Liga Nacional contra San Diego.
El venezolano Miguel Rojas fue incluido en el roster de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, después de haber estado fuera por dolor en la parte baja de la espalda.
El zurdo Justin Wrobleski también forma parte del roster de los Dodgers para el duelo ante Milwaukee. Los Cerveceros mantuvieron el mismo grupo de 26 jugadores que tuvieron para su serie divisional de la Liga Nacional contra San Diego.
El Juego 1 de la NLCS se disputa la noche del domingo.
A Rojas le realizaron pruebas después de que salió durante la victoria 3-1 de los Dodgers en Atlanta en el Juego 3 de la serie divisional de la Liga Nacional. Las imágenes mostraron en su mayoría problemas previos de espalda.
El infielder veterano entrenó con Los Ángeles el sábado en el American Family Field, y el mánager Dave Roberts indicó que Rojas probablemente formaría parte del roster de la NLCS.
El jugador de 37 años conectó el jonrón del empate en la novena entrada del Juego 7 de la Serie Mundial el año pasado en Toronto, para ayudar a los Dodgers a ganar su segundo campeonato consecutivo. Ha manifestado que se inclina por retirarse al final de la temporada.
La incorporación de Wrobleski le da a los Dodgers 13 lanzadores en su roster de la NLCS, después de que llevaron 12 para su serie contra los Bravos. Wrobleski, de 26 años, tuvo marca de 12-5 con efectividad de 3,66 en 22 aperturas y seis apariciones como relevista este año, y fue seleccionado por primera vez al equipo de estrellas de la Liga Nacional.
El infielder Hyeseong Kim quedó fuera del roster de los Dodgers para la NLCS. Participó en un juego contra Atlanta como reemplazo defensivo.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Dodgers Reveal New Shohei Ohtani Approach Amid Postseason Struggles
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are tempering expectations for superstar Shohei Ohtani as he struggles to make much of an impact at the plate.
It is no mystery that Ohtani is dealing with injuries all over his body, with his neck, right arm, and left knee all causing some discomfort.
Why Ohtani will continue to play every day
However, Ohtani is still set to play every NLCS game and will likely play the rest of the postseason for the Dodgers.
He went 2-for-13 in the NLDS with two walks, putting together some quality at-bats and seemingly getting more comfortable as time went on, but nowhere near the feared slugger he is known as.
Still, manager Dave Roberts will ride it out with Ohtani.
“Outside of (Game 3 starter Chris) Sale, I thought he did a good job of controlling the zone. I saw some better swings,” Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
“There’s nothing right now I’m going to hang my hat on outside of, I just believe in the person and the talent.
“I do think that getting a couple days out of a game environment to kind of work on his swing, rest the body, rest the mind is a benefit. I’m just never going to count Shohei out.”
How will the Dodgers use Ohtani?
According to Roberts, Ohtani will hit somewhere from 2-5 in the batting order, depending on how he looks during workouts and in his baseball activities.
Roberts made the bold call to move Ohtani down the batting order in Game 3 of the NLDS against Chris Sale, hitting him fifth, but only bumped him up to fourth in Game 4.
The good news for the Dodgers is that Ohtani has said rest is the best medicine for his current injuries, and the team has not played since Thursday.
He will have some time off his feet, and even if he is compromised, Roberts thinks the Brewers will respect Ohtani enough to give him opportunities to walk, and the onus is on the Japanese star to punish any aggressiveness from the pitching staff.
“If he’s in the batter’s box, he’s still a threat,” Roberts said Saturday to Dodgers Nation and other media. “He swung the bat well against these guys last postseason.
“Their memories — those pitchers, their memories are long. Now it’s just up to Shohei to understand that and control the strike zone. They’re just not going to give in to him regardless of how he might be swinging the bat over the last couple months, in my opinion.”
The Dodgers saw that impact in the NLDS when Ohtani drew a five-pitch walk in Game 4, stole a base, forced an errant throw, and later scored.
At the very least, LA will be hoping for more moments like that, with any hitting production being gravy.

item.content:encoded:
Según el mánager Dave Roberts, el de Los Teques mejoró notablemente luego de una infiltración de cortisona en la zona lumbar
Miguel Rojas está listo para la serie de campeonato con Dodgers.-Miguel Rojas apunta a ser titular en la Serie de Campeonato tras superar molestias físicas sufridas en los últimos días y que lo apartaron del duelo ante Bravos de Atlanta la semana pasada.
El infielder venezolano Miguel Rojas tuvo que abandonar el tercer compromiso de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional a causa de una dolencia lumbar, lo que también le impidió estar en el cuarto choque. Sin embargo, el estratega Dave Roberts confirmó ante los medios de comunicación que confía en incluir al experimentado jugador en el roster para la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, luego de que una infiltración de cortisona aliviara favorablemente el malestar en la zona.
Lea también: Reactivan Pdval para atender a 3.500 familias en Puerto La Cruz
Según lo indicado por el mánager todavía no tiene claro si el oriundo de Los Teques pueda estar de titular en el duelo frente a Milwaukee de este domingo. Pero si que pueda ser utilizado como un bateador emergente determinante desde la banca ante los lanzadores zurdos.
Conviene recordar que Rojas se consolidó como una figura clave en el séptimo partido de la Serie Mundial del año pasado, cuando empató las acciones de forma agónica mediante un jonrón en la novena entrada ante el cerrador de los Blue Jays, Jeff Hoffman. El veterano aporta un recorrido invaluable a la plantilla angelina al contar con dos anillos de campeón y 23 compromisos de experiencia en fases decisivas de octubre.
EO//Con información de: Líder

item.content:encoded:
- Shohei Ohtani, que acabó con de 13 al bate en la NLDS, realizó una sesión de prácticas de bateo en un intento por recuperar su swing antes del primer partido de la NLCS de los Dodgers contra los Cerveceros.
- El entrenador Dave Roberts sigue confiando en que Ohtani pueda salir de su bache, pero este se enfrentará a una dura prueba contra el as de los Cerveceros, Jacob Misiorowski.
MILWAUKEE — Shohei Ohtani lanzó con fuerza una bola que llegó hasta la segunda grada del campo central-derecho. A continuación, lanzó otra, esta vez un poco más cerca de la imponente pantalla de vídeo que se alza sobre el American Family Field y en la que se veía el enorme logotipo “2026 NLCS”.
«Ha sido un buen día de trabajo para él», afirmó el entrenador de bateo Aaron Bates tras el entrenamiento de los Dodgers del sábado. «Él y Bookie [Mookie Betts] habían estado hablando sobre el bateo estos últimos días. Fue idea suya batear en el campo. Nuevo campo, nuevo escenario, ese tipo de cosas».
Ohtani solo ha bateado en prácticas de bateo en un campo unas pocas veces esta temporada. Pero antes del primer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional contra los Milwaukee Brewers el domingo, realizó una sesión prolongada con la máquina de lanzamiento.
“Simplemente intenta no girar el barril demasiado pronto”, explicó Bates sobre en qué se ha centrado Ohtani desde el punto de vista mecánico. “Sentirse cómodo en la para que sienta que está en una buena posición para batear, pero sobre todo que la mano superior no gire demasiado pronto. Luego, mantener el movimiento hasta el final, lo que le ayuda a revertir el movimiento, mantiene bajo el nivel de esfuerzo y, obviamente, le permite mantener el contacto con la pelota durante más tiempo”.
Ohtani acabó con un balance de dos de 13 en la NLDS, registrando dos sencillos en los dos primeros partidos. El cuatro veces MVP intentará superar sus recientes dificultades cuando se enfrente al favorito al premio Cy Young, Jacob Misiorowski, en el primer partido.
Misiorowski ha subido el listón en su segunda temporada en las Grandes Ligas. Pero las dificultades de Ohtani le hicieron bajar a los puestos n.º 5 y 4 de la alineación de los Dodgers para los partidos 3 y 4, respectivamente, frente a los Atlanta Braves.
Sin embargo, la reciente racha negativa de Ohtani no va a cambiar la forma en que Misiorowski le lance.
“Todavía estamos en octubre”, afirmó el as de los Brewers. “Hay que seguir lanzándole como si fuera el mejor del mundo, confiar en tus lanzamientos, vencerle en su propio terreno y hacer tu trabajo”.
Ese historial es en lo que también se apoya el mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, ya que sigue pronosticando que Ohtani saldrá de su bache.
“En este momento no hay nada en lo que me vaya a basar, simplemente creo en la persona y en su talento”, declaró Roberts en una conferencia telefónica el viernes. “Creo que alejarse un par de días del ambiente de los partidos para trabajar un poco su swing, descansar el cuerpo y la mente es beneficioso. Nunca voy a descartar a Shohei”.
La mayor contribución de Ohtani en la NLDS no tuvo que ver con un swing. En su primer turno al bate del cuarto partido, aprovechó que Tyler Mahle le estaba tratando con cautela y consiguió una base por bolas tras cinco lanzamientos. A continuación, robó la segunda base y aprovechó un par de errores de los Braves para anotar.
“Aparte de [Chris] Sale, creo que hizo un buen trabajo controlando la zona”, dijo Roberts. “He visto algunos swings mejores”.
Pero los Dodgers también se mostraron optimistas mientras Ohtani estaba en la lista de lesionados, y de nuevo tras la semana de descanso que tuvo para trabajar su swing.
“En general, me siento muy bien”, declaró Ohtani el pasado 2 de octubre, la última vez que habló con los medios. “Siento que mi swing está mejor, que fluye con suavidad, y con solo un pequeño ajuste aquí y allá, estaré listo”.
Ohtani no logró forzar una racha positiva en aquel momento. Pero los Dodgers siguen predicando optimismo.
Decisión sobre la plantilla
Roberts afirmó que espera que el jugador de campo Miguel Rojas forme parte de la plantilla de los Dodgers para la NLCS, a pesar de haber sufrido una lesión en la espalda en el tercer partido de la NLDS.
Los Dodgers también tienen previsto incorporar a un lanzador y dar de baja a un jugador de campo, para equilibrar la plantilla con 13 lanzadores y 13 jugadores de campo.
“La duración, contar con un lanzador que pueda aguantar dos o tres entradas, es algo que, en esencia, protege contra los contratiempos en el pitcheo”, dijo Roberts cuando se le preguntó qué priorizarían los Dodgers. “En cuanto a la mano con la que lanzan, están bastante equilibrados. Así que eso realmente no entra en juego. Creo que para nosotros se trata más bien de quién puede cubrir un par de entradas en una situación de presión media o baja”.
El diestro Emmet Sheehan y el zurdo Justin Wrobleski podrían encajar en esa descripción.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Tarik Skubal Eager for the "Privilege" of More Postseason Pressure
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb

item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE, WI — Tarik Skubal feels healthy, fresh and ready to take the ball for the Dodgers in Sunday’s NLCS opener. Speaking at Saturday’s workout in Milwaukee, he praised the Brewers’ lineup and the pitcher he will face, Jacob Misiorowski. He also explained the easygoing start-day routine that has caught his teammates’ attention. For Skubal, being himself and keeping the task simple are part of getting ready for a game like this.
Milwaukee makes pitchers earn it
Skubal sees a Brewers team that can win in several ways, with hitters who make pitchers work throughout the order.
“First off, it’s a very talented roster. I think they do a lot of things really well,” he said. “They pitch, they play defense, they run the bases, they hit with runners in scoring position. They control the zone really well. Their walk percentage is up there at the top of the big leagues, I think, one through nine. And they don’t strike out a lot.”
“It’s a really good baseball team. They play the game the right way. I’ve got a lot of respect for the guys over there, and obviously the manager, Murph. I’m a big fan of his.”
On the mound, Skubal knows he will have to get ahead and earn outs in the strike zone.
“You’ve got to match it when you’re on the mound. Do everything you can to get ahead and understand they’re not going to chase,” he said. “Sometimes you’ve got to beat them in the zone. I think it’s going to be a fun matchup.”
Finding his own routine
Max Muncy and Dave Roberts have both spoken about how easy Skubal is to talk to on the day he pitches. Earlier in his career, he tried following the example of older starters.
“You come up and see all the older guys and the way they go about things. Almost always, they all have headphones in. They don’t really talk to anybody, and everybody stays out of their way,” Skubal said. “You naturally think, ‘Okay, that’s what big leaguers do. This is what I’m going to do.’”
“I did that early in my career, and I found it to be pretty exhausting. I found myself mentally exhausted in the second or third innings of games. I’m like, ‘Why am I tired? I should be ready to go today.’”
An injury in 2022 gave him time to rethink that approach.
“When I got hurt in ’22, I decided enough is enough. I’m caring way too much about all the little things that don’t really matter and don’t really impact the game of baseball,” he said. “Making sure the music is the right setting, making sure it’s the right songs at the right times. You’re caring about all the wrong things, I think.”
“For me, it was more mentally freeing to take my headphones off and be who I am and interact with guys. As it gets closer to game time, you get ready to go, and you’re going to go out there and compete.”
“I want to be myself, and then I’ll lock in as the game gets closer.”
A clubhouse that welcomed him
Skubal said the Dodgers encouraged him to bring that same approach when he joined the club.
“They have a culture where they want guys to be who they are. Be your authentic self, and they’re going to appreciate you for whatever that is,” he said. “Every guy’s different. We’re all humans at the end of the day, and we all tick differently. They wanted me to be me. That was the message early on.”
Getting to know his teammates took time, along with learning how each of them works.
“That’s something I also value, how to get everybody else going and marching in one direction,” he said. “Understanding how to communicate, that stuff takes time.”
“The clubhouse is great. Obviously, a veteran group, but at the same time very welcoming to who I am. We both have the same goal in mind, and that’s to win a World Series. That starts with Game 1 tomorrow.”
Respect for Misiorowski
Skubal enjoys studying pitching, and Misiorowski has given him plenty to watch. Beyond the velocity, he admires the right-hander’s ability to throw strikes.
“His ability to command pitches at that velocity consistently, he consistently gets ahead,” Skubal said. “Obviously, the velocity is what it is, and the stuff and the shapes are what they are. But I think his walk percentage and walks per nine are about as impressive as anything he does.”
“He forces teams to beat him. That’s the mark of a really good starting pitcher, a guy who’s going to force lineups to beat you. He does all those things.”
“As a fan of the game, I’m a fan as much as I’m a player, it’s fun to watch him pitch. Tomorrow is probably going to be a different story, but what he does is very impressive.”
“The pressure is a privilege”
The expectations around the Dodgers suit Skubal’s own goals.
“The pressure surrounding the Dodgers, I think it’s all a privilege,” he said. “As an athlete, this is what you want to be in. You want to have an expectation to win. I have those same expectations as a player.”
“Keeping the game the game, going out there and competing and doing what I can to put my team in a position to win, I think, is important. In bigger moments, simplify. Be who you are and leave it all out on the field.”
“You can live with whatever result happens as long as you gave it everything you had out there. That’s what I ask of myself every time out.”
Asked about his workload and how he feels heading into this start, Skubal gave an encouraging report.
“I feel good right now; I feel fresh. I feel healthy. That’s all you can ask for at this time of year,” he said. “The body feels good. I feel like the ball’s coming out really well, and I’m able to execute pitches.”
He wants to stay on the mound, while trusting Roberts and the relievers when it is time to hand over the ball.
“You trust the manager, trust the plan they have, trust the guys in the bullpen,” Skubal said. “The bullpen we have here is also very talented and can give us an advantage later in the game. You’ve got to trust that stuff and also trust where the game is, the situation.”
“I’m excited to go.”
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [Motor City Bengals] New intel reveals a denied Braves path for Tigers in Tarik Skubal trade talks
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins

item.content:encoded:
To the surprise of absolutely no one, the Dodgers and Braves are headed back to the NLCS. The entire LCS slate turned out (almost) the way everyone expected, as the three teams with the best regular season records in baseball have advanced to fight for their league's pennants, with the Guardians (ugh) playing spoiler on the American League side.
Tarik Skubal will get the ball for Game 1 of the NLCS against Jacob Misiorowski and a Brewers team that was rumored to be in on Skubal's trade market at the deadline. The Dodgers just rolled through their NLDS against the Braves, who were also in on the Skubal chase.
The Tigers seemed enamored by the package the Dodgers had to offer, but that doesn't mean that Scott Harris didn't negotiate with other teams. He was reportedly asking for a king's ransom, which only Andrew Friedman and LA were willing to give up for a rental.
According to Peter Abraham of the Boston Globe, the Braves were unwilling to part with reliever and potential closer-in-the-making Didier Fuentes, who posted a 2.45 ERA in 73 1/3 innings and a 3.86 ERA this postseason. In Atlanta's only win of the NLDS, he pitched an admirable 3 2/3-inning appearance and only gave up one run — a Max Muncy home run down to LA's last strike.
Braves were reportedly unwilling to give up Didier Fuentes in Tarik Skubal trade talks with Tigers
Fuentes was included in our Braves-Tigers trade proposal for Skubal alongside starter JR Ritchie and outfield prospect Patrick Clohisy. In an ideal world, that is how the trade would've shaken out: a controllable starter, a controllable backend bullpen arm, and a controllable outfielder.
The Dodgers were willing to give up two out of three in starter River Ryan and outfielder Zyhir Hope (and the jury will remain out on Brady Smith). The Tigers knew that none would be available to help them immediately, but the pedigree was evidently too hard to pass up.
Atlanta including Fuentes would've given them a leg up. Here was a controllable bullpen arm who's being primed for a long-term future as a closer, who could've slotted into the Tigers' awful bullpen immediately and maybe helped them thread the needle far more effectively than they actually did.
The teams that chose to back out of the Skubal bidding, including the Braves and Brewers, will have all offseason to ponder whether or not they should've just buckled down and overpaid for a rental — because it's working out pretty swimmingly for the Dodgers.

item.title: [ABC7 Los Angeles] Dodgers' Evan Phillips back 13 months after Tommy John surgery

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Reliever Evan Phillips was reinstated off the injured list Monday, returning to the Los Angeles Dodgers 13 months after having Tommy John surgery.
The 31-year-old right-hander spent the last month at Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he had a 1.80 ERA with 13 strikeouts and five walks in 10 innings over 12 games for the Comets.
"My primary mix is very sharp and ready to roll," he said before the Dodgers defeated the Colorado Rockies8-7 in 11 innings.
Phillips, who did not appear in Monday's win, had the surgery in May 2025, setting him on course for the first long-term rehab stint of his career.
"Credit to myself to stick with the process, leaning a lot on my family and my teammates here," he said. "I was very appreciative to spend my rehab here last year after the injury. I think that helped my mindset stay focused as well. Just ready for this next step."
Phillips won't be needed again in the closer role. Tanner Scott has been ably filling in for injured Edwin Díaz, who went on the IL in April for loose bodies in his elbow.
Phillips figures to slot into a middle-relief position as he builds up to a potentially bigger role in October, when the NL West-leading Dodgers are expected to seek a third consecutive World Series championship.
During his month in the minors, Phillips spent his first several games focused on the physical side of pitching, including experimenting with grips, location, and working on a changeup. Then he flipped the switch.
"The second half of it I really tried to step up the execution and competition side of things," he said. "That way, hopefully, it's not the first time I'm doing it here."
In a corresponding move, the Dodgers optioned right-hander Paul Gervase to Triple-A a day after he tossed two scoreless innings with two strikeouts against San Diego. Left-hander Jake Eder was released.
In other moves, the team added pitcher Carlos Duran to the 40-man roster and designated catcher Chuckie Robinson for assignment.
Duran, a 24-year-old right-hander, appeared in 30 games for Triple-A Oklahoma City, going 2-2 with a 3.86 ERA this season. He had 50 strikeouts in 35 innings while limiting hitters to a .203 average. He made his major league debut last season with the Athletics.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Tarik Skubal raves about Jacob Misiorowski, but Brewers starter passes
item.dc:creator: Matthew Moreno
item.description: There is added intrigue with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers squaring off in the National League Championship Series for a second year in a row thanks to the pitching matchup of Tarik Skubal and Jacob Misiorowski. item.content:encoded:
There is added intrigue with the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers squaring off in the National League Championship Series for a second year in a row thanks to the pitching matchup of Tarik Skubal and Jacob Misiorowski.
Skubal is the reigning two-time American League Cy Young Award winner, and Misiorowski is the presumed NL winner for 2026. Misiorowski downplayed starting opposite Skubal, but the left-hander was more than willing to heap praise on his counterpart.
“He’s very impressive. His ability to command pitches at that velocity consistently, consistently gets ahead,” Skubal began. “I think what stands out with him is obviously the velocity is what it is, and the stuff and the shapes are what they are, but I think his walk percentage and walk per nine is about as impressive as what he does.
“He doesn’t walk anybody. He forces teams to beat him. He doesn’t really beat himself too many times when he’s out there. I think that’s the mark of a really good starting pitcher is a guy that’s not going to beat themselves, going to force lineups to beat you.
“He does all those things. As a fan of the game — I’m a fan as much as I’m a player — it’s fun to watch him pitch. Now, tomorrow is probably going to be a different story, but yeah, what he does is very impressive.”
Comparatively, Misiorowski chose to highlight his focus being on facing the Dodgers, similar to when he’s previously been asked about starting in the same game as Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes.
“Like I said countless times before when I face Skenes or any guy like that, I’m not really looking at them. I’m looking at the lineup more than him,” Misiorowski explained.
“For me personally, it doesn’t really mean that much to face a guy like that. Obviously it’s cool. The dude’s insane. But I’m just hoping that these guys can do their job and handle business with him and let me do my thing and try to get that side taken care of.”
Skubal heads into a second consecutive Game 1 start with the Dodgers having gone 5-0 with 1.95 ERA in his last five outings, including the NL Division Series.
Meanwhile, Misiorowski has a career 1.59 ERA and 40.9% strikeout rate in three games (two starts) against the Dodgers, including the postseason.
Jacob Misiorowski respecting Shohei Ohtani
When Misiorowski faced the Dodgers during the regular season, he uncorked multiple fastballs over 100 mph to Shohei Ohtani. And although the Dodgers’ star has been mired in a prolonged slump, the hard-throwing righty is not taking him lightly.
“It’s still October. They’re going to find a way to get a bat on ball and get on base how they can,” Misiorowski said. “You got to still pitch like he’s the best in the world and trust your stuff, and go beat him at his game and do your job.”

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Notes: Miguel Rojas Injury Update, Tarik Skubal Loves LA, Pat Murphy’s Underdog Narrative

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have an injury update on veteran infielder Miguel Rojas after he left Game 3 of the National League Division Series early after an errant swing caused major back discomfort. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have an injury update on veteran infielder Miguel Rojas after he left Game 3 of the National League Division Series early after an errant swing caused major back discomfort. Though he didn't appear in the series-clinching Game 4, manager Dave Roberts still seemed hopeful that last season's World Series hero would be back in time for the the NL Champinship Series rematch against the Milwaukee Brewers.
"I just talked to him briefly, he's in good spirits," Roberts said on Saturday. "We're going to talk to him right now, but as far as the flight, I'm expecting him to be a part of it, be on the roster."
In other news, two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal opened up about his love for his new team.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal ahead of the trade deadline after he spent the previous six seasons with the Detroit Tigers. With his impending free agency likely pointing towards a contract worth $400 million or more, Dodgers fans should feel more at ease that the southpaw won't look to leave LA before after his most recent comments.
"It's a great team," Skubal said. “The culture that they have here. The preparation, the expectation to win — I love being a part of it."
Finally, Brewers manager Pat Murphy once again has decided to go with the underdog approach ahead of the NLCS. The 103-win Brewers do not appear to be underdogs purely going by regular season records, (or with possessing home field advantage), but the skipper spoke on different "luxuries" that LA has over Milwaukee.
"I just have the front office to thank for being able to pick up the right guys because those type of guys have filled in and did really nicely for us," Muprhy said. "But we don't have the luxury of maybe you have a guy that hadn't pitched much and he's going to make his debut in August. He's a $30 million two-time Cy Young winner or something like that. We don't have that cushion. So we're more desperate to play every single game."

Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. item.content:encoded:
ドジャース マンシーが大谷翔平を気遣ったワンシーン 不振の大スターに向けられたカメラを無言で徹底ガード タオルまで持ち出す
ドジャースが１０日（日本時間１１日）、敵地で前日練習を行った。練習中にはマックス・マンシー内野手が大谷翔平選手を報道陣のカメラからガードする場面があった。
大谷が屋外で打撃練習を行うため、ベンチでスパイクに履き替えている時だった。ベンチ外から報道陣のカメラが一斉に向けられたことに気づいたマンシー。自ら大谷の前に歩み寄って報道陣をギロリ。この様子に笑いが漏れると、足りないと思ったのか今度はタオルを両手で広げて徹底ガードした。
これには大谷も思わず苦笑い。シーズン終盤の負傷者リスト入りから打撃の状態が上がらず、８月を最後にアーチが出ていない状況。地区シリーズでは４試合で打率・１５４、本塁打、打点共に無しという状況だったが、第４戦では四球を選んで二盗を決めた。これが捕手の悪送球を誘って三塁へ進むと、敵失で同点のホームを踏んでいた。
不振のチームメートを守ろうとしたベテランの気遣い。地区シリーズ突破後のシャンパンファイトでは、大谷とマンシーが２人でハグをかわすシーンもあった。
ドジャースを支えるベテランは会見でキケ・ヘルナンデスら大舞台に強い選手について問われると「１０月に野球をするのは本当に難しい。とても大変。この時期に集中力を高めてプレーできるのは、やはり特定の気質を持った選手だと思う。僕たちには、そういう選手がたくさんいる。大舞台で結果を出せる選手を見るのは、うれしいことですね」と語っていた。
自身もＭＬＢ史上７人目となるポストシーズン２０本塁打に王手をかけている。「それは本当に素晴らしいこと。もし達成できるなら、そのホームランがチームの勝利につながる一発であってほしい。僕にとっては、いつもそれが一番大切。試合に勝って次に進み、次の試合にも勝つ。それが目標だ」と力を込めていた。

item.content:encoded:
AI 핵심 요약
beta
- 김혜성이 11일 다저스 훈련에 참여했다.
- 현지서는 챔피언십 시리즈 로스터 합류를 점쳤다.
- 김하성·송성문·이정후는 PS를 마쳤다.
!AI가 자동 생성한 요약으로 정확하지 않을 수 있어요.
[서울=뉴스핌] 유다연 기자=미국 프로야구리그 메이저리그(MLB) 로스엔젤레스(LA) 다저스 김혜성이 챔피언십 시리즈 로스터 합류 가능성을 높였다. 한국인 메이저리거 중 유일하게 포스트시즌(PS) 잔류에 성공했다.
다저스는 11일(한국시간) 공식 SNS 계정을 통해 "잠금"이라는 말과 함께 선수단 훈련 사진을 게재했다.
해당 사진에는 무키 베츠를 필두로 미겔 로하스, 윌 스미스, 오타니 쇼헤이, 테오스카 에르난데스, 타릭 스쿠벌, 맥스 먼시, 토미 에드먼, 알렉스 베시아, 프레디 프리먼, 키케 에르난데스, 앤디 파헤스, 사사키 로키, 호세 데 파울라가 위스콘신주 밀워키 아메리칸 패밀리 필드에서 훈련하는 모습이 담겼다.
다저스는 오는 12일 같은 장소에서 열리는 2026 MLB 내셔널리그 챔피언십 시리즈 1차전에서 밀워키와 맞붙는다.
이날 공개된 사진에 김혜성과 알렉스 프리랜드가 수비 훈련 중인 모습이 담겼다. 대부분 야수들이 타격 연습하는 모습이 공개된 것과 비교하면 사뭇 다른 풍경이다.
당초 미국 현지 언론은 김혜성의 챔피언십 시리즈 로스터 합류가 어려울 것이라고 분석했다. 외야수 미겔 로하스가 지난 3차전에서 통증으로 교체된 후 출전 여부가 결정되지 않았고, 다저스 데이브 로버츠 감독이 백업 야수 대신 투수를 포함시킬 것이라 예고했다.
이 명단에서 가장 먼저 빠질 선수로 김혜성이 꼽혔다. 김혜성은 지난 5월 빅리그 로스터에서 제외된 뒤 다저스 산하 마이너리그 트리플A구단인 오클라호마 시티에서 시즌을 보냈다. 올 시즌 빅리그 성적은 43경기 타율 0.259, 30안타(1홈런) 11타점 16득점에 그쳤다. PS 진출을 앞두고 다시 빅리그에 콜업됐지만, 지난 8일 애틀랜타와 디비전시리즈 마지막 경기에서 승부가 확정된 9회에야 대수비로 출전했다. 지난해 포스트시즌에서도 대주자와 대수비로만 투입됐던 점을 고려했다.
김혜성은 일단 연습에는 모습을 드러내 챔피언십 시리즈 로스터 합류에 성공한 것으로 보인다. 챔피언십 시리즈에서 자기에 대한 평가를 긍정적으로 만들어야 한다.
한편 김혜성 외에 MLB에서 뛰고 있는 한국 선수들의 가을야구는 종료됐다. 송성문이 속한 샌디에이고와 김하성이 속한 애틀랜타는 디비전시리즈 탈락으로 포스트시즌(PS)을 마무리했다.
샌디에이고는 올 시즌 내셔널리그 서부지구 2위(91승 71패)로 PS에 진출했다. 시카고 컵스와 와일드카드 2전 2승 후 밀워키와 디비전시리즈에서 1승 3패에 그쳐 탈락했다. 올 시즌 78경기 타율 0.191, 25안타(1홈런) 17타점 22득점을 기록한 송성문은 로스터에는 이름을 올렸지만, 경기에는 출장하지 못했다.
애틀랜타는 필라델피아와 와일드카드에서 2승 1패로 디비전 시리즈에 올랐다. 하지만 다저스와 디비전 시리즈에서 1승 3패로 PS를 마무리했다. 김하성은 와일드카드 2경기, 디비전시리즈 2경기에서 선발 출전했지만 안타 없이 2사사구 1득점 3삼진을 기록했다.
김하성은 지난해 프리에이전트(FA) 자격을 얻어 탬파베이와 2년 2900만 달러(약 389억 7020만 원)로 FA 대박을 쳤지만, 부상 복귀 후 성적이 나오지 않아 방출되는 수모를 겪었다. 이후 애틀랜타로 이적해 빅리그 생활을 이어간 김하성은 지난 시즌 48경기 타율 0.234, 40안타(5홈런) 17타점 19득점을 기록했다.
올 시즌을 앞두고 김하성은 애틀랜타와 1년 2000만 달러(약 268억 7600만 원)의 계약을 맺었다. 하지만 빙판길에서 넘어지며 골절상을 당해 복귀가 다소 늦어졌던 김하성은 올 시즌 51경기 타율 0.116, 15안타 9타점 11득점에 그쳤다. 포스트시즌에서도 기대했던 활약을 보여주지 못했다.
현지에서는 결별이 확실시 되는 분위기다. 일각에서는 빅리그 다른 팀에서조차 생존이 쉽지 않다는 분석도 나왔다. 포스트시즌이라는 마지막 기회도 살리지 못한 김하성은 새 활로를 뚫어야 하는 처지다.
이정후가 속한 샌프란시스코는 내셔널리그 서부지구 4위(65승 97패)로 일찌감치 PS 탈락이 확정됐다. 하지만 이정후는 올 시즌 143경기 타율 0.276, 149안타(10홈런) 57타점 65득점을 기록하며 코리안리거 가운데 가장 좋은 성적을 냈다.
올 겨울 찬바람을 맞을 것으로 예상되는 한국 선수들이 빅리그에 잔류할 수 있을지 관심이 쏠린다.
willowdy@newspim.com

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Tarik Skubal Defends Clayton Kershaw for Unfair Postseason Narrative
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: There is no doubt that Los Angeles Dodgers legend Clayton Kershaw is one of the best pitchers of this generation. The Dodgers southpaw is a surefire Hall of Famer after 18 spectacular seasons on the mound, all in Los Angeles. Kershaw helped catapult the Dodgers to new heights during his tenure, but his postseason struggles were evident. Kershaw is considered one of the greatest regular-season pitchers in baseball history, but the conversation changes when it comes to his October performance. How
item.content:encoded:
There is no doubt that Los Angeles Dodgers legend Clayton Kershaw is one of the best pitchers of this generation.
The Dodgers southpaw is a surefire Hall of Famer after 18 spectacular seasons on the mound, all in Los Angeles.
Kershaw helped catapult the Dodgers to new heights during his tenure, but his postseason struggles were evident.
Kershaw is considered one of the greatest regular-season pitchers in baseball history, but the conversation changes when it comes to his October performance.
However, it's not entirely black and white when it comes to Kershaw and October.
Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal recently defended Kershaw against the unfair postseason narrative surrounding him.
“I don’t really buy into that narrative with Kersh, the postseason struggles,” Skubal said.
On the surface, Kershaw's play in the regular season versus October is stark.
His regular-season ERA sits at 2.43, while his postseason ERA sits at 4.30. On top of that, Kershaw has had a number of meltdowns, including the 2023 National League Division Series against the Ariziona Diamondbacks and a 2019 relief appearance against the Washington Nationals.
Those meltdowns disproportionately skew his career postseason ERA over roughly 200 innings.
A ton of factors play into that, including the workload he endured before October. Kershaw made 41 postseason appearances, but four came on short rest, and nine were relief appearances.
“It takes a superhuman to be held to the standard he was being held to, in the biggest of moments,” Skubal said. “I think he was great. He did everything he could for his team. He wore it out there sometimes. Chasing box scores and stuff is kind of unfair to judge guys on, because I’m sure he was pitching through some stuff and grinding through some stuff.
“But he had to do it, because he was Clayton Kershaw.”
How Much Blame Does Clayton Kershaw Deserve for His Playoff Struggles?
The bad often outweighs the good, and that is no exception when it comes to Kershaw.
He had some stellar outings, including Game 2 of the 2016 NL Championship Series against the Chicago Cubs, Game 1 of the 2013 NLDS against the Atlanta Braves and Game 1 of the 2020 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Kershaw certainly deserves some blame; however, managers like Don Mattingly and Dave Roberts occasionally left him out too long, which eventually led to those blow-up innings where he got the blame.
Either way, Skubal — like many other MLB fans and pundits — doesn't buy into the "choker" label that has been unfairly placed on Kershaw.

item.title: [New York Post] How the ‘Dinosaur’ Dodgers continue to find the fountain of youth
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: MILWAUKEE –– Dave Roberts delivered the speech. Teoscar Hernández supplied the punch line. In the wake of their National League Division Series defeat of the Atlanta Braves last week, the Dodgers gathered around their manager at the start of a champagne celebration in Truist Park’s visiting clubhouse. item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE –– Dave Roberts delivered the speech. Teoscar Hernández supplied the punch line.
In the wake of their National League Division Series defeat of the Atlanta Braves last week, the Dodgers gathered around their manager at the start of a champagne celebration in Truist Park’s visiting clubhouse.
First, Roberts extolled their culture and competitiveness. He then declared that “we’re smarter, we’re better and we’re tougher” than their postseason competition.
That’s when, from the corner of the room, Hernández chimed in with one more observation.
“And we’re dinosaurs!” he shouted.
Cretaceous creatures, who have once again found the fountain of October youth.
Throughout the regular season and leading into the playoffs, the Dodgers’ aging roster loomed as their biggest area of concern. Their average lineup age of 30.9 years old, according to Baseball Reference, was the oldest in the majors.
Their grizzled veteran core has played more games (and traveled more miles, including two season-opening Asia trips) than any other club in baseball the past two years.

That’s why the team could help but notice the recent “dinosaur” comment made by new Padres owner José E. Feliciano –– even if he was trying to refer to the actual collection of fossils kept by Dodgers owner Mark Walter.
To the two-time defending champions, it still qualified as a perceived slight.
“We’ve heard it,” 36-year-old third baseman Max Muncy said. “But you can’t focus on the outside stuff for us.
Indeed, the Dodgers do not need any extra motivation this postseason, as they continue their quest for a third-straight World Series title in the NL Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
“You worry about yourself,” Muncy said. “You worry about how you’re getting ready for the game, how you’re preparing for the series.”
But talk about their age has nonetheless added some fuel to their competitive fire.
“Los Viejitos!!!” Kiké Hernández captioned on an Instagram photo of him, Muncy, Miguel Rojas, Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman earlier this week –– playfully using the Spanish term for “old folks” to describe the club’s five eldest statesmen.
“I like our dinosaurs,” Roberts also joked with AM 570 earlier this month. “Our dinosaurs have come through in the biggest spots.”
That was not always the case during the second half of this year’s regular season, when the Dodgers’ offense slipped into such a glaring funk –– highlighted by an inability to consistently slug the ball –– that one rival scout remarked in late August: “This is the oldest they’ve ever looked.”
Since then, however, they have rediscovered a jolt. They scored the fourth-most runs in the majors in September. They outslugged the Braves in the NLDS by belting eight home runs, all but one of which came from players age 33 or older.
Now, they are banking on their experience to give them an edge in this week’s NLCS, starting with a showdown against 24-year-old flamethrowing Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1 on Sunday.
“The toughest part about age is [managing it during the regular] season,” Roberts said. “But once you get through the marathon and you get to the sprint of the postseason, advantage goes to us in the sense of the experience.”
Father Time, of course, will eventually win out at some point.
Even Muncy acknowledged that there has been “some talk” of this being a potential final ride for this version of the roster.
“For us, it’s about playing for each other, and that’s what makes it so special,” Muncy said. “A lot of us have been through a lot of moments together –– good, bad, in the middle –– and I wouldn’t want to share those with anyone else, that’s for sure.”
For now, however, the Dinosaur Dodgers just want to keep on roaring.
Eight wins away from another World Series, age is the least of their concerns.
“I don’t like thinking that this could be towards the end [of our run], because I don’t think it is,” Muncy said. “I think we still have a lot of good baseball left in us. Hopefully we can keep going.”

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers’ Andrew Friedman Sends Clear Message on Hyeseong Kim’s Future With LA
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
Hyeseong Kim's 2026 season did not go as planned. He lost his backup infielder's job to Santiago Espinal in May and never got it back.
The Dodgers optioned Kim to Triple-A Oklahoma City after he collected a .259/.323/.328 slash line in 43 games. No player who made at least 100 plate appearances for the Dodgers this season finished with a lower OPS than Kim (.651).
Kim was on the Dodgers' roster for the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves, but made just one appearance as a defensive replacement in the ninth inning of Game 4. President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman hinted before the NLDS about what his limited role would look like.
"I think for us on this roster specifically, just his positional versatility and his foot speed," Friedman said. "We have a lot of team strengths, in my mind. Foot speed is not one of them. So there can be opportunities late in games to utilize that in a way to help us score a run."
Kim can already run and field at no worse than a league-average level. For him to hit well enough for the Dodgers to carry his bat on their rosters for the rest of the postseason, Kim will have to learn how to hit Triple-A pitching first.
In 85 games with the Oklahoma City Comets, the Dodgers' top farm team, Kim reached base at a .330 clip. In the hitter-friendly Pacific Coast League, only two teams finished with a lower OBP than Kim. And only two qualified players finished with a lower slugging percentage than Kim (.345).
Kim doesn't need to hit the ball over the fence to make the most of his talent; he merely needs to put the ball in play. A 24.9% strikeout rate against Triple-A pitching might be fine for a slugger. For Kim, it was abysmal.
"As far as his development, we think really highly of the player," Friedman said. "The swing got a little off this year, and we look forward to getting through this, hopefully winning 11 games this month, and then working over the offseason because we really believe in the ability."
In January 2025, the Dodgers signed Kim to a three-year, $12.5 million contract with team options for 2028 and 2029. The 27-year-old came over from Korea with little assurance of playing time but found his way into 71 games as a rookie.
Mostly on the strength of his glove, Kim accrued 1.7 bWAR in 71 games — nearly a 4-win pace over a full season. If his bat ever comes around, Kim could be a real asset. For now, the Dodgers will take what they can get from his feet.

item.title: [LancasterOnline] Christian Yelich and the Brewers looking to get past Shohei Ohtani and the Dodgers in NLCS sequel
item.dc:creator: JAY COHEN
item.description: MILWAUKEE (AP) — All along, Christian Yelich felt this was going to be part of the road for the Milwaukee Brewers. It was always going to be the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers — with their consecutive World Series titles and a payroll that casts a long shadow over Yelich and the small-market Brewers. “We’ve been expecting having to play them in this round since spring training, in the regular season,” Yelich said Saturday. “You kind of just know that’s what’s going to happen.” The 2026 NL Championsh
item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — All along, Christian Yelich felt this was going to be part of the road for the Milwaukee Brewers.
It was always going to be the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers — with their consecutive World Series titles and a payroll that casts a long shadow over Yelich and the small-market Brewers.
“We’ve been expecting having to play them in this round since spring training, in the regular season,” Yelich said Saturday. “You kind of just know that’s what’s going to happen.”
The 2026 NL Championship Series is a sequel, with Shohei Ohtani and the Dodgers taking on Jackson Chourio and the Brewers. Los Angeles swept Milwaukee in last year's NLCS on the way to the franchise's 26th NL pennant and ninth World Series championship. The Dodgers also eliminated the Brewers in the NLCS in 2018 and the wild-card round in 2020.
Game 1 on Sunday night features a pair of stingy aces. Tarik Skubal goes for Los Angeles after the two-time Cy Young Award winner was acquired in an Aug. 1 trade with Detroit, and Jacob Misiorowski — the front-runner for the NL Cy Young Award — starts for Milwaukee.
The return engagement for the NLCS also shines a light on the competing arguments at the center of MLB's collective bargaining negotiations. Baseball’s five-year labor contract expires Dec. 1, and management is expected to lock out players in a confrontation that could affect the 2027 season.
The Dodgers went 100-62 this season and won the NL West for the fifth straight year after they had an opening-day payroll of $323.6 million, second only to the New York Mets. Milwaukee's opening-day payroll of $125.9 million ranked 20th, and the Brewers set a franchise record with a major league-best 103 wins on the way to their fourth consecutive Central title.
“We’re focused on trying to win, and I think we have for a while,” Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold said. “Regardless of what the economics look like, the guys in there believe, and so do I.”
Milwaukee was shut down by Los Angeles in last year's playoffs, hitting .118 while managing just one run in each game in the sweep. Ohtani punctuated the series by swatting three solo homers and striking out 10 over six shutout innings in Game 4.
Ohtani won't pitch this time around because of injuries, and the Japanese slugger went 2 for 13 with four strikeouts in the four-game NL Division Series against Atlanta. But the Dodgers still have a formidable rotation, fronted by Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
“Every night when you play these guys, you know you’re going to face a great pitcher, a Cy Young-caliber pitcher,” Yelich said.

He is clearly not 100 percent after battling knee, bicep and neck injuries this year. Milwaukee Brewers superstar Jacob Misiorowski stil
item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski isn't changing approach even with Shohei Ohtani's slump appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Shohei Ohtani has just one extra base hit in his last 16 games and has not recorded a home run since Aug. 18. Calling the four-time MVP a shell of himself is underselling this shocking slump. He is clearly not 100 percent after battling knee, bicep and neck injuries this year. Milwaukee Brewers superstar Jacob Misiorowski still sees a unicorn, however, and he is not about to underestimate him in the biggest start of his MLB career.
The presumptive NL Cy Young Award winner intends to show Ohtani complete respect when the two face off in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday night.
"It's still October," Misiorowski told reporters, per the Dodger Blue YouTube account. "They're going to find a way to get a bat on ball and get on base how they can, so you got to still pitch like he's the best in the world. Trust your stuff and go beat him at his game and do your job."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
The 6-foot-7 right-hander is saying all the right stuff ahead of this NLCS rematch. He remembers what Ohtani did last year. The Japanese juggernaut finished off LA's sweep of the Brewers by mashing three home runs and striking out 10 batters in six scoreless innings pitched. It may be the greatest single-game performance ever.
Yes, he is not pitching this postseason, and yes, his bat is ice-cold, but Shohei Ohtani can still make a massive impact as long as he is in the lineup. Jacob Misiorowski can obviously do the same from the mound.
Following an inconsistent showing versus the San Diego Padres in the NL Division Series — two earned runs in four innings — the 24-year-old aims to squash the two-time reigning World Series champions in American Family Field. Consecutive ho-hum outings is highly unlikely. Misiorowski posted an MLB-best 1.80 ERA, 252 strikeouts and 0.802 WHIP in 174 2/3 innings during the regular season.
The Dodgers are a different kind of beast in the playoffs, but so is he. After a shaky end to his rookie campaign, the 2022 second-round draft pick regrouped and thrived out of the Milwaukee bullpen in the 2026 MLB postseason. He threw 12 magnificent innings that helped launch him into elite status in 2026. Misiorowski's confidence should be at an all-time high entering the NLCS.
But no amount of self-assurance will convince him to shrug off Ohtani. This mega matchup will take place at approximately 8 p.m. ET on Sunday.
Related: How Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski feels about starting NLCS Game 1 vs. Tarik Skubal

item.title: [MLB.com] Dream Skubal-Miz showdown all set for NLCS Game 1
item.dc:creator: Max Ralph
item.description: The Dodgers announced Friday that Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 on Sunday, while the Brewers announced Saturday that they will have ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound. item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers announced Friday that Tarik Skubal will get the ball in Game 1 on Sunday, while the Brewers announced Saturday that they will have ace Jacob Misiorowski on the mound. Both teams clinched their spot in the NLCS on Thursday, the Brewers with a 3-1 win over the Padres and the Dodgers with a 4-1 win over the Braves.
Misiorowski pitched just once in the series, throwing four innings of two-run ball in Game 1. Similarly, Skubal opened things against the Braves, going six innings with just one run allowed, and did not pitch again. Both should be well-rested.
The most realistic argument against a Skubal-Misiorowski duel lies in October superstar Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but the Dodgers righty pitched in Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, meaning he’d start Sunday on just four days’ rest. He will pitch in Game 2 on Monday with a regular recovery that would make more sense.
We’ve seen great pitching in the 2026 postseason thus far and several marquee matchups: Cam Schlittler vs. Payton Tolle; Chris Sale vs. Jesús Luzardo; Max Fried vs. Sonny Gray; Gerrit Cole vs. Drew Rasmussen; Yamamoto vs. Sale.
But Skubal vs. Misiorowski will take the cake.
After some struggles late in the regular season, Misiorowski pitched behind an opener when he made his postseason debut a year ago, but he was effective in three appearances. He allowed only one run across seven innings in the NLDS against the Cubs, before striking out nine and yielding just one run in five innings against the Dodgers in the NLCS.
But this is not the same Miz in 2026. The flame-throwing 24-year-old finished the regular season with MLB bests in ERA (1.80), strikeouts (252), WHIP (0.80) and opponents’ batting average (.157). It was more than a breakout -- it was among the greatest pitching seasons in MLB history.
Misiorowski’s four-seam fastball topped out at 104.8 mph and averaged 101.2 mph against the Padres in the NLDS. With the adrenaline that is sure to be present on Sunday, who knows what eye-popping numbers he could put up.
As for Skubal, he won’t win a third consecutive Cy Young. But that won’t take away from the 2.72 ERA he posted in 26 starts, including a 2.61 mark after his blockbuster trade to the Dodgers. Remember, too, that Skubal missed 44 days in the summer after he needed surgery to remove loose bodies in his left elbow. There have been few signs of rust from that recovery.
Skubal’s strong playoff debut with the Dodgers was just more of what we’re used to from the southpaw. He made six postseason starts as a Tiger in 2024 and 2025 with a 2.04 ERA, never going shorter than six innings and allowing more than two runs just once.
The Brewers and Dodgers will already provide appointment viewing throughout the NLCS, a rematch of the 2025 NL pennant battle and a meeting of MLB’s top regular-season teams in 2026. Add in the bout of Misiorowski and Skubal in Game 1, and this series should get off to an awfully hot start.

item.title: [Bozeman Daily Chronicle] Dodgers turn to Tarik Skubal for NLCS Game 1 opener vs Brewers; Yoshinobu Yamamoto set for Game 2
item.dc:creator: BETH HARRIS
item.description: LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, last year's World Series MVP, will start Game 2 on Monday at American Family Field, manager Dave Roberts said Friday. Skubal also started Game 1 of the NL Division Series. The two-time Cy Young Award winner pitched six dominant innings, allowing one run and two hits, in a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves. The left-
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, last year's World Series MVP, will start Game 2 on Monday at American Family Field, manager Dave Roberts said Friday.
Skubal also started Game 1 of the NL Division Series. The two-time Cy Young Award winner pitched six dominant innings, allowing one run and two hits, in a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves. The left-hander struck out seven and walked two.
Yamamoto started Game 3 of the NLDS, and struck out 10 over seven innings. The right-hander allowed one run and four hits to go with one walk.
Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell struggled as the Game 2 starter against the Braves, who won 3-2 to tie the best-of-five series 1-1. The Dodgers went on to eliminate the Braves, 3-1.
Roberts said the Dodgers were in discussions about adding a pitcher for the best-of-seven NLCS, which would require them to drop a position player. Rosters are due Sunday morning.
Miguel Rojas exited Game 3 against the Braves during an at-bat with lower back pain. The utility player underwent imaging, which mostly showed prior back issues. He took ground balls and a couple rounds of batting practice at Dodger Stadium on Friday.
Rojas, 37, has said he's leaning toward retiring at the end of the season.
“Today was encouraging,” Roberts said. “We still have a flight to get on and see how he comes in tomorrow for the workout there, so there’s nothing definitive.”

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers to make playoff roster cut but hope injured World Series hero isn’t it
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: The Dodgers are planning to cut a position player from their playoff roster for their upcoming National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers. For now, though, they are hopeful that injured veteran infielder Miguel Rojas won’t have to be the casualty. Rojas remains questionable to be on the Dodgers’ NLCS roster, according to manager Dave Roberts, after he suffered a back injury in Game 3 of the NL Division Series this past week that left him unavailable for the team’s series-c
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are planning to cut a position player from their playoff roster for their upcoming National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
For now, though, they are hopeful that injured veteran infielder Miguel Rojas won’t have to be the casualty.
Rojas remains questionable to be on the Dodgers’ NLCS roster, according to manager Dave Roberts, after he suffered a back injury in Game 3 of the NL Division Series this past week that left him unavailable for the team’s series-clinching victory in Game 4 over the Braves.
However, during a video conference with reporters on Friday, Roberts said Rojas is feeling better and took “a step in the right direction” during a team workout at Dodger Stadium.
“Today was encouraging,” Roberts said. “He took ground balls and took a couple rounds of BP. So that was good to see.”
Roberts emphasized that there is “nothing definitive” yet on Rojas’ status for the best-of-seven matchup against the Brewers, with the team waiting to see how he comes through another workout on Saturday after they travel to Milwaukee ahead of Game 1.
“We’ve just got to be certain that if we do have him on [the roster], he can stay healthy,” Roberts said, wary of the possibility of having to remove Rojas from the roster mid-series because of his injury, which would leave him ineligible for a potential World Series under MLB’s playoff roster rules.
But, Roberts also noted that an MRI revealed no new injury in Rojas’ back — just “stuff that he has had prior history” with — and reiterated that he was “encouraged, again, with what I saw today.”
If Rojas is good to go, then the Dodgers will have to trim another position player from their roster for the NLCS, with the team planning to carry 13 pitchers for the best-of-seven matchup instead of the 12 it had for the five-game divisional round.
The most likely candidate would be Hyeseong Kim, who was called up from Triple-A for the NLDS to serve as a pinch-running and defensive specialist. All the Dodgers’ other reserves (besides unused backup catcher Hunter Feduccia) made important contributions to their NLDS triumph — including rookie sensation Josue De Paula, who drew a pinch-hit walk during Wednesday’s go-ahead seventh-inning rally in Game 4.
As for the extra pitcher the Dodgers could add: Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan and Jack Dreyer would figure to be the foremost candidates.
“After we get off this call,” Roberts said Friday afternoon, “I’m gonna get with the guys and figure out what arm we’re going to add.”
Rojas initially got hurt while playing second base in Game 3 on Tuesday — in what was his second straight start for the two-time defending champions as an extra right-handed bat in their lineup against an opposing left-handed starter.
He said he tweaked his back while fielding a critical ground ball that got the Dodgers out of a fifth-inning jam, then felt continued discomfort after fouling a pitch off in an eighth-inning at-bat that ultimately forced him out of the game.
Rojas was initially optimistic the issue would be minor, but woke up on the morning of Game 4 feeling “sore and uncomfortable,” preventing him from partaking in any baseball activities that day.
“Tomorrow we will know a little bit more about where my back is,” he said during the team’s clubhouse celebration on Wednesday night. “Looking forward to being able to play in the next series.”
Though Rojas would likely be back in primarily a bench role for the NLCS (the Brewers have just one left-hander in their playoff rotation), his presence is nonetheless important — as a trusted right-handed bat; a defensive option at second base, third base and shortstop; and a steadying veteran presence in his 13th and likely final big-league season.
“We still have a plane flight, there’s another workout, and there’s no deadline right now; we’re not up against it,” Roberts said. “So we have time to ultimately make that decision.”

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] An Unlikely Dodgers Teammate Helped Save Edwin Díaz’s Season
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Kiké Hernandez revealed that a minor league player helped fuel Edwin Diaz’s rise. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Kiké Hernandez revealed that a minor league player helped fuel Edwin Diaz’s rise.
What caused Edwin Diaz’s turnaround
After Game 4 of the NLDS, amid a wild clubhouse celebration after the NLCS spot was clinched, Kiké Hernandez revealed that minor league catcher Chadwick Tromp found the issue in Diaz’s mechanics.
Tromp signed a minor-league deal with the Dodgers midseason.
“A former Brave, Chadwick Tromp, who was with us in AAA, noticed something in his mechanics, and they went over it after the game, and it was a very easy fix, and Sugar is back to being Sugar,” Hernandez said.
Since returning, the command has been much better for Diaz, while the velocity continues to increase, as does the fastball and slider movement.
Diaz and the Dodgers felt he was a few tweaks away from becoming the guy they signed for $69 million, and they were right.
Edwin Diaz’s full arc
Diaz has turned his debut Dodgers season around since returning from the injured list and a topsy-turvy minor league rehab assignment with the OKC Comets in Triple-A.
After a horrendous season by his standards, Diaz returned on September 18th and hasn’t allowed a run since.
He allowed one hit and a walk over five shutout innings in the regular season, and Dave Roberts trusted him enough to make the postseason roster and give him a high-leverage spot.
In return, Diaz made three appearances in the four-game NLDS, allowing one hard-hit single and recording two saves.
His postseason performance marked a full turnaround for Diaz.
“He’s had a tough season,” Roberts said after the NLDS. “He’s been hurt. He was having trouble with his delivery and went on a long rehab assignment.
“But to get him pitching this way – that’s the reason why we got him. The last two nights, that’s the reason why we acquired a guy like Edwin Diaz.
“He’s one of the great closers in the game. For him to be pitching his best right now, that’s what you hope for, and I give him a lot of credit.”
Now, Diaz is expected to keep closing, or at the very least, play a major role on the closing committee.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are slated to play the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series. Game 1 of the NLCS is scheduled to start at 5:00 p.m. PDT on Sunday. The game will be played at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Ahead of the NLCS, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced an update on injured infielder Miguel Rojas.
Los Angeles Dodgers’ Dave Roberts Announces Miguel Rojas News Before NLCS vs. Milwaukee Brewers
Via Orange County Register/Southern California Newspaper Group’s Bill Plunkett on X: Dave Roberts said Miguel Rojas had imaging on his back injury. “Nothing definitive.” He’s receiving treatment. Want to see how he handles plane fight, workout in Milwaukee tomorrow before making decision about NLCS roster
Rojas
exited Game 3 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park with a back injury.
Looking at Miguel Rojas
ATLANTA, GEORGIA – AUGUST 27: Miguel Rojas #72 of the Los Angeles Dodgers fails to cleanly field a ground ball in the seventh inning against the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park on August 27, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images)
Rojas is expected to retire at the end of the season.
The 37-year-old infielder has 13 years of big-league experience.
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – JULY 10: Miguel Rojas #72 of the Los Angeles Dodgers makes a catch during the ninth inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Dodger Stadium on July 10, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Melina Pizano/Getty Images)
Rojas hit .267/.312/.391 with four home runs and 23 RBI over 105 games during the regular season.
He has gone 1-for-4 with a double and a strikeout in the playoffs so far.
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – AUGUST 13: Miguel Rojas #8 of the Los Angeles Dodgers warms up before the game against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
Rojas began his MLB career with the Dodgers in 2014.
After the 2015 season, Rojas played for the Miami Marlins from 2015-22.
Rojas rejoined the Dodgers before the 2023 season. He has played for the team ever since.
TORONTO, ONTARIO – OCTOBER 31: Miguel Rojas #72 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts after Addison Barger #47 of the Toronto Blue Jays (not pictured) is forced out to win the game 3-1 in game six of the 2025 World Series at Rogers Center on October 31, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)
Throughout his big-league career, Rojas has posted 20.0 bWAR and a .677 OPS with 61 home runs and 386 RBI.
He has a career postseason OPS of .639 with two home runs and three RBI over 22 games.
Rojas had the most memorable moment of his career in Game 7 of last year’s World Series when he hit a game-tying home run off Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Jeff Hoffman in the ninth inning.
Dodgers-Brewers NLCS Schedule
- Game 1: 5:00 p.m. PDT on Sunday, Oct. 11 @ American Family Field
- Game 2: 2:00 p.m. PDT on Monday, Oct. 12 @ American Family Field
- Game 3: 5:00 p.m. PDT on Wednesday, Oct. 14 @ Dodger Stadium
- Game 4: 6:00 p.m. PDT on Thursday, Oct. 15 @ Dodger Stadium
- Game 5 (if necessary): 6:00 p.m. PDT on Friday, Oct. 16 @ Dodger Stadium
- Game 6 (if necessary): 5:00 p.m. PDT on Sunday, Oct. 18 @ American Family Field
- Game 7 (if necessary): 5:00 p.m. PDT on Sunday, Oct. 18 @ American Family Field
Games 1, 2 and 7 will be available to watch on FOX. The rest will be broadcast on FS1.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Edwin Díaz pitching like dominant closer Dodgers envisioned signing
item.dc:creator: Matt Borelli
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers finished off the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series behind a dominant effort from their pitching staff, which included Edwin Díaz recording his second save in as many days. Tasked with protecting the Dodgers’ 4-1 lead, Díaz retired all three batters faced on just eight pitches (seven strikes). He struck out Rowdy Tellez to begin the bottom of the ninth inning and then got Mauricio Dubón and Austin Riley to fly out. It was the latest encouragin
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers finished off the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series behind a dominant effort from their pitching staff, which included Edwin Díaz recording his second save in as many days.
Tasked with protecting the Dodgers’ 4-1 lead, Díaz retired all three batters faced on just eight pitches (seven strikes). He struck out Rowdy Tellez to begin the bottom of the ninth inning and then got Mauricio Dubón and Austin Riley to fly out.
It was the latest encouraging performance from Díaz, who has looked like a completely different pitcher since returning from the 15-day injured list at the end of the regular season.
“It’s great,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Edwin Díaz recording saves in back-to-back days. “He’s had a tough season. He’s been hurt. He was having trouble with his delivery and went on a long rehab assignment. But to get him pitching the way — that’s the reason why we got him.
“The last two nights, that’s the reason why we acquired a guy like Edwin Diaz. He’s one of the great closers in the game. For him to be pitching his best right now, that’s what you hope for, and I give him a lot of credit.”
Díaz finished the month of September on a high note by throwing five consecutive scoreless innings. He carried that momentum into the NLDS and did not allow a run in three appearances against the Braves.
“I feel great,” Díaz said of his recent success. “I’m happy with what I’m doing right now. I put in a lot of work this season. I went to the IL with elbow surgery. Came back, didn’t pitch the way everybody was expecting. Went back to IL with my neck. Then I started working on those things. Those things paid off at the end of the day.
“Last week and a half of the season, I did my job. The team trusts me. I think that was the most important thing for me, the team trusts me. They give me the ball every single day. And the last two nights it’s been amazing. That’s why I came here to win games and close games like this one. So I’m really happy right now.”
Edwin Díaz keeping focus on bigger picture
Díaz was happy to help the Dodgers eliminate the Braves, but quickly shifted the focus to the upcoming NL Championship Series and the team’s quest for a third consecutive World Series title.
“It was a great win,” Díaz said. “We came here with the goal to win the series in Atlanta, and we did it. Now we go back home but we have to still work, we have to put a lot of work together. Our goal is to win the World Series, not this the series. We’ve got eight more wins to go. So our goal is win those eight games. And at the end of the day, when we win those eight games, we celebrate.
“Now we’re going back to LA, keep working. I know all the guys are on the same track. Now we just celebrate a little bit, go back to L.A., get working and be ready for Sunday.”

item.content:encoded:
Max Muncy knows which Dodgers player had their bare butt exposed amid the team’s NLDS celebration.
But the Dodgers playoff legend refused to reveal the identity of said player. Instead, Muncy discussed a detail that shocked him about the now-viral video.
“I’m not gonna tell you who it was. I know who it was, but I’m not gonna tell you,” Muncy said.
Muncy asked Foul Territory’s AJ Pierzynski about the player’s fashion choice, beyond his bare butt.
“So, on that note, jockstraps with no sliders underneath?” Muncy said.
“That, to me, is one of the weirdest things about that is there’s no sliders underneath. This got way off topic real quick. Sorry about that one.”
While the Dodgers are all business on the field, fans can always count on some hilarious moments off the field from the star-studded roster. This October, it appears the viral butt cheek clip has taken the fan base by storm as the hilarious reactions from other players have also caused a stir on social media.
The Dodgers celebrated their NLDS victory over the Braves on Wednesday night, but their biggest task lies ahead. The NLCS matchup between the Dodgers and Brewers is slated to be one for the ages as both teams are deep in every facet.
Muncy is expected to play a big role for the Dodgers as the team chases its third consecutive World Series title. Against the Braves, Muncy hit his 19th postseason home run for the Dodgers, a franchise record.

item.content:encoded:
相手打者を寄せ付けない支配力が称賛を集めている。現地時間10月6日に行われたブレーブスとのナ・リーグ地区シリーズ第3戦に登板した山本由伸の投球だ。
【動画】えぐいキレ！山本由伸がスプリットで空振り三振を奪うシーンをチェック
勝った方が王手となる第3戦で、相手エースのクリス・セールとの投げ合い――。否が応でも緊張感が高まる舞台で28歳の日本人エースは真価を発揮した。「ヨシはやってくれる」（デーブ・ロバーツ監督談）と抜群の信頼を寄せられた先発マウンドに立った山本は、7回（98球）を投げ、10奪三振、1失点と好投。ドジャースが勝ち抜けを決めた同シリーズにおいて、流れをグッと手繰り寄せる勝利に貢献した。
2023年オフに大谷翔平を除いて投手史上最高額となる12年3億2500万ドル（約463億円＝当時のレート）の超大型契約を締結した山本。その価値を存分に示しているパフォーマンスには賛辞が止む気配はない。
そんな山本の投球はメジャーリーグの酸いも甘いも知る者たちの目にはどう映っているのだろうか。18年のキャリアを重ねた現役時代にMLBで通算200勝、そして2202奪三振を挙げた大投手のアダム・ウェインライト氏は、米野球専門YouTubeチャンネル『Foul Territory』において「今のヤマモトは時代を代表する投手の一人だ」と強調。昨秋のワールドシリーズで球界の常識を覆す“中0日連投”をやってのけた怪腕のタフネスをクローズアップした。
「あれは私の人生において見たことがない投球だった。これは投手をやったことがある人間以外には分からないだろうけど、ポストシーズンで先発した翌日は普通なら象に踏みつぶされたような感覚になるんだ。本当にそうなんだ。それなのにヤマモトは次の日も投げた。しかも、10年契約という重圧を背負いながらだ。そういうタフな姿をこのポストシーズンでも彼は見せている。もっと彼がどれだけ凄い勝負師なのかが広まるべきだ」
また、ドジャースOBで、現役時代にMLBで204勝を挙げた大投手のオーレル・ハーシュハイザー氏は、米スポーツ専門局『ESPN LA』の番組内で、山本の“ミスの少なさ”に言及した。
「彼は普段から制球が抜群だ。コントロールが優れていれば、4つ、あるいは5つの球種を使って打者の弱点をあらゆる攻め方ができる。ただ、私が特に感銘を受けるのは、内角へのストレートだ。ポストシーズンのような舞台で内角に投げるのはどんな投手でも多少なりとも怖さがある。一振りで仕留められる危険があるからね。メジャーリーグは誰にでもその力はある。でも、ヤマモトは重要な場面でこそ、際どい内角へのストレートを投げる。しかもミスなくね。本当に集中しきっていたんだ」
百戦錬磨の名投手たちがこぞって讃える山本。その現状からして一部で批判も頂戴した12年3億2500万ドルの契約の価値はあったと言えよう。
[文/構成:ココカラネクスト編集部]

item.title: [Sports Gazette] Max Muncy: The Dodgers Unsung Hero - Sports Gazette
item.dc:creator: Conner Rowntree
item.description: Muncy, the longest-tenured Dodger, joined the organization in 2017 on a minor league deal after being cut from the then-Oakland Athletics. item.content:encoded:
Muncy, the longest-tenured Dodger, joined the organization in 2017 on a minor league deal after being cut from the then-Oakland Athletics. The hard-hitting third baseman was called up to the Dodgers in 2018, and in less than a decade, Muncy went from nearly being out of baseball to cementing his legacy as an all-time great.
“I remember a guy that just got DFA’d that was sort of kicked to the curb by an organization that didn’t believe in him,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Muncy. “He was close to being out of baseball … He’s one of the leaders on our ballclub, the longest-tenured Dodger currently. So I just have nothing but praise.”
“The ability to kind of adapt, start, come off the bench and still [do] whatever it takes to help the team win — he’s all-in. He does everything you want as a manager, everything.”
When reflecting on almost being out of the game and facing an early forced retirement in 2016, Muncy broke down.
“Man, there’s a lot with that,” Muncy said. “It’s just a lot.”
Now, nine seasons later, the 36-year-old slugger is a three-time All-Star, Dodger Stadium home run leader, Dodgers playoff home run leader and three-time World Series champion. But “Mad Max” focuses on his team’s success, not personal accolades.
“There’s not much when it comes to me, personally, that I care about,” Muncy said. “But three rings is definitely what I [cherish] most.”
Although Muncy may not focus on his personal statistics, his teammates take notice, not just of the player he is, but the man under the uniform.
“To know that he’s now the Dodger [Stadium] all-time home run leader? Whatever it is … after being an older guy in Triple-A with me and then getting called up … special,” Dodgers reliever Brock Stewart said of Muncy.
“I don’t know if he always believed in himself, and I can relate to that, because I didn’t believe in myself all the time … But to see him and how he persevered through that feeling [or] that self-doubt and became what he is now [is] super special.”
Muncy’s clutch playoff performance has given the Dodgers a chance to win another ring and “Hunt History” by becoming the first National League team to win three consecutive World Series. That role matters even more with Shohei Ohtani slumping. The Dodgers superstar went just 2-for-13 at the plate in the Dodgers NLDS matchup against the Braves. If the Dodgers are going to have any success in the NLCS, especially with the highest-paid and unanimously best baseball player on the planet playing like he’s in pee-wee back in Oshu, Japan, they will need their unsung hero, and Muncy’s teammates know they can rely on him.
“He’s a guy that is always going to show up for the team and do whatever it takes to put the team in a good position,” says Dodger infielder Miguel Rojas.
“He’s a guy you always can root for, especially in this organization full of stars. He always gets [overlooked] a little bit, but I feel like he’s one of the leaders of this club, and he will be until he retires.”
The Dodgers now turn their attention to the MLB’s winningest team this season, the Milwaukee Brewers, and the NLCS. Last year, the Dodgers swept the Brewers en route to their second straight World Series title. This time around, however, the Brewers are confident it will be a different story.
“We’re now as rested as they are,” Brewers owner Mark Attanasio said. “Because last year, we had a very emotional win against the Cubs and a lot of celebrating afterward, and the next day we’re in batting practice. And now we have the same number of days off as they do, and have (Jacob) Misiorowski and (Logan) Henderson and all our pitchers rested.
“So it’s our best against their best, and that’s always fun.”
On the Dodgers side, Manager Dave Roberts gave his club a simple yet clear message after their Game 4, series-clinching win in Atlanta.
“Eight more wins. Stay focused. Everybody in this room helped get us to where we are and where we’re gonna go,” Roberts said to his team in the locker room.
“In the postseason, guys, you don’t know when the moment is gonna come to you. All of us gotta stay focused and get ready.”
If Max Muncy has proven anything during his Dodgers tenure, it’s that he’s ready to do whatever it takes for this team to win and make history. Game 1 of the NLCS is set for Monday in Milwaukee.

item.content:encoded:
米大リーグ（MLB）ロサンゼルス・ドジャースの選手のパートナーたちによる集まり「Dodgers Wives」が、公式インスタグラムを更新。大谷翔平選手の妻、真美子さんが10月3日と4日（いずれも現地時間）の投稿に連日登場し、その近影に注目が集まっている。
【比較写真】真美子さんの最新ショット！ 地区シリーズ第1戦、第2戦でコーデに違いも
MLBでは9月29日から、ポストシーズンが開幕。ドジャースは3日、アトランタ・ブレーブスとの地区シリーズ第1戦に臨んだ。
試合に際し、Dodgers Wivesは「1試合目！！ 私たちも全力で応援します」とつづり、選手のパートナーたちの集合ショットを公開。
1列目の左から2番目には、黒のノースリーブに白のパンツの真美子さんが写っていた。
真美子さんが公の場に姿を現したのは、大谷選手とともに出席した全米野球記者協会（BBWAA）ニューヨーク支部主催の夕食会（1月）以来、約8カ月ぶりのこと。
6月に第2子を出産してからは初めてとなる。
久しぶりに真美子さんの登場にファンが盛り上がるなか、Dodgers Wivesは翌4日、ブレーブスとの第2戦に際し、インスタグラムを更新。
またしてもパートナーたちの集合写真を公開したのだが、後列左端には、黒のTシャツを着た真美子さんの姿があった。
「待ってました！」「うあぁぁぁ、真美子さんだ」SNS反響
公の場に連日登場し、元気な様子を見せた真美子さんに、SNSでは
「待ってました！ 真美子さん！！」
「やっぱりいちばん目立ってますね！ お元気そうで何より」
「笑顔がとても素敵」
「真美子さん連日の応援、とても素晴らしい」
といった声が上がった。
また、海外ファンからも
「awhhh mamiko（＝うあぁぁぁ、真美子さんだ）」
「Mamikoooooooo（＝真美子さ〜〜〜ん）」
「Mamiko! So happy to see her（＝真美子さんだ！ 元気な姿が見られてとてもうれしい）」
「Mamiko looks so healthyyy（＝真美子さん、健康的で元気そう〜〜）」
など、注目する声が寄せられている。
BuzzFeed Japan

item.content:encoded:
El héroe del tercer juego de la Serie Divisional entre los Dodgers de Los Ángeles y los Bravos de Atlanta fue el cubano Andy Pagés, y en la conferencia de prensa posterior al desafío, el manager de los actuales campeones de la Serie Mundial, Dave Roberts, tuvo palabras de elogio para el nacido en el municipio de Mantua.
Roberts siempre ha apostado por Andy desde que lo subió a los Dodgers y ha sacado la mejor versión al máximo nivel, llevándolo a ser uno de los mejores jardineros centrales de todas las Grandes Ligas. Incluso cuando en 2025 no pasaba por un buen momento al inicio de la temporada, donde luego puso sus mejores números.
Dave Roberts elogió a Andy Pagés
«Nuestros muchachos simplemente siguen luchando, perseverando. Nunca sabes quién va a ser el protagonista. Esta noche Andy nos levantó enormemente con un gran hit», declaró a la prensa el polémico director, señalando a Pagés como el héroe del desafío. Esto dice mucho de la confianza que tiene en el antillano.
Hasta el momento, Andy ha pegado cuatro imparables en 14 turnos oficiales al bate, con dos remolques (los del miércoles), un boleto y cinco ponches. Su promedio de bateo es de .286, mientras que su porcentaje de embasado está en .333, con un slugging de .286 y un OPS de .619.
La Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional inicia este domingo en el American Family Field, casa de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Ese cotejo se repite del año pasado, donde los Dodgers salieron victoriosos por barrida para luego coronarse campeones de la Serie Mundial ante los Azulejos de Toronto.
