item.content:encoded:
El pinareño Andy Pagés fue el héroe del tercer juego de la Serie Divisional que dio el pase a la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional al conectar un cañonazo con las bases llenas para darle la ventaja a los Dodgers de Los Ángeles sobre los Bravos de Atlanta. Otra vez volvió a ser determinante en un momento clave, algo que se ha hecho habitual en su carrera.
Al finalizar el choque, Pagés ofreció sus declaraciones a la prensa presente en el Truist Park, donde conversó sobre la concentración que hay que tener en un momento tan importante, pese a que en los últimos meses ha estado lidiando con lesiones. No hay dudas de que, cuando está sano, es un jugador por encima de la media de la Liga. A continuación, la entrevista completa.
Entrevista de Andy Pages
P. Andy, ¿nos puedes describir ese turno al bate? Bases llenas, dos outs, conteo de 3-2, ¿es algo con lo que uno sueña desde niño?
ANDY PAGÉS: Me he estado preparando toda la serie para un momento así, darme una oportunidad, conseguir un buen lanzamiento para batear. Y por suerte pude dar un buen swing a un lanzamiento.
P. Cuando consigues ese hit, ¿cómo es ese momento? Estás parado en primera, el dugout se vuelve loco, ¿cómo es ese momento para ti?
ANDY PAGÉS: Obviamente es un momento muy emocionante. Muy feliz por el equipo en ese momento. Pero, sinceramente, lo único que tenía en mente era poner al equipo adelante, ponerles presión. Y nuestro bullpen, nuestro pitcheo, pudo hacer el trabajo y asegurar esta victoria.
P. Sé que todos ustedes saben cuál se supone que es el final, el objetivo final. Pero verlos poder celebrar y celebrarse entre ustedes, sé que no se vuelve aburrido, pero ¿cómo mantienes el interés en poder disfrutar el momento, sabiendo que el objetivo final es ganar el campeonato?
ANDY PAGÉS: Solo disfrutar el momento. Obviamente tenemos equipos grandes, series grandes por delante. Vamos a enfrentar equipos difíciles, así que prepararnos para esos momentos, pero también aprovechar la oportunidad de estar aquí y disfrutar estos momentos. Y sabiendo que nuestro objetivo final es ganar la Serie Mundial. Así que enfocarnos en eso.
Pagés pegó dos sencillos en tres turnos oficiales al bate para elevar su promedio ofensivo a .286, demostrando que ya está al ciento por ciento de sus capacidades físicas luego de la lesión. El cubano es una pieza clave tanto a la ofensiva como a la defensa en el equipo que comandó el polémico Dave Roberts.
Ahora resta esperar hasta el domingo, cuando empezará la Serie de Campeonato frente a los Cerveceros de Milwaukee, equipo más ganador de la temporada regular. Será una serie difícil y tendrán que lidiar en el primer choque con Jacob Misiorowski, en estos momentos uno de los mejores lanzadores de todas las Grandes Ligas.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers legend explains why Tarik Skubal trade means more in MLB playoffs
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers already knew Tarik Skubal could change their rotation. Now, a Dodgers legend has explained why the move could matter even more in October. Skubal was brought in from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline for a package that included top prospects Zyhir Hope, River Ryan and Brady Smith. The Dodgers did not make that investment simply to strengthen their regular-season rotation. They wanted another ace for the moments when every game carries significantly more weight. Tha
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers already knew Tarik Skubal could change their rotation. Now, a Dodgers legend has explained why the move could matter even more in October.
Skubal was brought in from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline for a package that included top prospects Zyhir Hope, River Ryan and Brady Smith. The Dodgers did not make that investment simply to strengthen their regular-season rotation. They wanted another ace for the moments when every game carries significantly more weight.
That value was on full display in the National League Division Series.
Tarik Skubal is built for the postseason stage
Skubal started Game 1 against the Atlanta Braves and delivered exactly what Los Angeles hoped to get when it made the trade.
The left-hander allowed one run and two hits over six innings while striking out seven. He also retired 15 consecutive hitters at one point, helping the Dodgers take a 5-3 victory and an early series lead.
The Dodgers eventually finished off Atlanta in four games, advancing to the NL Championship Series.
That is where the importance of the Skubal trade becomes clearer.
Los Angeles already had talented arms, but postseason baseball can expose even the deepest rotation. A starter who can take the ball in Game 1 and immediately settle a series gives a team something that regular-season depth cannot fully measure.
Sep 19, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) reacts after giving up a walk to the San Francisco Giants in the during the second inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Skubal's first season with Los Angeles has backed up that idea. He went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts in 10 regular-season starts for the Dodgers.
Now the stakes are even higher.
The Dodgers will face Milwaukee after the Brewers finished the regular season with an MLB-best 103-59 record. The series is a rematch of last year's NLCS, and Skubal is in line to face Misiorowski in Sunday's opener if both teams follow their expected rotation plans.
That is precisely why Los Angeles surrendered so much prospect capital for Skubal.
The Dodgers did not need another good regular-season pitcher. They needed someone capable of taking the ball when the margin for error disappears.
After his Game 1 performance against Atlanta, Skubal has already shown that the trade can pay off where it matters most. Now he gets another chance to prove it with a trip to the World Series on the line.

item.content:encoded:
Ladies and gentlemen, we’ve got ourselves a rematch.
Just like last year, Shohei Ohtani’s Los Angeles Dodgers and Christian Yelich’s Milwaukee Brewers are meeting in the NLCS.
And, once again, Pat Murphy’s club has home-field advantage. Games 1, 2, 6 and 7 will be at American Family Field in Milwaukee, WI.
Not everything about this Series is the same, though.
“I think it is different this year. … We’re going in to beat them,” Murphy told Fox Sports, referring to his team getting swept in 2025. “We earned it in the regular season to get home-field advantage. We’re going in to beat them, we don’t care who they have.”
If you’d like to be there to see if the Brew Crew really have what it takes to dethrone the defending World Series champion Dodgers, tickets are available for all four hypothetical contests in the Cream City.
At the time of publication, the lowest price we could find on seats for any one game in Milwaukee was $224 including fees on Vivid Seats.
Prices start at $144 including fees for fans hoping to attend a showdown at Dodger Stadium.
Ahead of the NLCS, Milwaukee battled with San Diego in a tense, back-and-forth four-game NLDS that saw instantly iconic moments like a clutch Jackson Chourio catch in Game 1, a Jackson Chourio walk-off single in Game 2 and Garrett Mitchell robbing Manny Machado of a home run in Game 4.
As for the Dodgers, the club continued their winning ways in the postseason [Editor’s Note: They haven’t lost a playoff series since the Diamondbacks beat them in the 2023 NLDS] and beat up on the formidable Braves.
Kiké Hernández smashed a home run — the 17th postseason dinger of his career, putting him ahead of Babe Ruth (!) on the all-time list — in the decisive fourth game and stellar offensive performances from Andy Pages and Max Muncy.
We can’t wait to see what comes next.
For more information, our team has everything you need to know and more about the Dodgers vs. Brewers 2026 NLCS below.

A complete breakdown of all the best prices on tickets for every hypothetical game at Milwaukee’s American Family Field can be found here:

For fans who prefer to watch on the tube, you can catch this nervy series on FOX and FS1.
Both providers listed above can be found on the one-stop shop known as DIRECTV.

Fans hoping to get a concert or three in this year too are in luck.
After a bit of digging, we found that many of the biggest names in music will be on the road this year and next.

Who else is out and about? Take a look at this list of all the biggest rockers on tour in 2026 to find the show for you.

Levy stays up-to-date on all the latest tour announcements from your favorite musical artists and comedians, as well as Broadway openings, sporting events and more live shows – and finds great ticket prices online. item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers will have time to reset rotation, bullpen, and struggling Shohei Ohtani for NLCS

item.description: ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5. By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5.
By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game.
"It's important. It was very important," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Once you get to an elimination game, a Game 5 or a Game 7, anything can happen. And to be able to win today, get back, reset, have a day off tomorrow, set the rotation, it's huge."
The extra rest means Tarik Skubal likely will be the choice to start against Milwaukee instead of handling a Game 5 against the Braves. Similarly, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow will be well rested for their expected NLCS starts.
Infielder Miguel Rojas may need the extra rest for a sore lower back that kept him out.
Also, Edwin Díaz will have ample time to reset after recording saves on back-to-back days to close out the series against Atlanta. The ninth-inning work showed Díaz is re-established as the closer.
"The team trusts me," Díaz said. "I think that was the most important thing for me, the team trusts me. They give me the ball every single day. And the last two nights it's been amazing. That's why I came here to win games and close games like this one. So I'm really happy right now."
Despite those advantages, Roberts is preparing for a tough NLCS as the Dodgers try to move closer to their goal of becoming the first NL team to win three consecutive World Series.
"We've got our work cut out," Roberts said, adding extra rest also will be important for such players as Ohtani and Freddie Freeman.
Ohtani was 2 for 13 against Atlanta and hasn't homered since Aug. 18 while dealing with injuries to his right biceps, left knee and neck that have also kept the two-way player off the mound.
"So kind of enjoy this one, get Shohei a couple of days to get back," Roberts said. "Freddie, he had a big series, but, again a couple of days will help him. Give our guys in the 'pen a little reset. So we'll be ready to go Game 1."
Díaz pitched a perfect ninth inning in the clinching win. The on-field celebration was a low-key affair, but Roberts and his players, wearing "Take October" T-shirts and goggles to protect their eyes, soon were drenched with champagne.
The Dodgers made the most of their opportunity to celebrate another postseason series win while maintaining their focus on a third straight World Series championship.
"Our goal is to win the World Series, not this series," Díaz said. "We've got eight more wins to go. So our goal is win those eight games. And at the end of the day when we win those eight games, we celebrate.
"Now we're going back to LA to keep working. I know all the guys are on the same track. Now we just celebrate a little bit, go back to LA, get working and be ready for Sunday."
Andy Pages' bases-loaded single in the seventh drove in two runs to give the Dodgers a 3-1 lead. Max Muncy added to the lead with a homer in the ninth, his third blast of the postseason.
"Obviously, we have big teams, big series coming up," Pages said. "We're going to face tough teams, so prepare for those moments, but also take advantage of the opportunity of being here and enjoying these moments. And knowing that our ultimate goal is to win the World Series. So focus on that."

item.title: [Sodo Mojo] Return of prime Edwin Díaz is Mariners fans' most confusing playoff rooting interest
item.dc:creator: Paul Taylor
item.description: At times, it's been suggested that Edwin Díaz almost looks like Stephen A. Smith. That's where any resemblance ends though, with Smith traditionally known for being a lot more controversial and polarizing. Now though, Díaz might be finding himself perceived somewhat similarly to the ESPN personality, particularly by the Mariners fanbase. The majority of baseball fans in Seattle remember Díaz fondly as the electric closer who led the majors with 57 saves in 2018, tied for second-most in MLB histo
item.content:encoded:
At times, it's been suggested that Edwin Díaz almost looks like Stephen A. Smith. That's where any resemblance ends though, with Smith traditionally known for being a lot more controversial and polarizing. Now though, Díaz might be finding himself perceived somewhat similarly to the ESPN personality, particularly by the Mariners fanbase.
The majority of baseball fans in Seattle remember Díaz fondly as the electric closer who led the majors with 57 saves in 2018, tied for second-most in MLB history. The 32-year-old was also selected as an All-Star for the first time and named AL Reliever of the Year. It was a shame when he was traded to the Mets following the season, as part of a blockbuster deal to get Robinson Canó and the remaining half of his 10-year, $240 million salary off the books and begin a full rebuild.
The point is that Díaz was not viewed as a villain in Seattle; it's not like he chose to get traded to the Mets. Sure, the whole deal didn't work out particularly well for the Mariners, specifically with Jarred Kelenic as the can't-miss top-rated prospect who did in fact miss. However, none of this was exactly Díaz's fault and yet now, M's fans must be feeling conflicted about whether to cheer for him or not in the playoffs.
The three-time Reliever of the Year has experienced a renaissance in the playoffs, but with the Dodgers of all teams. That's right, the same Dodgers who have taken over the mantle from the Yankees as the Evil Empire. The same Dodgers who spend as if there's no tomorrow and are taking aim at becoming just the third team in Major League history to win three consecutive World Series championships.
Under any other circumstances, Mariners fans would be cheering Edwin Díaz's resurgence
This was a rough year for Díaz, who was limited to 14 appearances due to dealing with right elbow loose bodies and then neck inflammation. Unsurprisingly this impacted his performances when he did pitch, as highlighted by an eye-bulging 8.68 ERA and 1.982 WHIP in those 14 appearances, spanning 18.2 innings. It was tough not to feel bad for him, despite being a member of the Dodgers.
Now though all bets are off, especially in Seattle, after Díaz turned things around following the return from his second stint on the Injured List this year. Since then, he's had eight straight scoreless appearances, in the process allowing just two hits and producing 12 Ks. Worst of all from a Mariners fan perspective, the three-time All-Star saved two games in the Dodgers' NLDS versus the Braves, including the clincher on Wednesday night in Atlanta:
It's bad enough that no one really wanted Díaz to leave Seattle in the first place, although objectively speaking we can understand why the Mariners did it at the time. It was probably the assumption he would burn out, and that it was a good idea to sell high and offload Cano's contract. With everything the righty has achieved since, it tells you the M's didn't know what they had, although we acknowledge this is being stated with that wonderful benefit of hindsight.
Irrespective, this whole situation feels a little weird. Sure, Mariners fans want to root for Díaz as an individual, with many happy he has bounced back from a challenging regular season. However, to see him playing a significant role in the Dodgers' postseason run makes it both frustrating and confusing. In fairness the M's fanbase is more than used to dealing with such emotions, but it doesn't make it any less painful.

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers in beating the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday night to close out the National League Division Series in four games improved their record under Dave Roberts to 19-9 (.689) with a chance to close out a postseason series. The rest of MLB since 2016 is 92-88 (.511) in such games.
Wednesday’s win was also the 72nd career postseason win for Roberts, surpassing Tony La Russa for second-most in MLB history.
“It’s special,” Roberts said on Monday night in Atlanta. “I have a lot of respect for Tony and the managers that have done what I’m doing; they’ve done it for a long time.”
Roberts is now a dozen wins behind Joe Torre for the most postseason wins ever.
Roberts has done all this in 11 seasons at the helm of the Dodgers, and his 11th season isn’t finished yet. Torre managed a total of 29 seasons in the majors, though 76 of his 84 postseason wins came in his dozen years with the New York Yankees.
Modern managers have more opportunities to amass postseason wins, with both the wild card round and Division Series. Plus, League Championship Series before 1985 were only best-of-5 instead of best-of-7, making in harder for earlier managers to pile up the October victories. So here is every MLB manager with at least 30 postseason wins, broken down by series.
| Manager | Postseason wins | World Series | LCS | Division Series | Wild Card |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Joe Torre | 84 | 21 | 29 | 34 | |
| Dave Roberts | 72 | 16 | 24 | 27 | 5 |
| Tony La Russa | 71 | 13 | 34 | 24 | |
| Bobby Cox | 67 | 11 | 30 | 26 | |
| Dusty Baker | 57 | 9 | 21 | 25 | 2 |
| Bruce Bochy | 57 | 16 | 20 | 17 | 4 |
| Terry Francona | 44 | 11 | 15 | 16 | 2 |
| Jim Leyland | 44 | 5 | 16 | 23 | |
| Casey Stengel | 37 | 37 | | | |
| A.J. Hinch | 36 | 7 | 9 | 15 | 5 |
| Sparky Anderson | 34 | 16 | 18 | | |
| Joe Maddon | 32 | 5 | 9 | 16 | 2 |
| Tommy Lasorda | 31 | 12 | 16 | 3 | |
| Joe McCarthy | 30 | 30 | | | |
All of Casey Stengel’s 37 wins came in the World Series, and the same for Joe McCarthy’s 30 wins in the Fall Classic.
If we look at a more modern era, since the League Championship Series has been around since 1969, here are the most postseason wins in just the World Series and LCS combined:
- Joe Torre 50 wins
- Tony La Russa 47 wins
- Bobby Cox 41 wins
- Dave Roberts 40 wins
- Casey Stengel 37 wins
- Bruce Bochy 36 wins
- Sparky Anderson 34 wins

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are headed to the National League Championship Series for the third straight season.
After defeating the Atlanta Braves in four games, the Dodgers will head to Milwaukee to take on the Brewers for a 2nd straight season and potentially advance to the World Series.
LA picked up a 4-1 win over the Braves to advance on Wednesday evening, and immediately following the win, Edwin Diaz, who picked up the save, sent out a 4-word message on social media.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Next Opponent: Who Does LA Play in the NLCS?
Edwin Diaz Sends Message After Advancing to the NLCS
When the Dodgers inked Edwin Diaz to the largest contract for a reliever in MLB history, it was to close out games in October, and considering Diaz picked up saves in both Game Three and Four of the NLDS, it's safe to say he's the team's closer once again.
Via X.com, he had this message to relay after the postgame celebration on Wednesday evening:
@SugarDiaz39: "NLCS LETS GOOO DODGERS"
Edwin Diaz is fired up to be one step away from the World Series, as should the rest of the team.
Diaz struggled for much of the regular season and also battled injuries, but since returning from the IL in late September, he has been lights out.
More MLB on Heavy: Ronald Acuña Jr. Off-Field News Surfaces After Braves-Dodgers NLDS
Looking at Edwin Diaz's First Season with the Los Angeles Dodgers
Edwin Diaz has thrown three innings during the MLB playoffs, and he has yet to allow a run on just one hit allowed and three strikeouts.
During the regular season, Diaz posted an ERA of 8.68 over 18.2 innings.
As noted, the Dodgers inked Diaz to such a lucrative contract to show up when it matters in October, and the 3X All-Star has clearly done that thus far.
Diaz has not allowed a run in his last eight relief outings.
More MLB on Heavy: Kike Hernandez Making MLB History Shouldn't Surprise Los Angeles Dodgers Fans

item.title: [New York Post] Andy Pages’ NLDS heroics for Dodgers were a year in the making
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA – This was never about redemption.
Or so Andy Pages said.
“I don’t even think of what happened last year,” Pages said in Spanish. “What happened, happened.”
The way Pages viewed it, his miserable offensive performance on the Dodgers’ World Series run last year wasn’t something for which he had to make up.
The experience, Pages said, made him the player he is now.
The player he is now drove in the runs that sank the Atlanta Braves on Wednesday night and sent the Dodgers on their way to a 4-1 victory in Game 4 of their National League Division Series.
“Tonight,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said, “Andy picked us up huge with a big hit.”
The best-of-five series over, Pages walked around the visiting clubhouse at Truist Field in a commemorative gray shirt that was soaked with cheap sparkling wine and beer. A pair of goggles covered his forehead.
“Special,” he said. “Special.”
The journey here started a year ago, when Pages batted just .078 in the postseason. By Game 5 of the World Series, he was on the bench.
But Pages said he considers that World Series to be a wonderful memory, and not just because he made a game-saving catch in Game 7 as a defensive replacement.
“Because we won,” he said.
And rather than sulk over not starting the last three games of the World Series, Pages decided to use his failures to guide his training.
To be the kind of player who could be trusted in big games, Pages figured, he had to become a more selective hitter.
Improving his eye by stepping in against an artificial pitching machine called a Trajekt Arc, Pages made his first All-Star team this year.
A broken hand in late August nearly derailed his season, but Pages did what he could to remain sharp. Before he was able to swing a bat again, Pages was stepping in against the Trajekt Arc again.
Pages returned for the final week of the regular season and batted .333, which is why what happened next was shocking.
In the first two games of the NLDS, Pages was a combined 0-for-7. What was worse than the numbers was how he looked. He looked lost. He looked desperate.
Pages’ ABS challenge privileges were revoked after a particularly unwise effort to turn a called strike into a ball.
At this point, manager Dave Roberts acknowledged he was concerned.
However, Roberts said, “This is one of those things where I’m gonna continue to give Andy leash. I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re gonna need him to be an active part of our team.”
Pages rewarded Roberts with a two-hit performance in the Dodgers’ Game 3 win.
In Game 4, Pages stepped into the batter’s box with the game on the line.
Seventh inning. Two outs. Bases loaded. Game tied, 1-1. Fireballer Ryan Suarez on the mound.
Pages worked a full count.
Suarez threw him a 99.7-mph fastball on the inner half of the plate and Pages banged it up the middle.
Two runs scored, and the Dodgers were suddenly ahead, 3-1.
“I was waiting for that moment,” Pages said. “I prepared a long time for that moment, and thanks to God I was able to get the result.”
He prepared for the moment. He dreamed of the moment.
But he didn’t try to visualize it.
“I think that when you think too much about something, it doesn’t happen,” he said. “You have to let things happen.”
Did he ever.
Redemption, evolution, call it whatever you want.
Pages finally had his October moment in the batter’s box.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: He finally did it! Dodgers' Andy Pages ends two-year postseason slump at the perfect time

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
He pounded his chest twice as he left the batter’s box, and all of Dodgers nation rocked to the beat.
Andy Pages did it. He finally did it. He finally broke out of his baffling two-year October slump with a hit so powerful, he didn’t even have to climb over Kiké Hernández to get it.
How powerful? With one smooth swing he broke a tie by scoring two runs while sending two teams packing, the Atlanta Braves trudging home for the winter and the Dodgers charging into the National League Championship Series.
Yeah, it was a blast, both figuratively and literally, Pages’ two-out, two-strike bases-loaded single in the seventh inning Wednesday night silencing the lame tomahawk-chopping fans at Truist Park and giving the Dodgers an eventual clinching 4-1 victory against the Braves in the National League Division Series.
Certainly, it only gets tougher from here. In winning this best-of-five series three games to one, the Dodgers can now prepare for a best-of-seven showdown task against either the mighty Milwaukee Brewers or blazing San Diego Padres.
Yes, they will need to hit better, they will need Blake Snell to find his focus, they will need Shohei Ohtani to show up.
But…Andy Pages! Seriously! If a guy who was seven for 66 in the last two postseasons and was so helpless last year he was benched for the last three games of the World Series…if that guy can drive in the winning run from the bottom of the order? The once-fallible Dodgers may just be unbeatable.
“There’s no more talented team than the Los Angeles Dodgers,” manager Dave Roberts shouted in the postgame clubhouse. “We’re the best organization in sports, top to bottom. We’re smarter, we’re better, and we’re tougher.”
At that point, someone referenced a recent comment from Padres owner José E. Feliciano insinuating that the Dodgers, baseball’s oldest team, was composed of dinosaurs.
“And we’re dinosaurs!” shouted a voice above the clubhouse din.
If they’re dinosaurs, their first initial is “T” and their last name is ‘Rex.”
It’s OK to start seriously thinking about a three-peat now. They’re now just eight wins away but, given how mediocre the American League playoff teams appear, they could realistically be just four wins away.
Andy Pages comes through in the seventh inning to break a tie and four relievers close out a 3-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves to win the NLDS in four games.
Here’s guessing that the NLCS will be the real World Series. And here’s guessing the Dodgers will be ready.
Pages, who won the hearts of Dodger fans last October when he made a leaping game-saving catch over the back of Kiké Hernández, was granted his first big October swing thanks to the Braves largess.
In the seventh inning of a 1-all tie, Teoscar Hernández redeemed himself for another fielding blunder with a single that finally drove dizzying Tyler Mahle from the game.
In came Game 2 rookie sensation Didier Fuentes, only this time, he was all rookie and zero sensation, walking Josue De Paula and Kyle Tucker to load the bases. Considering De Paula is just a kid and Tucker has been struggling, the fact that both showed such patience in such a pressure situation was pretty cool. And moments later, it got even cooler.
In came veteran reliever Robert Suarez, and Pages was ready for him, working the count full before lining the two-run single up the middle.
The Dodgers added a run two innings later on a Max Muncy home run — has there ever been a playoff game when he hasn’t homered? — to finalize the score.
When the game ended on an Austin Riley fly out to right field, Pages celebrated in center field by taking off his cap, turning his face to the sky and pounding the cap three times into his glove.
It was a series that was worth the emotion, the Dodgers famous starting rotation giving up just four runs in 21 ⅓ innings, the bullpen solid behind a revived Edwin Díaz, and the offense doing just enough to beat Braves aces Chris Sale and Mahle.
In the fifth inning of a tie game, starter Tyler Glasnow issued walks to Riley and Michael Harris II. With two out, in came Alex Vesia. Up stepped slugger Matt Olson. The fans climbed to their feet. This was the Braves’ big chance.
But Olson swung at the first pitch and lined it directly to second baseman Kiké Hernández to end the threat and quiet the joint. Díaz threw a hitless ninth for his second save of the series and…who’s going to beat them?
Afterward, Roberts referenced nearly half of his team when talking about his pride. He talked about Pages’ hit, about De Paula’s walk, about reliever Edgardo Henriquez’s 1 ⅔ shutout innings, about Muncy’s bat and Freddie Freeman’s glove
“I guess, amazement,” he said. “Our guys just continue to fight, persevere. You never know who the guy’s going to be.”
The only glaring weakness was, once again, the superstar who used to be their strength. Ohtani scored the Dodgers’ first run after drawing a walk but went hitless in three ensuing at-bats. He only got two hits in the four-game series and you have to wonder if his injury-wracked body would be better out of the lineup.
How well are they playing without the full services of their most historic player? On the verge of making history, the Dodgers don’t even miss him.

item.content:encoded:
8 de octubre de 2026 - 9:55 PM
Atlanta - Andy Pages impulsó dos carreras con un sencillo con las bases llenas en la séptima entrada para darle la ventaja definitiva a Los Ángeles, y los reinante bicampeones Dodgers vencieron el miércoles 4-1 a los Braves de Atlanta para sentenciar su serie divisional de la Liga Nacional.
Los Dodgers ganaron juegos consecutivos en Atlanta para llevarse 3-1 la serie al mejor de cinco y avanzar a la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional dentro de empeño por convertirse en el primer equipo de la Liga Nacional que conquista tres Series Mundiales seguidas.
El cubano Pages conectó una línea por el centro a un lanzamiento en cuenta de 3-2 del venezolano Robert Suárez para remolcar al dominicano Teoscar Hernández, quien había empalmado un sencillo ante el abridor Tyler Mahle, y al corredor emergente Tommy Edman, para poner el 3-1 en el marcador 3-1.
Acto seguido, el colombiano Didier Fuentes concedió base por bolas al bateador emergente dominicano Josue De Paula y a Kyle Tucker para congestionar las bases. Edman corrió por De Paula.
El jonrón solitario de Max Muncy ante el cubano Raisel Iglesias en la novena aumentó la ventaja y dejó al toletero con un gran total de 19 cuadrangulares de postemporada con los Dodgers, ampliando su récord de la franquicia.
El derecho de los Dodgers Tyler Glasnow, en su primera apertura desde el 24 de septiembre, permitió apenas un hit, pero otorgó cinco bases por bolas en cuatro innings y dos tercios.
Después de conceder dos boletos en la quinta, el zurdo Alex Vesia terminó la entrada con un rodado de Matt Olson a la segunda base.
La oportunidad desperdiciada dejó a los Braves con 18 pasaporte en la serie, pero ninguno se concretó en carrera.
Glasnow y cuatro relevistas se combinaron para permitir apenas tres hits. Tanner Scott lanzó una octava entrada perfecta antes de que el puertorriqueño Edwin “Sugar” Díaz sacara tres outs rápidos para apuntarse el salvamento.
Fue el segundo salvamento en noches consecutivas para Díaz, de vuelta en el puesto de cerrador de los Dodgers.
Mahle, originario de Newport Beach, California, y que creció como aficionado de los Dodgers, permitió dos carreras —una limpia— en seis innings y un tercio.
Michael Harris II conectó el primer lanzamiento de Glasnow para un sencillo antes de robarse la segunda y, finalmente, anotar desde tercera con un lanzamiento descontrolado que rebotó en el protector de pecho del receptor Will Smith.
Los Dodgers empataron en la segunda con ayuda de dos errores de Atlanta. Shohei Ohtani recibió base por bolas, se robó la segunda y avanzó a tercera por un tiro desviado del receptor Sean Murphy hacia el jardín central. El elevado de Muncy a la zona corta del jardín izquierdo fue dejado caer por el campocorto hondureño Mauricio Dubón para otro error, lo que permitió que Ohtani anotara.
Hernández se estrelló contra la pared al intentar atrapar el doble de Ozzie Albies ante Vesia para abrir la sexta. Hernández se señaló la cabeza y el cuello al hablar con un preparador físico, pero se mantuvo en el juego.
El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez dejó varado a Albies en segunda. Henríquez permitió un hit al cubrir una entrada y dos tercios sin carrera para llevarse la victoria.
Las noticias explicadas de forma sencilla y directa para entender lo más importante del día.

item.content:encoded:
Oct 7, 2026, 10:01 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz picked up his second save in as many nights on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with a strikeout in his team's 4-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series. Diaz missed most of the 2026 regular season due to elbow and neck injuries. However, he's been dominant since returning from the injured list in mid-September. Diaz allowed just two baserunners while notching nine strikeouts in his final five innings pitched of the regular season, and he's now logged low-stress saves in each of his first two appearances of the playoffs. With Diaz rounding into form, Los Angeles' bullpen looks like a major strength heading into the National League Championship Series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
More Recent News
Oct 7, 2026, 9:52 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians left-hander Foster Griffin was dominant in a bulk relief appearance in his team's 9-3 win over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Griffin followed Cleveland opener Daniel Espino and allowed two hits and one earned run while striking out seven across 2 2/3 innings of work. The 31-year-old was used exclusively as a starting pitcher during the regular season, posting a 15-6 record with a 3.60 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, and 158 strikeouts across 172 2/3 innings (31 starts) split between the Guardians and the Washington Nationals. However, Griffin struggled mightily late in the year, pitching to a 5.05 ERA in the second half and a 6.87 ERA across 18 1/3 innings in September. If Griffin can rediscover his early-season form in a bullpen role, he could help Cleveland mount a comeback in the ALDS.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians outfielder Jo Adell had a big night in his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, going two-for-four with a walk and three RBI. With the game tied 1-1 in the third inning, Adell put the Guardians ahead for good with a three-run triple off of White Sox left-hander Hagen Smith. Across 660 regular-season plate appearances split between the Guardians and the Los Angeles Angels, Adell hit .240/.298/.401 with 23 home runs, 94 RBI, 70 runs scored, and five stolen bases. He was better with Cleveland than he was with Los Angeles, posting a .740 OPS across 204 trips to the plate after the Guardians acquired him at the trade deadline. Adell has notched a couple of key hits for Cleveland in the ALDS and now has four RBI across the first three games of the series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:32 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages had the key hit in his team's 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday, logging a go-ahead two-run single off Braves right-hander Robert Suarez in the seventh inning. Pages finished the game with two hits and two RBI in three at-bats. The 25-year-old was a critical piece of the Dodgers lineup during the regular season, hitting .274 with 23 home runs, 85 RBI, 75 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases. However, Pages struggled mightily during the Dodgers' run to the 2025 World Series, notching just four hits in 55 postseason plate appearances. After his big night on Wednesday, Pages has already logged four hits in just 15 plate appearances in the 2026 playoffs.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:19 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians right-hander Cade Smith was lights out to secure his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Smith entered the game in the eighth inning and recorded the final six outs, logging five strikeouts without allowing a single baserunner. The 27-year-old was one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, pitching to a 1.95 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 107 strikeouts and 41 saves across 74 innings (69 games). Smith has been dominant so far in the Division Series as well, as he's yet to allow a hit or a walk in his four innings of work. If Cleveland is going to mount a comeback in the series, it will likely need Smith to continue his dominance.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:11 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez was one of the stars of his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series. In five plate appearances, Ramirez recorded a double, a triple, a walk, two RBI, two runs scored, and a stolen base. With Cleveland leading 5-3 in the 8th inning, it was Ramirez's two-run triple that sealed the win for the Guardians and kept the series alive to see Game 4. The 34-year-old battled through injuries and underperformance in 2026, hitting .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs, 53 RBI, 71 runs scored, and 37 stolen bases across 544 plate appearances. Ramirez also got off to a slow start in the postseason, going hitless in his first eight trips to the plate against the White Sox. If Cleveland is going to rally all the way back from two games down in the ALDS, it will need Ramirez to stay hot in Games 4 and 5.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Robert Gasser Starting Game 4 of NLDS Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:08 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser will start for the Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres, according to Brewers reporter Sophia Minnaert. It will be Gasser's first career postseason start after throwing 2 2/3 innings of relief in the playoffs for the Brew Crew last year. The 27-year-old southpaw went 5-5 on the season with a 3.87 ERA (4.24 FIP) and 1.19 WHIP with a career-high 103 strikeouts and 35 walks in 109 1/3 innings across 21 appearances (20 starts). The problem for Gasser is that he has not made a start in almost two weeks, so he could be a bit rusty. Manager Pat Murphy will surely have a short hook on the young left-hander as the Brewers look to close the best-of-five series out in San Diego. Gasser was outstanding down the stretch in 2026, allowing two earned runs or fewer in each of his last six starts, walking 12 and striking out 31 in 32 1/3 innings during that span. He did not face the Padres at all during the regular season, which could give him a bit of an advantage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Sophia Minnaert
Mason Miller Back From the Paternity List for Game 4


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:03 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced on Wednesday that they returned right-handed closer Mason Miller from the paternity list, taking the place on the National League Division Series roster of left-handed reliever Wandy Peralta. Miller blew a two-inning save in Game 2 of the series in Milwaukee against the Brewers and was then unavailable for the win in Game 3 at Petco Park on Tuesday night. It is great news for the Padres, who did not have left-handed high-leverage reliever Adrian Morejon on Tuesday due to a left-shoulder issue. The Padres had to go to Game 1 starter, right-hander Michael King, for the two-inning save with both Miller and Morejon unavailable. It is uncertain if Morejon will be able to pitch late in the game in another must-win contest on Wednesday in Game 4, but the Padres will at least have their stud closer back in the fold. The two-time All-Star was lights-out during the regular season, his first full season with the Friars, posting a 1.67 ERA (1.17 FIP), 0.900 WHIP, a career-high and league-high 38 saves, a career-high 129 strikeouts, and 26 walks in just 70 innings pitched. With their season on the line, expect manager Craig Stammen to be aggressive in his usage of Miller if Game 4 is close in the later innings, even though he showed command issues in the ninth on Sunday in Milwaukee.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Miguel Rojas Not Worried About Back/Hip Injury


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 12:28 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back, hip) said he felt some tightness in his left lower-back/hip area during a swing in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday against the hosting Atlanta Braves before he was pulled mid at-bat, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. However, Rojas was not concerned about his availability for the rest of the series and going forward. Rojas probably will not be in the Dodgers' starting lineup for Game 4 of the series on Wednesday at Truist Park against Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle, but it sounds like he should be available off the bench. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder has made two starts so far in the NLDS against the Braves and has gone 1-for-4 with a double and a strikeout. He was hitless in three at-bats with a strikeout in Tuesday's Game 3 win before being replaced at second base by Tommy Edman. Rojas has mostly been a bench player for the Dodgers in his 13th year in the league (fourth with L.A.) in 2026, but he proved in last year's World Series that he is still capable of coming through in the clutch when needed. He hit .267 (60-for-225) with four homers and 23 RBI during the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Oct 7, 2026, 11:57 AM ET
St. Louis Cardinals right-handed closer Riley O'Brien was a first-time All-Star in 2026 in his first full season as the team's closer, and he ended the year tied with San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller for the National League lead in saves (38) with a 4.08 ERA across a career-high 64 innings pitched. O'Brien also set a career high in appearances (66) in his first full year as a big-leaguer. He did not allow an earned run in his first 13 appearances of the year and ended the first half with a 3.43 ERA and a 7.9% walk rate in 39 1/3 frames. O'Brien had 24 saves in his first 28 opportunities. But in 27 appearances after the All-Star break, O'Brien had a 5.11 ERA in 24 2/3 innings, and his walk rate rose to 14.4% while he went 14-for-18 in save chances. Three of his blown saves in the second half came in September, and five of his losing decisions came in his final 13 outings. The 31-year-old said he experienced "fatigue" in the closing days of the season and that his legs have "been feeling heavy compared to how they felt early in the year," according to Daniel Guerrero of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. As he tired, the velocity of O'Brien's pitches suffered. To be able to maintain velocity through the entire season, O'Brien said he plans to focus on putting on "as much muscle as I can."--Keith Hernandez
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Daniel Guerrero
Curtis Mead the Favorite to Start at Second Base Next Year


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Boston Red Sox infielder Curtis Mead is considered the favorite to open next season as the team's starting second baseman, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline this summer, but he ended up playing in only one game for Boston due to a fractured wrist that he suffered in his second at-bat with the team. The 25-year-old will now have all offseason to heal up, and he will enter spring training as the team's primary option at the keystone as they attempt to get back to the playoffs in 2027. The Australian native was having a breakout 2026 campaign with the Nationals before being traded to Boston, and he finished the year with a .253/.353/.498 slash line with an .851 OPS, 17 home runs, 48 RBI, 49 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 285 at-bats in 88 combined games with Washington and Boston. "That would be, I would say, broadly our plan," said manager Chad Tracy when asked about second base. "He was acquired for a reason. You see the numbers that kind of project at least toward a 30-home run season. And adding that, we were really excited about that."--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Walker Buehler to Start Game 4 of NLDS Against Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:36 AM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that veteran right-hander Walker Buehler will make the start in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers. Buehler will make his first postseason appearance this year after going 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA (4.51 FIP) and 1.35 WHIP with 131 strikeouts and 57 walks in 153 2/3 innings pitched across his 32 starts for the Padres in his first season with the team. The 32-year-old is no longer the high-end ace that he was with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he does have plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA (3.21 FIP) with 114 strikeouts and 36 walks in 94 2/3 innings pitched. Buehler's last start came on Sept. 26 against the division-rival Arizona Diamondbacks, when he allowed four runs (three earned) with a walk and three strikeouts in just 3 2/3 innings for a no-decision. He picked up a win in his only outing against Milwaukee in 2026, giving up just one earned run with two walks and five strikeouts in six innings at Petco Park back on Aug. 11. Buehler will most definitely be on a short leash in a must-win game for San Diego if he is not on his game early on.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Padres PR
Adrian Morejon Dealing With "Stickiness in his Shoulder"


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
San Diego Padres left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon (shoulder) was unavailable in Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on Tuesday night against the Milwaukee Brewers due to "stickiness in his shoulder," manager Craig Stammen told AJ Cassavell of MLB.com. There is still a chance that Morejon will be available for Game 4 against the Brewers in San Diego on Wednesday night as the Friars attempt to force a Game 5 back in Milwaukee on Friday night. With Morejon unavailable and closer Mason Miller on the paternity list, the Padres' bullpen was very short on Tuesday night, but Game 1 starter Michael King came to the rescue and threw the final two innings for SD to pick up a save in the 4-3 victory. Morejon has already had two two-inning appearances in this postseason, once in the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs and again on Saturday against the Brewers in Game of the NLDS, when he allowed the game-winning home run to catcher William Contreras. The hard-throwing Cuban left-hander was one of the most effective late-inning setup men during the regular season, though, going 9-3 with a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, three saves, and a career-high 107 strikeouts in just 86 innings out of the bullpen. With Miller unlikely to be back with the team on Wednesday, the Padres could really use Morejon's left arm on Wednesday evening.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - AJ Cassavell
Oct 6, 2026, 10:58 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman was one of the stars of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday. Freeman had just one hit in four plate appearances, but it was a solo home run off Braves ace Chris Sale. Freeman put together another strong regular season in 2026, hitting .288/.362/.430 with 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 74 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. The 37-year-old's production tailed off late in the year, as he hit just .184 in September and slugged just one home run across 249 plate appearances after the All-Star break. However, Freeman has looked like his vintage self so far this postseason. Across the first three games of the NLDS, Freeman has logged four hits, two home runs, two RBI, and three runs scored.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:40 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers utility man Enrique Hernandez struck one of the big blows of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, clubbing a two-run home run off of Braves ace Chris Sale to open the scoring in the fourth inning. It was Hernandez's only hit of the night, but it helped the Dodgers chase Sale out of the game after just five innings of work. Hernandez missed a large chunk of the regular season with an oblique injury and was not particularly effective when healthy, hitting .222 with four home runs across 96 plate appearances. However, the 35-year-old has a long history as an unlikely postseason hero. Across 332 career plate appearances in the playoffs, Hernandez has now hit .272 with 18 home runs and 44 RBI.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:30 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers right-hander Edwin Diaz notched his first save of the 2026 postseason on Tuesday, shutting the door in his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. Diaz allowed a leadoff double to Braves second baseman Ozzie Albies but rallied to retire the next three batters he faced. The 2026 regular season was largely lost to injury for Diaz, who spent time on the injured list due to both elbow and neck issues. However, the 32-year-old closed the season strong after returning from the neck injury in mid-September, allowing just one hit and one walk while recording nine strikeouts across his final five innings (five games) of the year. If Diaz can rediscover his peak form in October, he could be an impact arm for the Dodgers at the end of games.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:22 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto was the star of his team's 3-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday night. The 28-year-old allowed just four hits, one walk, and one earned run while recording 10 strikeouts across seven innings of work. Yamamoto was dominant during the regular season, recording a 14-9 record with a 2.53 ERA, 0.87 WHIP, and 182 strikeouts across 185 innings (28 starts). He's also been remarkably effective in the postseason to this point in his career, logging an 8-1 record with a 2.14 ERA, 0.83 WHIP, and 58 strikeouts across 63 innings. Following Yamamoto's gem, the Dodgers will have a chance to close out Atlanta in Game 4 and advance to the National League Championship Series on Wednesday.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:10 PM ET
San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller has been placed on the paternity list and will not be available for his team's matchup against the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune. Miller blew a save opportunity in San Diego's Game 2 loss to the Brewers, allowing a walk-off, two-run single to Milwaukee outfielder Jackson Chourio. Still, the hard-throwing right-hander was one of the best relievers in baseball in the regular season. Across 70 innings (66 games), Miller pitched to a 1.67 ERA and 0.90 WHIP with 129 strikeouts and 38 saves. Without Miller, San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon could be the next man up in the ninth inning for the Padres.--Will Brady
Source: The San Diego Union-Tribune - Kevin Acee
Miguel Rojas Suffers Back Injury in Game 3 of NLDS


Keith Hernandez




Oct 6, 2026, 8:52 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back) injured himself on a swing in the eighth inning and left Game 3 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves in the middle of his at-bat on Tuesday night, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. Rojas was reaching towards his lower back with his left arm after a swing. He was making the start at second base against Braves left-hander Chris Sale, and he went 0-for-3 at the plate with a strikeout before being replaced at the keystone by Tommy Edman. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder is a bench player for the Dodgers at this point in his career, but despite not playing all that much anymore, he saved the Dodgers' season in last year's World Series victory over the Toronto Blue Jays in Game 7 of the series. Rojas hit .267 (60-for-225) during the regular season with only four home runs, 23 RBI, 23 runs scored, and a stolen base. If Rojas' injury is serious enough for the Dodgers to remove him from the NLDS roster, he would be unable to return for the NL Championship Series if the team advances.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Gavin Sheets Scratched From Game 3 Lineup With Neck Stiffness


Keith Hernandez




Oct 6, 2026, 7:44 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that outfielder/first baseman Gavin Sheets (neck) was scratched from the Game 3 lineup on Tuesday in the National League Division Series against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers due to neck stiffness. Sheets will be available off the bench, though, so he should be considered day-to-day. Outfielder Samad Taylor is now serving as the designated hitter and will bat eighth in the order against Brewers right-hander Dustin May. Sheets hit 17 homers (two shy of his career high) in 125 regular-season games but missed all of September while on the injured list with a foot injury. The 30-year-old veteran left-handed slugger has played in only two games so far in the postseason for San Diego, but he did have a big two-run home run in Game 2 of the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs. Since the start of July, Sheets has hit just two home runs, so he has really struggled to tap into his power from the left side in the second half of the season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Ronald Acuna Jr. Battling Knee Soreness, Serving as DH in Game 3


Keith Hernandez




Oct 6, 2026, 4:53 PM ET
Atlanta Braves outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr.'s knee has been sore since he slid during Game 2 of the National League Division Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday, according to Mark Bowman of MLB.com. As a result, Acuna will serve as the designated hitter and bat second for Atlanta in Game 3 of the series in Atlanta against Dodgers right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Lane Thomas will now start in right field and bat seventh, with catcher Sean Murphy heading to the bench. Acuna has a history of knee injuries, so the Braves will get him off his feet as the series heads to Atlanta tied one game apiece. The former MVP has gone 2-for-9 with two runs scored and a stolen base at the plate in the first two games of the NLDS against the Dodgers. The Braves will need Acuna to be at his best for the remainder of the series in order to knock off the defending World Series champions. The five-time All-Star had two separate trips to the injured list during the regular season due to hamstring issues and ended up hitting .255/.345/.451 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 21 stolen bases, and 61 runs scored across 408 at-bats.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Mark Bowman

item.title: [Heavy.com] Dodgers Keep Pushing Off Shohei Ohtani Problem
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers won the NLDS on Wednesday night, needing four games to defeat the Atlanta Braves in the best-of-five series. That series victory, which the Dodgers hope is the start of their three-peat World Series journey in this postseason, masked something, though. Shohei Ohtani still isn’t right. The Dodgers have more or less acknowledged this already. After years of not moving him around the batting lineup, they’re moving him around the batting lineup. And sure, the Dodgers might be
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers won the NLDS on Wednesday night, needing four games to defeat the Atlanta Braves in the best-of-five series.
That series victory, which the Dodgers hope is the start of their three-peat World Series journey in this postseason, masked something, though. Shohei Ohtani still isn’t right.
The Dodgers have more or less acknowledged this already. After years of not moving him around the batting lineup, they’re moving him around the batting lineup.
And sure, the Dodgers might be so super-powered that it doesn’t even matter if they get Ohtani’s best. In some ways, it feels like they’re unbeatable.
But Ohtani is one of one for a reason. There’s no baseball player on the planet. Even when he’s not able to pitch, at least in the past, his contributions at the plate and on the bases have been otherworldly.
At the moment, though, Ohtani is very human.
What’s Wrong With Shohei Ohtani?
In an injury-plagued season, Ohtani simply appears to still be injured.
The Dodgers aren’t going to go too in-depth on any such speculation, but that doesn’t stop onlookers from feeling like that has to be the case.
The Ringer’s Anthony Dabbundo wrote on X: “It probably won’t matter because dodgers run prevention machine goes brrrr, but Shohei Ohtani hasn’t had a good at bat in any of the first four NLDS games and doesn’t seem healthy.”
That about sums it up. Something just doesn’t seem right with Ohtani.
Ohtani is 2-for-13 so far in the postseason, and that extends to a cold finish to the regular season for him.
For what it’s worth, Ohtani doesn’t yet have an extra-base hit in the small sample of the NLDS.
He went 0-for-3 with a walk and a run in the clinching Game 4.
Even dating back to the regular season, Ohtani is 10 for his last 60 (.167 average) with no home runs in that span.
Dodgers Dilemma
With almost any other hitter on the planet, you’d take an honest look at how he was feeling and consider a change.
It almost feels like Ohtani is above that. Sure, the Dodgers don’t want to hurt him worse, but if he believes he can be in the lineup, L.A. doesn’t want to tell him no.
It puts the Dodgers in tough spots, though. They have to make judgments on how his health might impact his play, except they aren’t inside his body to really know how he’s doing.
And truly, the Dodgers could win it all without Ohtani. So if he’s going to play, he needs to be more helpful than hurtful, because they have other options.
Los Angeles might not be able to solve this. There isn’t a ton of time.
But one way or the other, Ohtani is going to impact what happens in these playoffs. He always does. This year, it just might look a little different.

item.content:encoded:
월드시리즈 3연패에 도전하는 로스앤젤레스(LA) 다저스가 양대 리그를 통틀어 가장 먼저 챔피언십시리즈 진출을 확정했다.
다저스는 8일(한국시각) 미국 조지아주 애틀랜타 트루이스트파크에서 열린 애틀랜타 브레이브스와 2026 미국 메이저리그(MLB) 내셔널리그 디비전시리즈(NLDS·5전3승제) 4차전에서 4-1로 이겼다. 시리즈를 3승1패로 마무리한 다저스는 밀워키 브루어스-샌디에이고 파드리스 디비전시리즈 승자와 월드시리즈 진출을 다툰다.
두 팀은 경기 초반 실책과 폭투로 한 점씩 주고받았다. 애틀랜타가 1회말 다저스 선발 타일러 글래스노우의 폭투로 먼저 홈을 밟았고, 다저스는 곧바로 2회초 상대 실책을 틈타 균형을 맞췄다.
투수전 양상으로 흘러가던 승부는 7회초 갈렸다. 다저스 앤디 파헤스는 안타와 볼넷으로 잡은 2사 만루 기회에서 바뀐 투수 로베르트 수아레스와 풀카운트 승부 끝에 2타점 적시타를 때렸다. 9회초에는 맥스 먼시가 애틀랜타 마무리 라이셀 이글레시아스를 상대로 쐐기 솔로 홈런을 날렸다. 4-1로 앞선 다저스는 9회말 마무리 에드윈 디아스를 올려 경기를 매조지었다.
코리안 빅리거들의 명암도 엇갈렸다. 다저스 김혜성은 9회말 2루수 대수비로 그라운드를 밟았다. 올해 포스트시즌 첫 출전이다. 반면 애틀랜타 김하성은 이날 끝내 출전하지 못한 채 시즌을 마무리했다. 김하성은 포스트시즌 4경기에 나섰으나 5타수 무안타 2볼넷 3삼진 1득점으로 부진했다.
한편, 아메리칸리그 디비전시리즈(ALDS)에서 2패로 벼랑 끝에 몰렸던 클리블랜드 가디언스는 이날 미국 일리노이주 시카고 레이트필드에서 열린 시카고 화이트삭스와 3차전에서 9-3으로 승리하며 기사회생했다.

item.title: [New York Post] Doctober classic propels Dodgers to NLCS in quest for World Series three-peat
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate. So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches? So what if he was still in the fifth inning? Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances. The Dodgers advanced to the NL Champ
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Dave Roberts didn’t hesitate.
So what if Tyler Glasnow had thrown only 78 pitches?
So what if he was still in the fifth inning?
Glasnow had walked his second batter of the inning, and Roberts wasn’t about to take any chances.
Calling on Alex Vesia to record the final out of the inning, Roberts initiated a chaotic sequence of events that resulted in the Dodgers claiming a 4-1 victory over the Braves in Game 4 of their National League Division Series.
The Dodgers advanced to the NL Championship Series.
Because of Tarik Skubal.
Because of Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
Because of Freddie Freeman.
And because of David Ray Roberts, the manager affectionately known as Doc who has a game or two like this every October.
The victory over the Braves on Wednesday was a Doctober classic.
On a day in which one of his four aces lasted only 4 ⅔ innings, Roberts figured out how to cover 13 outs of the game with a notoriously unpredictable bullpen.
Roberts’ fingerprints were also all over Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning that broke open the game.
When Teoscar Hernandez singled that inning with one out, Braves manager Walt Weiss replaced starting pitcher Tyler Mahle with right-hander Didier Fuentes.
Fuentes forced Max Muncy to ground out, but Hernandez advanced to second base on the play.
Due up was Game 3 hero Kike Hernandez.
Rather than have the right-handed utilityman face Fuentes, Roberts deployed rookie Josue De Paula as a pinch hitter. The left-handed-hitting De Paula drew a walk, at which point he was replaced on the basepaths by Tommy Edman.
Kyle Tucker followed up with another walk to load the bases, at which point Weiss turned to fireballer Robert Suarez to pitch to Pages.
Pages batted .078 in the postseason last year, which resulted in his benching in the World Series. He was 0-for-7 in the first two games of this series, but Roberts stuck with him.
Roberts’ faith was rewarded by the most important hit of Pages’ three-year career, a single to right field that drove in two runs to push the Dodgers in front, 3-1. The runs were the Dodgers’ first of the series that weren’t scored via a home run.
The manager demonstrated an equal level of creativity in directing his bullpen.
Vesia returned for the sixth inning, only to give up a leadoff double to Ozzie Albies. Roberts kept the left-hander in for another batter, the left-handed-hitting Drake Baldwin, who lined out.
Roberts’ next call to the bullpen was for Edgardo Henriquez, who spent the last two weeks of the regular season on the injured list. Henriquez gave up a run in the Dodgers’ Game 2 loss, but not only did Roberts trust him to prevent Albies from scoring, he also had him pitch the seventh inning.
From there, it was simple.
Tanner Scott pitched the eighth inning. With Muncy homering in the ninth inning to increase the lead to 4-1, Edwin Diaz came in to record the last three outs.
The Dodgers moved to within four wins of playing in their third consecutive World Series, and they did it with Shohei Ohtani still missing in action.
Ohtani was 2-for-13 in this series.
“It’s good to know that we can still win games without him doing a whole bunch,” Roberts said. “But he’s going to come to life. It will happen.”
Roberts has squinted extra hard in recent days to find evidence of that.
Here’s the reality: In his last 22 combined games between the regular season and playoffs, Ohtani has no home runs and only one RBI.
That isn’t a slump.
The No. 1 player in the game doesn’t go this long without hitting in the prime of his career without something being seriously wrong with him.
Ohtani spent 15 days last month on the injured list because of a discomfort in his right arm. A couple of days before he was placed on the IL, he said his left knee was also bothering him.
The uncertainty over Ohtani’s capabilities forced Roberts to move him around the lineup.
With Mookie Betts grinding out quality at-bats as the leadoff hitter and Freeman producing enough to solidify his place as the team’s No. 2 hitter, Ohtani was removed from the top of the order.
Against the left-handed Chris Sale in Game 3, Ohtani batted fifth. Against the right-handed Mahle on Wednesday, he batted cleanup.
Ohtani managed to create something out of nothing in the second inning. He drew a walk, then stole second base, prompting Braves catcher Sean Murphy to airmail a throw into center field. Ohtani scampered to third base. When Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubón dropped a popup by Muncy in shallow left field, Ohtani scored to tie the game at 1.
Ohtani didn’t collect any hits Wednesday, but he didn’t have to.
Roberts had the game under control.

item.title: [Field Level Media] Andy Pages' clutch hit sends Dodgers past Braves, into NLCS
item.description: ATLANTA — Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning broke open a pitchers’ duel and helped the Los Angeles Dodgers close out their National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves with a 4-1 win in Game 4 on Wednesday. The Dodgers, who won the series 3-1 and are looking to be the first National League team to win three straight World Series, await the winner of the other NLDS between the Brewers and Padres. Milwaukee leads that best-of-five set 2-1 entering a Wednesday matchup i
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Andy Pages’ two-run single in the seventh inning broke open a pitchers’ duel and helped the Los Angeles Dodgers close out their National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves with a 4-1 win in Game 4 on Wednesday.
The Dodgers, who won the series 3-1 and are looking to be the first National League team to win three straight World Series, await the winner of the other NLDS between the Brewers and Padres. Milwaukee leads that best-of-five set 2-1 entering a Wednesday matchup in San Diego.
Pages’ hit was Los Angeles’ first with runners in scoring position in the series after the team started 0-for-14. It came off of Robert Suarez after Teoscar Hernandez hit a one-out single against Braves starter Tyler Mahle and then reliever Didier Fuentes issued back-to-back two-out walks.
Pages had two of the Dodgers’ five hits and two of their three RBIs in the win.
His clutch hit came the inning after Atlanta got nothing out of Ozzie Albies’ leadoff double, with Edgardo Henriquez (1-0) escaping the jam to earn his first career postseason victory.
Los Angeles’ Max Muncy tacked on an insurance run with a solo homer in the ninth, his third long ball of the postseason.
Mahle (0-1) was a tough-luck loser, charged with two runs (one earned) on three hits over 6 1/3 innings. He struck out four and walked one.
Michael Harris II had two of Atlanta’s three hits, including a double. However, the Braves’ situational hitting issues continued as they finished the series 1-for-23 with runners in scoring position.
Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow battled through 4 1/3 innings, allowing just one run on one hit, walking five and striking out five. Alex Vesia, Henriquez, Tanner Scott and Edwin Diaz followed and combined to allow no runs on two hits over the final 4 1/3 innings, setting down the final seven Atlanta batters in a row.
Diaz earned his second save of the series.
Los Angeles’ pitching staff gave up eight runs on 18 hits over the four-game series.
The Braves opened the scoring in the bottom of the first on a wild pitch that scored Harris. He led off with a single, stole second and moved to third on a fielder’s choice.
The Dodgers equalized in the second behind a pair of Braves errors. Shohei Ohtani drew a leadoff walk, stole second and moved to third on an errant throw from catcher Sean Murphy. Muncy then hit a sky-high popup to shallow left that shortstop Mauricio Dubon dropped, allowing Ohtani to score.
–Curt Weiler, Field Level Media

item.title: [Orange County Register] Andy Pages comes through in the clutch to send Dodgers to NLCS
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett

item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Overmatched last postseason and benched during the World Series, Andy Pages used the embarrassment to fuel an All-Star season in 2026.
But he was hit by a pitch on Aug. 21 that broke a bone in his hand, didn’t return until the final six games of the regular season and started the postseason, trying to do too much (by his manager’s estimation) to make up for last fall’s lack of contributions.
The accounts have been reconciled. It was Pages’ clutch two-out, two-run single in the seventh inning that broke a tie and lifted the Dodgers to a 4-1 victory on Wednesday night in Game 4 of their National League Division Series with the Atlanta Braves.
The victory sends the Dodgers to the National League Championship Series against either the Milwaukee Brewers or San Diego Padres. The Dodgers have reached baseball’s Final Four for the fifth time in the past seven years, the eighth time in the past 11. Their quest for a ‘three-peat’ will continue Sunday either in Milwaukee or at home against the Padres.
This series was decided in the seventh inning.
With the score tied 1-1, Teoscar Hernandez – fresh off a collision with the left field wall that left him on the warning track dirt, rubbing the left side of his head – singled with one out off Braves starter Tyler Mahle. It was just the third hit off Mahle and it came on just his 85th pitch. But Braves manager Walt Weiss went to his bullpen, bringing in Game 2 hero Didier Fuentes to face Max Muncy.
Fuentes got Muncy to ground out, Hernandez moving to second, but he walked pinch-hitter Josue De Paula and Kyle Tucker to load the bases with two outs.
Weiss had a quick hook, pulling Fuentes and handing the ball to veteran Robert Suarez to face Pages. Pages got ahead in the count, 3-and-1, then swung and missed at a 99.1 mph fastball from Suarez. He got another fastball on the full count and didn’t miss, stroking it through the middle for the Dodgers’ first – and only hit – with a runner in scoring position in their 16 at-bats in those situations during the four games of this series.
Runs had been hard to come by in Atlanta. After Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Chris Sale squared off in Game 3, Mahle and Tyler Glasnow allowed just a dirty run each through the first six innings.
In the bottom of the first, Michael Harris II led off with a single off of Glasnow. He stole second, went to third on a ground out and score when Glasnow spiked a knuckle curve in the dirt well in front of home plate. It bounced off Will Smith’s chest protector back towards the mound and Glasnow couldn’t retrieve it in time to get Harris.
In the top of the second, Shohei Ohtani took a five-pitch walk, stole second and went to third when Braves catcher Sean Murphy threw the ball into center field. Ohtani scored when Braves shortstop Mauricio Dubon dropped Max Muncy’s pop-up in shallow left field.
Mahle struck out only four in his 6⅓ innings (three of them consecutively in the fourth inning) and got just seven swings-and-misses on 95 pitches. But he got a lot of soft contact – and when he didn’t, it usually found a Braves fielder’s glove. The Dodgers hit seven balls in the first six innings with exit velocities of 95 mph or higher (the StatCast standard for “hard-hit”). Only one of them was a base hit – Pages’ third-inning single (106.7 mph).
Against Glasnow, the Braves just didn’t make much contact at all.
He gave up that leadoff single to Harris in the first inning but no other hits. He did walk five, though, including two in the fifth inning that prompted Manager Dave Roberts to pull him from the game after 78 pitches.
Dodgers pitchers somehow walked 18 batters in the series but let none of them score. Alex Vesia retired Matt Olson to end that fifth inning. Edgardo Henriquez held the Braves scoreless over the next two. Tanner Scott retired the slumping heart of the Braves’ order and Muncy gave Edwin Diaz cushion in the ninth inning with a solo home run (his 19th career postseason homer, a franchise record).
More to come on this story.

Glasnow got the start on Wednesday for the Los Angeles Dodgers in their potential closeout game against the Atlanta Braves. With two outs in the fifth inning at Truist Park in Atlanta, Ga., Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made the decision to pull Glasnow. The righty Glasnow had just walked his secon
item.content:encoded:
Tyler Glasnow had some choice words after being pulled from Game 4 of the NLDS on Wednesday.
Glasnow got the start on Wednesday for the Los Angeles Dodgers in their potential closeout game against the Atlanta Braves. He ended up going 4.2 innings, allowing just one hit and one earned run but also walking five total batters.
With two outs in the fifth inning at Truist Park in Atlanta, Ga., Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made the decision to pull Glasnow. The righty Glasnow had just walked his second batter of the inning to put the Dodgers in a precarious position with the score tied 1-1.
As Roberts came out to get him, Glasnow was shown cursing on the FOX Sports broadcast. He appeared to say, “That’s f–king crazy.” Here is the video (but obviously watch out for the bad language).
As of now the Dodgers have issued 18 walks in this series and not a single one has scored. Glasnow issued 5 in his 4.2 innings & was NOT happy about the early hook. https://t.co/bI8Bnlzm5O
— Dallas Braden (@DALLASBRADEN209) October 7, 2026
Glasnow was only at 78 pitches at the time that he was pulled. But as evidenced by the five walks, he did not quite have his best stuff during Wednesday’s game.
Dodgers reliever Alex Vesia came into the contest for Glasnow and ultimately secured the final out, getting Braves slugger Matt Olson to ground out. While Roberts has been criticized many times in the past for seemingly overmanaging his pitching staff, he certainly appeared to have made the right call there.
